The smartest workspace isn’t a distant future – it’s the strategy you adopt this quarter.

Ready to plot your course for 2026? The insights are here – apply them, iterate, and press forward. Feel free to reach out to us if you have any questions.

Live Questions From the Event (With Answers)

Q: What does the cross communication of each hub’s dev team look like? How frequently do they communicate with one another to ensure each hub is seamlessly working together on OfficeRND?

A: When we designed the Hubs architecture, we followed distributed system principles to ensure that each Hub has access to the most up-to-date data. Where real-time updates are critical, we use immediate data propagation. In other areas, like the Data Hub, synchronization happens on a regular schedule – currently every two hours. To support seamless collaboration, the dev teams have structured touchpoints, including shared planning sessions, regular syncs for cross-Hub initiatives, and aligned delivery timelines.

Q: Where will the data reside? The US does not benefit from GDPR like Europe. Data should not leave the US, however, are there other third parties involved?

A: This is all covered in our Terms and Conditions. US customers are currently hosted in AWS Ireland

Q: Yield management (dynamic pricing), requires data and elasticity models. Where is the pricing data coming from?

A: We’re currently in the discovery phase of this functionality. At this stage, we’re exploring various data sources, including historical booking data, space utilization patterns, and pricing benchmarks across similar locations. Our goal is to build a foundation that supports dynamic pricing by combining internal data with potential external market signals—while ensuring accuracy, fairness, and flexibility for operators.

Q: I missed the information on the email automation – is this for flex in general or attached to an additional service (‘hub’)?

A: This functionality is part of the Experience Hub. In Q2, the Experience Hub team is focused on enabling admins to send advanced emails to members. The capabilities include:

  • Customizable Emails: Admins can fully edit subject lines and email bodies using rich text, images, and attachments to create engaging, on-brand messages.
  • Targeted Delivery: You’ll be able to segment audiences to ensure that each message reaches the right members.
  • Performance Tracking: Open and engagement rates will be available to help optimize future communications and improve impact.

Q: Will OfficeRnD support official tax calculations per country?

A: OfficeRnD provides robust and flexible tax configuration tools designed to accommodate the diverse tax requirements of different countries and regions. The platform allows administrators to set up tax rates at multiple levels, ensuring compliance with local tax regulations:

  • Global Level: Apply a default tax rate across the entire organization.
  • Company or Member Level: Assign specific tax rates to individual companies or members.
    Product or Revenue Account Level: Set tax rates for specific products or revenue accounts.

Q: Any updates on the e-invoicing peppol requirements?

A: We’re currently in the research phase and plan to focus on this initiative in Q3. Rather than building a full solution in-house, we’re exploring partnerships with specialized e-invoicing platforms that can generate PEPPOL-compliant invoices and submit them to the relevant government authorities where required. This approach allows us to meet local compliance needs more efficiently while maintaining a seamless experience within OfficeRnD.

Q: Is there likely to be a spike in demand as businesses shift to one or two people using multiple AI agents

A: Yes, we expect a significant shift in how businesses operate as AI agents become more capable. Instead of large teams, we anticipate leaner teams supported by multiple specialized AI agents—handling tasks like customer support, scheduling, reporting, or even sales. This transformation could lead to increased demand for flexible workspaces, shorter-term bookings, and more tailored services, as businesses prioritize agility and cost efficiency. We’re closely monitoring this trend to ensure OfficeRnD can support these emerging workflows.

Q: Can you utilize the AI to re-engage old leads and keep them in rotation? More cold outreach?

A: Yes, absolutely. AI can be leveraged to identify and re-engage old leads by analyzing past interactions, segmenting audiences, and generating personalized messaging. It can also support more effective cold outreach by suggesting optimal timing, channels, and content—keeping leads warm and in rotation with minimal manual effort.

Name: We Sponsored This Coworking Ecommerce Deep Dive: Here are the Surprising Insights
Author: asen-stoyanchev
Short cards description: Picture a future where booking a meeting room or securing a day pass is as frictionless as reserving a hotel room or flight online.
Post body:
Picture a future where booking a meeting room or securing a day pass is as frictionless as reserving a hotel room or flight online.

That future is unfolding right now for coworking and flex spaces around the world. In fact, that future isn’t just arriving, it’s already here

We at OfficeRnD had the pleasure of underwriting and contributing to Hector Kolonas’ This Week In Coworking Undercurrent on ecommerce in coworking, and we’re excited to share the key takeaways.

In case you’re already wondering, an undercurrent is a deep dive report exploring an emerging industry trend.

So, below is a recap of the recent undercurrent “Our E-commerce Era: Has coworking’s big e-commerce era finally arrived?” featuring insights from industry leaders like Miro Miroslavov (OfficeRnD), Kane Wilmott (iQ Offices), Anne Olsen (The Shop Workspace), Chiko Abengowe (Perfect Office Solutions), Lyndon Cookson (AccelerateX), Ben Rigby (x+why), and Josh Dane (Runway East), as well as experts from Flexspace AI.

Read on for the most important findings and firsthand advice on why ecommerce is reshaping coworking and how to capitalize on it.

Why Ecommerce in Coworking – Why Now?

Ecommerce has long been a cornerstone of industries such as hospitality, airlines, and even restaurants. Consumers book everything online, from flights to fitness classes, so why should coworking be any different?

According to Miro Miroslavov, CEO & Co-founder at OfficeRnD,

We want to see coworking spaces make more money … ecommerce and selling directly is a huge piece of this.

Other industries have already demonstrated consumers’ preference for direct bookings. Hotels see more direct revenue than online travel agency bookings, and restaurants find that many visitors who discover them on aggregator sites ultimately book directly.

Coworking is no exception: prospective members and meeting-room renters now expect a “Book Now” button on your website rather than a phone call or a wait for a quote.

What Operators Are Selling Online? (And Seeing Real Returns)

Operators who have embraced ecommerce aren’t limiting it to just a single product. Many are listing a range of offerings. As Anne Olsen (The Shop Workspace) explains:

We saw such an incredible surge of activity around day passes and conference rooms that we figured, why not just make everything available?

Commonly sold items:

  • Day Passes & Meeting Rooms: The most popular products, cited by Kane Wilmott (iQ Offices) and others, because they’re simple to list and require minimal customization.
  • Virtual Mail & Virtual Offices: Chiko Abengowe (Perfect Office Solutions) stresses that capturing a midnight sign-up from someone who wants a business address is a big revenue opportunity.
  • Coworking Subscriptions: Some operators sell 10-day or unlimited monthly bundles, giving members flexible ways to buy time.
  • Private Offices: While more complex to sell without a human touch, a few operators do let prospective tenants buy small or short-term offices directly online.

Many experts reported meaningful revenue gains. Anne Olsen cited an additional…

$50,000 in the last year

…across a couple of locations after streamlining their online purchase flow.

Meanwhile, Eyal Lasker (Flexspace AI) reported that an average location “5x their revenue from online transactions within the first 12 months” after adopting a dedicated e-commerce platform.

Want to know how to leverage the power of ecommerce, turn website visitors into paying customers, and boost sales? Check out the Growth Hub. 

Hallmarks of a Great Ecommerce Experience

“Less clicks. That’s it,” emphasized Kane Wilmott (iQ Offices). The biggest success factor for operators is to minimize friction:

  • Simplicity: Fewer clicks or form fields for a fast checkout.
  • Live Availability: Real-time room schedules and membership capacities build trust.
  • Consistent Branding: Even if the transaction occurs on another sub-platform, the look and feel should match your space’s vibe.
  • Automations & Follow-Ups: Once booked, confirmation and arrival details should reach users instantly.

You don’t want random errors or boxes you can’t fill

…adds Ben Rigby (x+why). A confusing checkout can quickly frustrate potential members.

Key Challenges to Overcome

While the benefits are obvious, implementing ecommerce isn’t always seamless. Anne Olsen recalled how an early, clunky system drove people away: “It made people not really want to engage.” Ensuring the tech matches your service standards is vital.

Other challenges:

  • Team Alignment: Staff members who rely on commissions need clarity on who gets credit when customers buy online.
  • Product Clarity: Without a phone call to explain every detail, the online product page must handle common questions—yet avoid overwhelming prospective buyers.
  • Tracking & Analytics: Lyndon Cookson (AccelerateX) stressed the importance of setting up robust analytics to pinpoint drop-off points and refine marketing campaigns.

Pro Tips from Industry Experts

  • “Just do it.” (Chiko Abengowe, Perfect Office Solutions)
     Don’t let fear of retooling your sales process stand in the way. You’re missing out on late-night or quick-turn purchases.
  • Act as a Customer (Anne Olsen, The Shop Workspace)
     Test your own workflow to uncover friction, outdated copy, and missing features.
  • Optimize the Marketing Funnel (Lyndon Cookson, AccelerateX)
     Without solid data on conversions, you’re wasting ad spend. Make sure you feed booking data back to Google or your ad platforms.
  • Keep Personal Touch Where It Counts (Ben Rigby, x+why)
     Automated booking is great for smaller items, but bigger offices or custom enterprise deals may still need human interaction.

Final Word from OfficeRnD

“E-commerce is the future of technology for coworking spaces, for many reasons,” shared Miro Miroslavov, CEO & Co-founder at OfficeRnD, which underwrote this Undercurrent.

Our mission is to help operators of flexible coworking spaces generate more revenue, grow faster, and be more profitable. And a huge piece of that is e-commerce.

He added that better data and analytics help spaces measure conversion rates, fine-tune marketing budgets, and scale confidently.

What’s Next?

Coworking’s ecommerce era is not a far-off possibility – it’s already redefining how operators attract and convert members. If your workspace isn’t offering online booking for desks, day passes, or meeting rooms, you’re likely losing revenue.

We can do transactions while we sleep. That’s amazing.

…sums up Kane Wilmott.

The Big Benefits

1. Higher Occupancy and Revenue

Author: asen-stoyanchev
Short cards description: At OfficeRnD, we’ve worked closely with countless coworking and flex space operators who pride themselves on providing vibrant, welcoming environments.
Post body:
At OfficeRnD, we’ve worked closely with countless coworking and flex space operators who pride themselves on providing vibrant, welcoming environments.

But there’s a problem we see time and again: website visitors have to fill out lengthy contact forms or even make calls just to learn how to book a hot desk, meeting room, or sign up for a membership.

This often feels like a barrier to prospective members who simply want to purchase – or at least see real-time availability on the spot.

By implementing a seamless, embeddable ecommerce storefront, operators can skip the endless back-and-forth emails and sign-up hurdles.

Instead, they can sell desks, rooms, and memberships straight from their website – reducing friction and improving the overall booking experience.

In this blog post, we’ll explore why embedding your booking process directly into your website can boost engagement, improve brand consistency, and drive more conversions. We’ll highlight the pitfalls of overly complex contact forms and outline how a streamlined platform can make all the difference.

We recently sponsored a massive and super insightful deep dive into the emerging ecommerce trend in the coworking industry. Check it out here. 

Why a Frictionless User Journey Matters

Picture this: A curious visitor on your website has just discovered the perfect office suite for their growing startup. They’re sold on the location, love the amenities, and the pricing fits their budget. At this point, you’re practically guaranteed a conversion, right?

Not quite – because if your booking process isn’t easy, intuitive, and streamlined, you risk losing them just as they’re about to sign up. In today’s digital-first world, convenience is king. Users expect an online experience that:

  • Doesn’t slow them down with unnecessary steps.
  • Reflects a cohesive brand identity from start to finish.
  • Respects their time by simplifying bookings and payments.

When visitors encounter overly complex sign-up forms or convoluted booking processes, it quickly becomes cumbersome and discourages them from following through on their purchase.

The Cost of Distraction

As soon as a potential customer clicks a link that opens a new tab or takes them off your site, there’s an opportunity for them to pause – or even abandon the entire process.

They might see a notification, open another browser, or simply have second thoughts. Keeping them within your digital ecosystem means fewer distractions and a quicker path to purchase.

Building Trust Through Your Brand

Trust is everything in online transactions. If someone is about to commit to a monthly membership or meeting room rental, they want to be sure their payment details (and personal information) are safe.

A consistent, branded experience provides reassurance that your business is professional and reliable. When your booking process matches the look and feel of the rest of your website, you send a subtle message: “You’re still in good hands; no detours or weird handoffs here.”

The Problem with Complex Booking Methods

So why do many operators still rely on external booking solutions, off-site payment gateways, lengthy online forms, or phone bookings? In many cases, it’s simply the way they started out.

They built a basic website and added additional steps as they expanded. While that might have been enough in the early days, times have certainly changed.

Higher Abandonment Rates

Numerous studies – like those cited by the Baymard Institute—have shown that anything from unexpected fees to tedious checkout processes can push potential customers away.

In fact, Baymard’s research found the average cart abandonment rate is about 69.99%. If you compound that friction with having to leave your site, it’s even more likely they’ll bounce before finalizing a booking.

Loss of Brand Continuity

When your user lands on a page with an unfamiliar color scheme or different branding elements, it creates confusion. They may wonder if they’re still dealing with your company or if they’ve stumbled onto a completely unrelated service.

Fragmented Analytics

If you’re sending traffic to another domain to complete the transaction, gathering cohesive analytics data can become complicated.

Tracking the customer journey from a marketing perspective is important: you want to see who’s clicking what, how far they’re progressing in the booking funnel, and what might be causing them to drop off.

Brand Consistency: The Magic Ingredient

Let’s say you run a creative, boutique coworking space. Your branding might be full of vibrant colors and fun illustrations that reflect the energy of the community you host.

But if your booking process suddenly shifts to a stark, white-and-blue checkout page from a third party – or requires visitors to fill out a lengthy form or even call a number just to learn how to book – it’s like stepping into a different world.

How Consistency Reduces Cart Abandonment

A unified brand presentation keeps the customer experience tight and predictable. The moment your visitors feel something is off or out of sync, they might question:

  1. Whether they can trust this new page.
  2. Why they’re being sent away in the first place.
  3. If the checkout process will be complicated or time-consuming.

Eliminate these doubts, and you’ll eliminate a lot of reasons for people to leave.

Showcasing Professionalism

Professionalism comes through in small details. By embedding a branded ecommerce storefront on your site, you’re telling visitors you value their time enough to keep everything in one place.

Plus, it simply looks more polished and signals that you’ve invested in a best-in-class customer experience.

Actionable Tips for a Better Booking Experience

Now that we’ve established why an on-brand booking process is critical, let’s explore ways you can optimize your website’s booking flow.

  1. Make Navigation Seamless
     Keep the path from discovery to checkout as short as possible. If someone sees a “Book Now” button, ensure it leads directly to an embedded form or a short, straightforward flow.
  2. Minimize Form Fields
     Nobody wants to fill out pages of personal details. Ask only for information you absolutely need. You can gather further details once the person is on-site.
  3. Offer Multiple Payment Options
     Some prefer credit cards, others might like digital wallets, and certain businesses pay via direct invoicing. Providing diverse payment choices appeals to a broader audience.
  4. Use Clear Calls to Action (CTAs)
     Avoid vague phrases like “Submit.” Instead, opt for action-oriented buttons such as “Confirm Your Booking” or “Reserve Your Space.”
  5. Mobile-Optimize Everything
     More people are booking from smartphones and tablets. If your booking form or checkout page isn’t mobile-friendly, you risk losing that audience.
  6. Display Trust Signals
     Incorporate badges or short statements about security and encryption to reassure users. Even better: if you have testimonials or reviews, highlight them somewhere in the checkout process.
  7. Provide Transparent Pricing
     Hidden fees or unclear pricing structures can tank your conversions. Show your costs upfront and be clear about what’s included.

Industry Observations

Many of them report a more streamlined user journey and fewer barriers for prospective members, especially when compared to systems that require multiple sign-up steps or direct users to third-party platforms.

Name: Harnessing the Power of the OfficeRnD Visitor Hub [ Webinar Recap]
Author: asen-stoyanchev
Short cards description: If you’re looking to streamline visitor management, enhance security, boost revenue, and deliver a standout guest experience in your workspace, our latest webinar – “Harness the Power of OfficeRnD Visitor Hub: Explore Its Most Advanced Features Yet” – offered a front-row seat to the newest developments in our platform.
Post body:
If you’re looking to streamline visitor management, enhance security, boost revenue, and deliver a standout guest experience in your workspace, our latest webinar – “Harness the Power of OfficeRnD Visitor Hub: Explore Its Most Advanced Features Yet” – offered a front-row seat to the newest developments in our platform.

Presented by Miro Miroslavov (Co-founder and CEO at OfficeRnD) and Momchil Blaskov (Product Marketing Manager at OfficeRnD), the session walked through all the ways the Visitor Hub can transform front-desk operations, from advanced delivery tracking to tour coordination and beyond.

Below is a comprehensive recap of the most important insights including answers to some of the questions asked during the webinar.

If you want the full experience, be sure to watch the on-demand webinar afterward – this is only a glimpse of all the knowledge our speakers shared!

Ready to watch the on-demand webinar and unlock all the insights shared? Do it here. 

Understanding the Visitor Hub as Part of the OfficeRnD Ecosystem

During his introduction, Miro set the stage by explaining OfficeRnD’s overall vision of making flexible work “the way of working.” Over the years, OfficeRnD has expanded into a robust platform with multiple products (or “hubs”), each focusing on a distinct operational challenge.

The Visitor Hub is one of these specialized solutions, enabling coworking and flexible workspace operators – as well as corporate offices – to manage visitors, contractors, deliveries, and event guests more effectively.

In this modular approach, users can opt to adopt only the specific hubs that solve their most pressing problems. For instance, you can combine Visitor Hub with the main coworking management solution (OfficeRnD Flex) or workplace management product (OfficeRnD Workplace).

Or, if you already rely on other tools for visitor management, it’s easy to integrate them with the rest of the OfficeRnD platform via powerful APIs and integrations. Check out our full list of integrations for flex spaces here.

According to Miro, this design ensures the Visitor Hub remains robust enough to stand on its own while integrating seamlessly with the wider OfficeRnD ecosystem.

Check out the different use cases of the Visitor Hub for coworking and flex spaces and for corporate workplaces. 

Simplifying Delivery Management

One of the major highlights of the webinar was the new delivery log functionality. According to Momchil, as e-commerce grows, front desks receive an ever-increasing volume of packages – from mail and boxes to parcels of various shapes and sizes.

The Visitor Hub helps operators track deliveries in real-time, record their status, and automatically notify recipients via email, push notifications, or SMS. It also supports multiple delivery types and offers a place to attach photos, so recipients know exactly what’s waiting for them.

Especially in large or busy spaces with potentially dozens of daily deliveries, this level of oversight prevents confusion, misplaced packages, and cluttered reception counters.

Operators can even log packages if they arrive after-hours or when the tablet isn’t in use, ensuring that the system accurately records the full chain of custody from arrival to pickup.

Streamlining Tours, Contractors, and Vendor Check-Ins

For most flexible spaces, successful tours are a key factor in turning curious prospects into paying customers. The Visitor Hub introduces a specialized tour check-in flow, ensuring each visitor or group gets the correct custom fields – such as phone number, email, or reason for visit – while automatically notifying the relevant team member (a community manager, salesperson, or facility manager) that a tour is about to start.

Similarly, for contractors or other external vendors, the platform supports custom fields and sign-off documents, so you can capture any legally required information or waivers. Hosts are notified the moment a new contractor arrives, and the visitor data is recorded for compliance and security.

This approach is particularly valuable for maintenance crews, event setup teams, or construction vendors who need swift but safe access to your premises without bogging down the front desk.

Boosting Revenue with Shortcut Buttons and Upsells

Recognizing that front desks are not just a place to greet guests but also a gateway to sales, OfficeRnD introduced custom shortcut buttons right on the Visitor Hub tablet homepage.

In one tap, walk-in visitors can be taken directly to a purchase screen for Day Passes, Services, or other offerings.

As Miro noted, the user experience is intentionally streamlined. When a visitor taps “Buy a Day Pass,” for instance, a QR code appears, which visitors can quickly scan to complete the purchase securely on their own device.

This not only reduces friction (no awkward, multi-step process in a public area) but also frees staff to focus on providing excellent hospitality rather than serving as manual payment processors. In the near future, we plan deeper integrations with point-of-sale hardware, but for the majority of operators, this approach is both simple and secure.

Generating High-Quality Leads

We at OfficeRnD see the Visitor Hub as more than a sign-in system; it’s also a tool to capture critical lead data. Because you can tailor forms and fields for different visitor flows – tours, events, and more – you can request permission to include the visitor in follow-up marketing campaigns.

Better yet, with upcoming integrations through Zapier, the Visitor Hub can automatically send these leads to your CRM of choice (HubSpot, Salesforce, etc.).

Operators can follow up on visits promptly, track lead quality, and nurture new relationships that turn into lasting memberships.

Enhancing Security and Compliance

It’s crucial to know who’s in your building and why they’re there. The Visitor Hub ensures every external guest checks in electronically, capturing visitor photos, personal information, signature requirements, and signed documents.

Teams also have the option to print badges through integrated, high-quality label printers, helping staff and community members immediately recognize who’s an authorized guest and whether they’ve completed the check-in properly.

From a compliance angle, having a record of every visitor’s name, contact details, and time of check-in/check-out can save you headaches during audits or emergency situations.

OfficeRnD’s ongoing improvements also let you customize host notifications and success screens, giving guests a clear, post-check-in message about where to go or whom to contact if they have questions.

So, What’s Next for the Visitor Hub

Momchil took a moment to preview the near-term roadmap, which includes:

  • Enhanced integrations via Zapier to seamlessly add or retrieve visitor records from Eventbrite, Google Sheets, and CRMs
  • Customizable success screens, allowing operators to guide visitors toward specific desks, meeting rooms, or floors.
  • Host notification upgrades that include more visitor data, such as visitor type or the number of delivered items.
  • Meeting room assignments built into visitor flows, so guests instantly know which space they’re heading to.

These enhancements will amplify the Visitor Hub’s flexibility, taking yet another step toward a truly unified visitor management ecosystem for all types of work environments.

Don’t Miss the On-Demand Webinar

This blog post only scratches the surface of what was discussed during our “Harness the Power of OfficeRnD Visitor Hub” webinar. Our speakers went into even greater detail, answered audience questions, and demonstrated real-life scenarios where the Visitor Hub shines.

If you’d like the full picture and want to see how your workspace can benefit from these advanced features – be sure to watch the on-demand webinar today. It’s an excellent opportunity to learn first-hand from the people who helped build and shape this powerful tool.

Ready to see the Visitor Hub in action? Book a live demo to see how these solutions fit your unique workflow. We can’t wait to help you transform your visitor experience and drive new revenue streams in the process.

Attendee Questions (Plus Answers)

1. What are the key differentiators that set your Visitor Hub apart from competitors such as The Receptionist?

  • It’s seamlessly integrated with your Flex/Workspace system.
  • Ensures extreme customizability to fit your specific use cases, including custom flows, fields, notifications, and shortcut buttons.
  • You can standardize on fewer vendors and optimize the time spent evaluating/signing contracts with your vendor.

2. Currently, the visitor data does not synchronize with “Opportunities.” It would be extremely valuable to be able to do this.

We will explore it as an improvement for the future.

3. Deliveries – If a member doesn’t click “Picked Up,” is there an automatic notification reminder for them in OfficeRnD, or can one be set up?

This makes sense. We will explore it as an improvement for the future.

4. Will we be able to link this to HubSpot CRM, or do we have to use Zapier?

You will have to do it through Zapier. We will explore in the future to make it part of the native HubSpot integration.

5. Tours – Can we set a maximum number of people per tour slot? If so, how can we manage this within the platform?

This is part of the Tour module improvements. We will share the feedback with our team focused on this area.

6. With tour management streamlined into Visitor Hub, are there plans to allow further customization with tour time windows, etc.?

This is part of the Tour module improvements. We will share the feedback with our team focused on this area.

7. Will we be able to connect tour booking to our Google Calendar soon? The lack of that is the only thing keeping us from using OfficeRnD Tours.

This is part of the Tour module improvements. We will share the feedback with our team focused on this area.

8. Is there any Mail Management Feature in progress to log incoming mail and get instructions from virtual office clients to get their mail forwarded, scanned, or just held for pick-up? That would be very helpful for operators with a high volume of virtual office clients.

Not at the moment. We will explore doing this through integration partners.

9. How would all these different options – regular guest check-ins, contractors, events, tours, etc. – be displayed on the tablet home page? Would there be a way to keep it clear and user-friendly to avoid confusion?

They are behind the check-in button. When you click it, you will see all the options.

Name: 8 Effective Strategies to Increase Occupancy Rates in a Struggling Coworking Space
Author: asen-stoyanchev
Short cards description: The coworking space industry has seen substantial growth over the past decade, but like any fast-evolving sector, it’s not without its challenges – especially as we move into 2025.
Post body:
The coworking space industry has seen substantial growth over the past decade, but like any fast-evolving sector, it’s not without its challenges – especially as we move into 2025.

Today’s workspace operators grapple with rising operational costs, increased competition, and shifting workforce expectations.

In such a dynamic environment, maintaining a high occupancy rate is crucial for sustainability and profitability.

Quick Summary of Top Strategies

  • Conduct thorough market research to identify local demand.
  • Offer flexible pricing and membership models.
  • Foster a vibrant community and networking culture.
  • Strengthen your marketing efforts and online presence.
  • Continuously upgrade facilities and amenities.
  • Prioritize customer service and retention.
  • Explore strategic partnerships and collaborations.
  • Regularly measure performance and adapt strategies accordingly.
Check out the latest OfficeRnD FlexIndex for Q1 2025 and see how you measure against industry benchmarks across 6 important KPIs. 

Understand Your Market and Target Audience

Conduct Market Research

Before you start making tweaks to your coworking space, make sure you know the market you’re serving. Conduct thorough surveys with local startups, freelancers, and small businesses to gauge their specific needs – such as preferred workspace arrangements, budget limitations, and desired amenities.

Explore local demographic data from municipal or regional economic development offices to see if remote workers or gig workers are more prevalent.

Analyze social media groups, LinkedIn forums, and local business directories to understand gaps in current coworking offerings. Consult industry-specific publications and real estate agencies to track emerging trends and fluctuations in workspace demand.

You might discover that your region is dominated by tech startups or, conversely, that you have a strong community of creatives who crave flexible solutions tailored to their unique needs.

For more insights, you can refer to resources like JLL’s Global Coworking Trends and the Global Coworking Unconference Conference (GCUC), which provide up-to-date industry data.

Want to go the extra mile?

Attend local Chamber of Commerce events or business meetups to network and gain firsthand knowledge of what local professionals are looking for in a coworking environment.

We recently introduced the OfficeRnD Growth Hub - an embeddable e-commerce storefront that helps you unleash your sales potential and grow your business.  

Define Your Ideal Customer Profile

Whether your space appeals to remote teams, digital nomads, early-stage startups, or creative agencies, be specific about who you want to serve.

Here’s a list of the most common industries that use coworking spaces. Tailor your workspace design, membership perks, and marketing language to resonate with that audience.

Analyze Competitors and Identify Market Gaps

Study your competitors’ offerings. Do they cater primarily to tech startups? Are they hosting frequent networking events that attract a particular demographic?

Pinpoint what they’re doing well and where they might be lacking. Position your space to fill those gaps.

This could mean offering specialized amenities for podcasters or focusing on a wellness-centric workspace.

Optimize Pricing and Membership Models

Flexible Pricing Strategies

Gone are the days when coworking spaces had a single, rigid membership. Depending on your target market, you could offer day passes, part-time memberships, and full-time memberships.

You might also introduce different membership tiers to cater to different budgets and usage patterns. Forbes also highlights how flexibility is becoming increasingly vital in the modern workspace.

Discounts for Long-Term Commitments

Encourage loyalty by offering discounted rates for members who commit to three, six, or twelve months at a time. This strategy not only helps secure long-term revenue but also fosters a sense of community.

Bundling Services

Combine your basic desk or office access with additional benefits like meeting room credits, printing packages, or even event tickets. By creating these “value bundles,” you can attract customers who appreciate getting more for their money.

Enhance Community and Networking Opportunities

Hosting Events and Workshops

One of the unique selling points of coworking spaces is the ability to bring people together.

Host events, workshops, or seminars on topics relevant to your members, such as digital marketing, productivity hacks, or emerging technologies. Look to organizations like Startup Grind for inspiration.

Member-Exclusive Networking Opportunities

While public events can draw new prospects, exclusive gatherings for members help deepen the sense of belonging within your space. This could be something as simple as a weekly breakfast or a monthly “Members’ Night Out.”

Building a Sense of Community

Consider implementing activities that help create shared experiences. This could include book clubs, group fitness sessions, or even volunteer programs where members collaborate on community projects.

Fostering real, meaningful connections will set your coworking space apart in 2025 and beyond.

Improve Marketing and Online Presence

Leverage Social Media and Content Marketing

A strong digital marketing strategy can significantly boost your occupancy rates. Share success stories of your members, highlight upcoming events, and create engaging social media content.

You can also maintain a blog to address popular industry trends or provide workspace tips. Here are 17 proven marketing strategies that help increase your reach.

Optimize for SEO and Local Search

When people search for “coworking space near me,” you want to rank at the top of the results. Optimize your website for local keywords, claim your Google My Business profile, and encourage members to leave reviews.

Here’s a complete SEO guide for coworking spaces.

Referral Programs and Partnerships

Offer incentives to current members or local business allies for bringing in new clients.

This could be a discount on membership or a monetary reward. Collaborations with local coffee shops, restaurants, or tech stores can also help cross-promote each other’s offerings.

Upgrade Facilities and Amenities

Modernize Design and Workspace Functionality

Outdated décor and cramped layouts won’t make a good impression on potential clients. Consider renovating to create open, well-lit spaces with private nooks for phone calls or focused work.

Here’s a complete guide to coworking space layout.

Amenities That Matter

High-speed internet is a must, but you can go further by providing ergonomic furniture, fitness areas, a stocked pantry, or wellness rooms where members can meditate or take breaks.

A good example to follow is WeWork’s approach to regularly updating its spaces for both productivity and comfort.

Cleanliness and Maintenance

No matter how impressive your amenities are, they won’t mean much if your space isn’t clean and well-maintained. Invest in regular deep cleaning, ensure bathrooms are always stocked, and fix equipment issues promptly.

Focus on Customer Service and Retention

Exceptional Onboarding

From the moment a new member walks in, they should feel welcomed and supported. Offer a guided tour, introduce them to community managers, and maybe provide an onboarding packet detailing all the perks they have.

Gather and Act on Feedback

Use quick surveys or suggestion boxes to gather feedback. If members notice that the phone booths are always booked, consider adding more.

If they want more networking events, start planning some. Demonstrating that you value and act on feedback fosters loyalty.

Loyalty Programs and Personalized Services

Offer freebies or discounts based on usage history. You could provide a free meeting room hour for every three months of continuous membership.

Personalized services, like custom mail handling or dedicated account managers for larger teams, can also go a long way.

Leverage Strategic Partnerships and Collaborations

Partner with Local Businesses and Influencers

Reach out to local businesses or community influencers who align with your brand.

This partnership could involve co-hosted events, discounted memberships for their staff, or cross-promotion on social media.

Collaborate with Professional Groups

Organizations like local Chambers of Commerce or industry-specific networks can bring a steady flow of potential members. Offer them special meeting rates or membership deals in exchange for introductions.

Establish Cross-Promotional Opportunities

If there’s a nearby coffee shop frequented by professionals, propose offering their customers a day pass at your coworking space. In return, you can feature their coffee or snacks at your events.

Measure Performance and Adapt

Track Key Performance Metrics

Monitor your occupancy rate, churn rate, and overall member satisfaction (often measured through NPS scores). By focusing on data, you can identify what’s working and what needs to be improved.

Leverage Data Insights

If you notice a spike in churn at the same time each year, dig deeper. Are you failing to re-engage members, or are you missing seasonal trends? Adjust your offerings accordingly.

OfficeRnD Flex is a deeply customizable coworking management platform that has powerful analytics allowing you to monitor key metrics and take more informed business decisions.

Continuously Test and Optimize

Running a coworking space successfully is an ongoing process. Try different marketing campaigns, tweak your membership offers, and test new events. Measure the impact and keep refining.

In Conclusion

In today’s crowded and competitive coworking landscape, struggling with occupancy rates is not uncommon.

Yet, with the right mix of market research, flexible membership models, community-building initiatives, and effective marketing, you can boost your occupancy rates and set yourself apart.

Don’t be afraid to innovate; the coworking industry is constantly changing, and staying ahead requires creativity and adaptability. Whether you’re revamping your current model or starting from scratch, consider implementing these strategies to foster sustainable growth.

Ultimately, a successful coworking space hinges on meeting and exceeding the evolving needs of modern professionals. Stay proactive, remain open to feedback, and keep a pulse on industry trends. Your efforts will pay off in the form of increased membership and a thriving, dynamic community.

Post body:
Picture this: A key client or potential customer walks into your office for a meeting, only to be met with confusion and chaos at the front desk.

The receptionist scrambles to find their host, Slack messages fly, and the visitor awkwardly waits, wondering if they’re even in the right place. Not exactly the seamless, professional experience you want to provide, is it?

In today’s hybrid work environment, where employees split their time between home and office, managing visitors can be a logistical headache.

Who’s in the office today? Where should visitors check in and where should they wait afterwards?

How do you keep everything secure while still offering a warm welcome? That’s where Visitor Hub comes into play – the modern, intuitive visitor management platform designed to take the guesswork (and the stress) out of handling office guests.

In this blog, we’ll explore seven essential use cases for Visitor Hub that will transform the way your company manages visitor flow.

Let’s dive in.

#1 Streamlined Operations for Time and Cost Efficiency

The Problem

Reception staff juggle multiple responsibilities at the front desk which can slow down productivity for both employees and guests.

Manually signing in visitors, tracking arrivals, completing the necessary paperwork, and notifying hosts can be time-consuming and prone to errors.

The Solution

Visitor Hub eliminates manual processes by automating visitor check-ins, sending instant host notifications, and providing a clear overview of who’s expected and when. By digitizing and automating visitor management, companies can reduce the time spent on manual sign-ins, free up reception staff for higher-value tasks, and minimize administrative costs and inefficiencies.

A smooth, efficient check-in process also means visitors spend less time waiting around unacknowledged and more time engaging with your space and employees in meaningful ways.

#2: Simplify Deliveries with Hassle-Free Package Management

The Problem

With different employees working on different schedules in a hybrid office, managing package deliveries can become chaotic.

Packages pile up at the front desk, important deliveries get misplaced, and employees often have no idea when their packages arrive, leading to frustration and inefficiency.

The Solution

Visitor Hub streamlines package management by logging deliveries, notifying recipients instantly, and ensuring that packages are securely stored until pickup.

Employees receive automated alerts when their package arrives, eliminating confusion and unnecessary back-and-forth.

By keeping track of all deliveries in one centralized system, companies can prevent lost packages, reduce front desk workload, and create a seamless experience for employees handling important shipments.

#3 Seamless Visitor Hosting

The Problem

Coordinating visitor arrivals in a hybrid workplace can be tricky. Without a structured system in place, guests might arrive not registered, without a host in sight, and experience delays at check-in.

This creates an unprofessional and disorganized first impression leaving your guests feeling frazzled and unwelcome.

Check out the use cases of the Visitor Hub for coworking and flex spaces.

The Solution

Visitor Hub ensures a seamless and welcoming visitor experience by sending automated reminders, allowing guests to pre-register and check in, and distributing customizable forms ahead of time.

Reception teams can further enhance the experience by instantly notifying the host when their visitor arrives, reducing wait times.

#4 Enhanced Security and Compliance

The Problem

Security is a top priority in any workplace, but hybrid offices face unique challenges. Without a structured visitor management system, unauthorized guests can slip through unnoticed, confidential areas may be compromised, and regulatory compliance can become difficult to track.

Additionally, manual data entry and collection can significantly inhibit accuracy and security.

The Solution

Visitor Hub enhances workplace security by implementing visitor verification, badge printing, and access control integrations to ensure only authorized individuals are coming in or utilizing secure areas.

Companies can maintain compliance with industry regulations by automating visitor logs, tracking entry and exit times, and securely storing visitor data.

They can further increase their security and compliance measures with custom flows, buttons, and fields that collect information as to why they are visiting, who they are meeting with, and how long they will be on the premises.

Visitors can also sign legal agreements or other official documents digitally to decrease the risk of error and information getting compromised.

#5 Contractor and Vendor Management

The Problem

Managing contractors and vendors in a hybrid workplace can be quite complex – they aren’t exactly a new guest, but they’re not a regular employee either.

Without a dedicated system, it can be difficult to track who is on-site, delays and bottlenecks are almost inevitable, and the potential for compliance issues can rise. This can lead to security gaps and inefficiencies in coordinating external workers.

The Solution

Visitor Hub simplifies contractor and vendor management by offering pre-registration and simplifying the check-in process with self-scanning QR codes.

Hosts and managers can also import their vendor or contractor information to prevent these guests from having to fill out the same information every time they arrive.

#7 Events Management

The Problem

Hosting events in a hybrid workplace comes with unique challenges. Coordinating guest lists, managing check-ins, and ensuring a smooth experience for attendees can be overwhelming, especially when dealing with both in-person and virtual participants.

Without a structured system, event registration can be chaotic, leading to long wait times, lost attendees, and missed networking opportunities.

The Solution

Visitor Hub simplifies event management by offering pre-registration, digital check-ins, and real-time attendee tracking to keep everything organized.

Automated guest notifications and badge printing ensure a seamless arrival experience, while integrated analytics provide insights into attendance and engagement.

#7 Employee Check-ins for Presence & Emergency Tracking

The Problem

In a hybrid workplace, it is not always clear who will be in the office on any given day. This lack of visibility can create logistical challenges for team collaboration and pose serious risks in emergency situations.

Without an efficient system to track employee presence, companies may struggle with workplace coordination, emergency roll calls, and compliance with safety regulations.

The Solution

Visitor Hub enables effortless employee check-ins, giving organizations real-time visibility into who is on-site at any moment.

Employees can check in via QR codes, mobile apps, or self-service kiosks, ensuring an accurate log of attendance and resources. This will also give hosts and managers insight into which desks, offices, or meeting rooms are in use should an emergency occur.

Final Words

Though managing a workplace can come with its own set of challenges, Visitor Hub enables companies to turn those challenges into seamless, efficient experiences for employees, visitors, vendors, and event attendees.

From streamlining front desk operations and enhancing security to simplifying package deliveries and improving emergency tracking, Visitor Hub is the all-in-one solution for modern workplace management.

Companies everywhere are striving to optimize their workplaces. Clear communication, efficient resource management, and an engaging environment are cornerstones of a thriving office culture.

Traditional static signage can’t keep up with the pace of daily updates like shifting meeting schedules, changing desk reservations, or unexpected announcements.

According to a MarketsandMarkets report, the global digital signage industry is projected to experience substantial growth in the coming years, thanks to advancements in display technology, cloud integration, and interactive software.

Organizations hoping to stand out and adapt to changing business models find these solutions indispensable. Digital signage in the workplace is not just a futuristic concept – it’s already revolutionizing how teams communicate, stay organized, and enhance security.

This blog post explains what digital signage is, highlights its numerous benefits, and shows an effective suite of digital signage apps that can transform day-to-day office operations.

Let’s dive right in.

What Is Digital Signage in the Workplace?

Digital signage involves leveraging electronic displays – often touch-enabled – to show content such as event schedules, office maps, news feeds, or room availability.

These displays can be placed in lobbies, hallways, reception desks, meeting room entrances, or any other high-visibility spot.

Many organizations adopt this approach to keep employees and visitors informed while reducing reliance on traditional, easily outdated methods of communication.

Digital signage in the workplace takes this concept further by integrating with workplace management systems.

Employees receive real-time data for desk bookings, meeting room schedules, and any vital office-wide announcements.

Visitors find navigating the premises easier, checking in quickly, and enjoying an overall professional experience. The result is a cohesive environment where efficiency, brand identity, and user satisfaction converge.

5 Key Benefits of Digital Signage

#1 Improved Communication

Every office depends on timely and accurate communication. Screens in hallways, reception areas, and outside meeting rooms can display crucial reminders, upcoming events, and even emergency alerts.

Team leaders can quickly disseminate urgent bulletins or highlight successes across all displays simultaneously. The ability to push updates in real time allows everyone to stay on the same page without overloading email inboxes.

Information presented on digital displays stands out more than a printed flyer. Employees are far more likely to notice a dynamic graphic, a brief video, or even a scrolling news ticker than a static poster pinned to a noticeboard.

Office managers can use these displays to reinforce company-wide priorities, post quarterly goals, or celebrate milestones. Such continuous and dynamic visibility keeps morale high and eliminates any ambiguity about what’s happening within the company.

#2 Enhanced Brand Experience

A consistent brand experience matters as much to employees as it does to visitors. Large, vibrant displays in reception areas set a welcoming tone that aligns with the company’s visual identity. Incorporating logos, color palettes, and messaging helps reinforce organizational culture.

Guests walk away with a memorable first impression, which can be vital for client-facing businesses that often hold on-site meetings or events.

Professional display setups also highlight a company’s commitment to innovation. People equate a modern office environment with forward-thinking leadership, which can boost employee pride and attract high-caliber talent.

Staff members feel immersed in the company’s culture, and visitors immediately understand what the organization stands for.

#3 Cost and Time Efficiency

Printing posters, signs, and nameplates can be costly and time-consuming. Digital signage eliminates the need for constant reprinting.

A single screen can easily switch between multiple displays or messages. Office managers, for instance, can rotate through different daily announcements, highlight upcoming office gatherings, and convey departmental achievements—all from a centralized management dashboard.

Human resource teams benefit, too. Company-wide reminders about benefit enrollment deadlines, training sessions, or policy updates can appear on displays at strategic times, ensuring employees who missed an email don’t fall through the cracks.

This is a sustainable approach that minimizes paper waste and reduces the time spent on manual updates or sign replacements.

#4 Increased Workplace Efficiency

Streamlined processes and resource utilization are critical in a fast-paced workplace.Digital signage integrated with room booking software,  from corporate offices to university booking software, ensures that employees can see at a glance which spaces are available

Occupied desks or meeting rooms are easily identified, eliminating confusion and guesswork. Last-minute schedule changes become less stressful, as an updated booking instantly appears on the display.

Efficiency also extends to real-time wayfinding. Employees and visitors can quickly locate the nearest available desk, identify specific people’s seating arrangements, or navigate to a particular conference room.

This is especially helpful for larger or growing offices that have added new departments or facilities. A quick glance at the screen tells employees everything they need to know, minimizing lost time.

#5 Enhanced Security

Let’s state the obvious – a secure environment is essential for any organization. Digital signage can integrate with security systems to verify credentials or send critical alerts during emergencies.

Real-time monitoring of facility access helps ensure only authorized individuals enter restricted areas. Organizations set up custom check-in steps for guests, making it straightforward to maintain compliance with safety regulations.

While high-tech solutions are convenient, they also serve to protect employees and company property. Quickly identifying suspicious activity or unauthorized visitors is simplified when front-desk staff can see all pertinent check-in information at once.

Everyone feels safer and more confident when security is visibly maintained through robust, integrated tools.

3 Typical Use Cases in the Workplace

#1 Meeting Rooms Management

Meeting rooms can become a real headache without a proper booking system. Digital signage outside each room provides immediate clarity on whether the space is free or in use.

A quick tap on the touchscreen allows employees to reserve the room or check in for a pre-booked session. These capabilities foster better collaboration and reduce unnecessary scheduling conflicts.

Setting up automatic room release is another advantage. If a meeting organizer doesn’t check in within a specified timeframe, the space reverts to available status. This eliminates wasted resources and frees up rooms for other teams to use.

#2 Reception and Visitor Management

A well-placed display at the reception desk leaves a lasting impression on guests. They can check-in, print a temporary badge, and even view a digital floor plan of the office for easy navigation.

Any friction that might occur while signing paper logbooks or waiting for a receptionist to become available is reduced. Hosts are instantly notified of a visitor’s arrival, ensuring swift and personalized greetings.

This level of interaction shows visitors that the organization is committed to efficiency and hospitality. Potential partners, clients, or job candidates interpret these digital tools as markers of a dynamic and forward-thinking environment.

Reception staff benefit, too, because they can attend to more pressing tasks while confident that the digital signage system is guiding guests effectively.

#3 Employee Communications & Emergency Alerts

Centralized displays serve as bulletin boards for employees, posting a wide range of updates – anything from holiday schedules to urgent security notifications.

In the case of an emergency, immediate alerts on every screen ensure crucial information reaches everyone in the building without delay. Coordinated evacuation notices or safety instructions show up instantly.

Non-emergency notifications also flow seamlessly. Shared calendars, highlight reels of internal achievements, and motivational quotes can be displayed to uplift or inform employees as they walk through the office.

The possibilities are endless when you can adapt your content based on what’s happening in real time. Now, let’s explore some handy digital signage solutions that people love.

Name: Mastering Wi-Fi and Networking: Key Takeaways from Our Expert-led Webinar
Author: asen-stoyanchev
Short cards description: In today’s flexible workspace environment, seamless Wi-Fi and robust networking aren’t just “nice-to-haves.” They’re foundational elements that define productivity and member experience – whether you’re a boutique coworking site or a network of large-scale flex offices.
Post body:
In today’s flexible workspace environment, seamless Wi-Fi and robust networking aren’t just “nice-to-haves.” They’re foundational elements that define productivity and member experience – whether you’re a boutique coworking site or a network of large-scale flex offices.

Recently, we hosted a webinar entitled “Wi-Fi & Networking: Best Practices and Smart Strategies for Your Space” alongside experts from OnX Solutions and isofy. The session delved into the intricacies of sourcing internet connections, selecting and optimizing hardware, implementing smart Wi-Fi strategies, and even turning your network into a revenue stream.

If you missed the live discussion, here’s a succinct recap of what was covered.

1. All Internet Connections Aren’t Created Equal

Paul Hoffman from OnX Solutions kicked off with an overview of internet service options and emphasized the importance of truly redundant connectivity.

He stressed how one hour of internet downtime can have a massive ripple effect on coworking operations, and recommended that operators meticulously compare carriers to find the right balance of speed, reliability, and cost.

OnX’s carrier-agnostic approach gives clients a wide variety of ISP options to ensure genuine redundancy – meaning you won’t accidentally purchase a “backup” connection that relies on the same physical infrastructure as your primary circuit.

This is just a quick recap of the webinar "Wi-Fi & Networking: Best Practices and Smart Strategies for Your Space". To learn all the insights watch it on-demand here. it's free.

2. Network Hardware & Infrastructure

Moving beyond the ISP side, the conversation turned to core and access layer hardware – firewalls, switches, and access points (APs). The experts agreed that investing in the right gear can save headaches in the long run.

While “enterprise-grade” solutions might carry a higher upfront cost, they also deliver better performance, consistent firmware updates, and more reliable support. And since you may need to replace access points every four to five years (and core networking gear every eight years), choosing the correct solution at the start is paramount.

Top Tip: If you have a large conference room that seats 30+, consider dedicating an AP specifically to that space. Overloading a single AP by trying to serve multiple areas can diminish performance significantly.

3. Wi-Fi Optimization: Beyond the Basics

Yes, connectivity is essential – but “more signal” doesn’t always equate to “better.” The experts walked through common pitfalls, such as overlapping channels and too strong radio frequencies.

The result?

Members might see full bars, but still experience sluggish performance. A deliberate design that factors in coverage, capacity, channel planning, and power settings is crucial.

Additionally, if your users frequently complain about “bad Wi-Fi,” it may not always be the wireless radios themselves – sometimes it’s DNS issues, VLAN misconfigurations, or even aging end-user devices. Thorough diagnostics help pinpoint the actual cause and prevent ongoing guesswork.

4. Integration: OfficeRnD & isofy

The webinar shined a spotlight on the OfficeRnD + isofy integration. By syncing member data across both platforms, new members are automatically provisioned onto the network with the correct credentials and VLAN.

Beyond reducing administrative overhead, it ensures that members enjoy seamless connectivity – no extra logins or repeated data entry required.

On the back end, network administrators gain real-time insights into which users are online, how many guests have checked in, and how bandwidth is being consumed.

Armed with this data, operators can more accurately track day-pass usage, occupancy rates, or even explore additional revenue streams.

5. Monetizing Your Network

Traditionally, internet access might be viewed as a cost center for operators. But the panelists described creative ways to turn connectivity into a revenue driver:

  • Tiered Bandwidth: Offer higher-speed connections to certain teams or individuals at a premium.
  • Private Networks: Upsell dedicated IP configurations for enterprise teams with high security or compliance requirements.
  • Hardware Colocation: In locations with enterprise clients, renting out a locked rack space for specialized equipment can add to your recurring revenue.
  • Public IP Addresses: If you can lease multiple static IPs from your ISP, reselling them to tenants in need of external-facing services can further enhance your bottom line.

The experts cautioned, however, that your core network must be rock-solid before layering on premium services. Reliability, speed, and security must come first.

6. Key Takeaways & What’s Next

  • Security Matters: A publicly shared Wi-Fi password may be acceptable in some spaces, provided you layer additional authentication beneath it. Segment guests vs. members, and ensure that your firewall and VLAN structures are robust.
  • Future Tech: Wi-Fi 7 is on the horizon, promising major leaps in speed. But remember—you’ll need matching infrastructure (e.g., multigig switches, high-speed backhaul) to unlock its full potential.
  • Unified Approach: Networking, member management, and even access control are all part of a single digital ecosystem. If one link fails, the entire user experience suffers. Platforms like isofy and OfficeRnD help unify these moving parts.

Name: The Quick Guide to Office Space Planning [2026]
Author: asen-stoyanchev
Short cards description: The hybrid office looks different from the traditional in-person office space. Space utilization is more flexible because the same people aren’t in the office each day. There’s more focus on the purpose of each square foot, and less concern about fitting a full workforce in at once.
Post body:
The hybrid office looks different from the traditional in-person office space. Space utilization is more flexible because the same people aren’t in the office each day. There’s more focus on the purpose of each square foot, and less concern about fitting a full workforce in at once.

Leaders at hybrid companies should give their staff a workspace built for collaboration, while also looking for ways to reduce square footage and cut costs.

Proper office planning is what lets you create an office that makes sense for your company. You can plan the space you have around the needs of your hybrid workforce and your budget. In 2026, the average office runs at about 43% daily utilization (XY Sense), so most companies pay for far more space than they use on a typical day.

Quick summary

  • A well-planned office can raise employee productivity, improve collaboration, and lower long-term costs.
  • A hybrid office needs specific amenities and areas to work well, including configurable furniture, hot-desking, and tech-connected meeting rooms.
  • Size your office to peak-day attendance, not total headcount, and review usage over time.

What is office space planning, and why is it important?

Office space planning means planning your space’s layout, tools, and usage so that every square foot has a purpose, whether that’s productivity or collaboration.

The goal is to match your space to your business needs so your employees, remote or in-office, have what they need to get work done.

Here are some of the benefits of a well-planned office.

Higher productivity

Your layout shapes how employees interact with the workspace, work with each other, and do their tasks. For example:

  • Dedicated workspaces let employees concentrate without interruptions.
  • Proximity to essential facilities, such as bathrooms and breakrooms, cuts the time wasted walking the office.
  • Small and medium meeting rooms let hybrid teams meet easily, whoever happens to be in that day.

Improved collaboration

Spaces built for collaboration help your employees work better together and bring teams closer, both socially and physically.

According to the World Economic Forum, one of the main reasons employees stay in a job is that they enjoy working with their colleagues.

A space where people build relationships affects your company’s output and can raise employee retention.

Cost savings

Offices with unused corners, empty lounges, and surplus desks quietly burn money. Larger spaces cost more in rent, and they cost more to run: more air conditioning, more lighting, higher energy bills.

Companies that match their office size to real attendance cut real estate costs by 20% to 40%, with further savings on utilities, cleaning, and maintenance. Good space planning is what turns that into money you keep.

Supports employee well-being

A well-planned office works for the people in it, not just the business. Comfort at work, direct access to natural light, quiet spaces, and good air quality, shapes how people feel and how they work.

Start with peak-day attendance

Most hybrid offices run about 43% daily utilization (XY Sense, 2025). More than half the floor sits empty on an average day, and you pay rent on all of it. Global building utilization has climbed to 53% (CBRE, 2026), up from 38% in 2024, so offices are busier than they were two years ago, though still far from full.

Attendance also moves across the week. People cluster on Tuesday, Wednesday, and Thursday, and those peak days run roughly 35% above the weekly average. Size your office to the weekly average and you’ll be short on desks midweek. Size it to your full headcount and you’ll pay for desks that sit empty every Friday.

The number to plan around is peak-day attendance divided by your desk-sharing ratio. A team of 120 on a 3-day policy might bring 97 people on a busy Wednesday and need about 70 desks at a 1.4x sharing ratio.

You can run these numbers in a few minutes with our office space planning calculator. Enter your team size, average days in office, and sharing ratio, and it sizes the desks, workstations, and common areas you need, then shows the cost you’d save by matching space to real attendance.

What makes a good hybrid office space?

A good hybrid office needs several amenities and areas so your employees have what they need to work, alone and in teams. Here are the main ones:

  • Open and shared spaces: Hybrid teams do well in flexible environments. Open space with multiple desks, shared workstations, and informal meeting areas lets people choose where they work based on the task in front of them. That supports creativity and spontaneous collaboration.
  • Quiet zones: Many hybrid employees come in specifically to focus. Dedicated quiet zones, soundproofed and away from high-traffic areas, give them that. People also use these spaces for unplanned virtual meetings and private calls.
  • Meeting rooms: Tech-connected meeting rooms let employees collaborate regardless of location. Include video conferencing systems, large displays, and microphones. You can use OfficeRnD Workplace so employees book meeting rooms in a few clicks.
  • Configurable furniture: Hybrid environments change. Configurable furniture that’s easy to move or reconfigure helps. Include pieces that suit different work styles, such as sitting and standing desks.
  • Storage and organization: Hybrid employees split their time between home and office, and carrying belongings around all day gets old fast. Add storage, like lockers, to make the switch between in-office and remote days easier.

As desk demand drops, many teams are moving that floor space into meeting rooms, focus booths, and collaboration areas. The square footage people no longer need for solo work goes toward the reason they came in: working with each other.

Build these features in, and you get a space where employees can work well, however and wherever they choose.

How to plan an office space

Planning a hybrid office means analyzing how the space will be used and what your employees need to do their jobs.

You’ll balance flexibility, technology, and comfort so your team can get work done from anywhere. The process has six key steps.

1. Assess your space and needs

First, look at the size of your space, the floor plan, plumbing, and electrical outlets, and design around them. This step saves you from costly redesigns later.

Next, consider your company’s needs:

  • How many employees will use the office regularly?
  • Do they usually work independently or in teams?
  • What functions do they need to get work done?

Hybrid is now the default. JLL’s 2025 occupancy benchmark found 67% of office workers are hybrid, in the office one to four days a week, with another 15% in five days a week, and 18% fully remote. A single fixed desk per person no longer matches how people show up.

So count how many employees come in on a typical peak day, usually a Tuesday or Wednesday, rather than your total headcount. You can size desks, workstations, and common areas from that number with our office space planning calculator.

Based on those answers, you might add hot desks for people who work mostly remote and dedicated workstations for those who come in often. That keeps the office efficient and the experience good.

2. Choose a layout

The best layout for hybrid teams mixes open spaces for independent work with meeting rooms for working together.

Your team needs to collaborate, but cramming everyone into one room won’t work either.

So plan a mix of spaces that fit your team:

  • Quiet booths for sales calls
  • Private, soundproofed spaces
  • Meeting rooms for collaboration
  • Tables for team sessions
  • Shared desks for more remote workers
  • Dedicated spaces for frequent in-office employees and office managers

3. Plan for technology

Hybrid offices depend on technology to connect remote and in-office teams. Key considerations:

  • Accessibility: The whole office needs internet connectivity, especially work zones.
  • Smart meeting rooms: Equip collaboration spaces with tools that make it easy to work together when some people are in and some aren’t. Think video conferencing and interactive whiteboards.
  • Power outlets: Place desks near outlets so people can charge laptops or power desktops without hunting for a socket.
  • Flexibility: Tech and office designs change fast. Consider modular setups and adaptable layouts so furniture upgrades are simple.

4. Use the right management and space planning tools

Office resource booking software helps you manage how your space gets used, the same way a university booking system helps institutions manage lecture halls, labs, and study spaces. Employees book desks and meeting rooms ahead of time, and the office doesn’t get overcrowded.

Choose a tool that connects with your other software. OfficeRnD Workplace, for example, works with Slack, Google Calendar, Stripe, and more. See our full list of integrations here.

The platform also lets you coordinate employee schedules and track space usage, so you can adjust the office over time. In addition, here’s a current comparison guide on the best space management software.

5. Incorporate branding and aesthetics

Your office should reflect your company’s identity, even in a hybrid setup. A well-designed space looks professional and shapes how clients see your business. Include:

  • Brand elements: Use color schemes that match your culture. Put your logo in key spots, like the wall behind the front desk.
  • Plants and greenery: Greenery makes a space feel calmer and more alive.
  • Appropriate decor: Use decor that fits your company, whether that’s creative, professional, or calm.

6. Test and adjust

The work isn’t done once you’ve made the changes. A good layout needs ongoing fine-tuning:

  • Gather feedback: Survey employees regularly to learn what’s working and what isn’t.
  • Analyze room usage patterns: Use a tool like OfficeRnD Workplace’s Analytics to see room usage, desk occupancy, and underused space, then make decisions from real data.
