Name: Overcoming Communication Overload In A Hybrid Environment
Author: asen-stoyanchev
Short cards description: As more businesses embrace hybrid work , communication channels have surged. Hybrid teams have turned to an increasing number of apps to mimic the natural flow of information that once came from working side by side.
Post body:
As more businesses embrace hybrid work, communication channels have surged. Hybrid teams have turned to an increasing number of apps to mimic the natural flow of information that once came from working side by side.

Over the past year in particular, there has been an increase in the amount (78%) and range (73%) of communication channels employees are expected to use for work.

And, as if there wasn’t enough communication to deal with in a day between Slack and Teams channels, Zoom calls, emails, and project management tool notifications, now, hybrid team members need to be able to book conference rooms, reserve desks, and co-ordinate meetings across rotating in-office days.

Talk about communication overload!

To overcome these unique communication challenges at your hybrid workplace, you need to resolve any existing issues first. Then, you can build a culture around efficient communication — no matter where your team works from.

Quick Summary:

  • An increase in the volume of communication that hybrid workers have to manage on a daily basis is causing workplace frustration and information overload.
  • It’s also costing your business money in wasted time, interrupted focus, and miscommunication — leading to errors.
  • These issues can be overcome by:
    • Running a communication audit to find areas of improvement in your current communication methods
    • Optimizing your channels and matching the form of communication with the channels it’s being transmitted through
    • Creating a communication hierarchy
    • Building a culture around focus and deep work — saving additional communications for the appropriate times and meetings
    • Integrating a hybrid workplace management system to make in-person collaboration simple so you don’t need so much online communication

What is Communication Overload?

Communication overload is the feeling of overwhelm that comes from receiving too many messages or too much information through too many channels in a workday. This can look like excessive emails, back-to-back meetings, and constant notifications, making it hard to focus or prioritize.

It’s stressful and affects productivity.

According to the Harvard Business Review, in 2022 the average employee was receiving 120 messages a day. This number will continue to climb as the number of channels we need to monitor in a workday increases.

According to the 2024 State of Business Communication report from Grammarly, hybrid workers report spending over 40 hours each week on communication alone, leaving little time for actual focused work.

Communication overload is more than just a workplace frustration. It puts your company at risk of losing talent. If people feel like they can’t be productive and are constantly stressed trying to keep up with communications, they’re going to seek work elsewhere.

Why Is Communication Overload a Problem?

Grammarly’s report on business communication also found that nearly half of business owners say scattered communication across too many channels is driving up costs, and staff are saying that poor communication is a leading cause of their “quiet-quitting.”

In a hybrid work environment, the problem only becomes more complex. Teams have to juggle extra coordination: syncing schedules for in-office days, booking desks to work at on their in-office days, and finding meeting rooms.

Add on after-hours messaging and you can see how quickly work is spilling into personal lives, piling on the stress.

With nearly 40% of workers saying they’d quit if they were forced back to the office full-time, simplifying collaboration in a hybrid setup is no longer just a nice-to-have — it’s a must for retaining a productive and engaged team.

Information Overload in Internal Communication

It’s not just the sheer amount of communication that’s overwhelming staff — it’s the overload of information within this communication.

Using the wrong channels for the wrong types of information creates chaos. We’ve all been stuck in meetings that could’ve been emails or tangled in Slack threads that should’ve been a quick call or stand-up meeting.

Important documents shared through instant messages or emails? Good luck finding the right version later.

And internal updates? They often miss the mark — nearly 80% of leaders think their updates are relevant, but only 46% of employees agree. This is because communication differs across functional teams and within your vertical staff hierarchies.

This is a critical disconnect that’s costing teams time, clarity, and engagement.

When employees are bombarded with too much information, processing it all becomes impossible. Overwhelmed, they tune out. This can manifest as staff scrolling social media at work, taking more sick days than usual, or just stepping back and not interacting with their peers in the same way.

Fifty-nine percent of employees report feeling disengaged — a key sign of quiet quitting. This means a large chunk of your workforce may be mentally checking out without actually leaving.

And the impacts don’t stop there. Communication overload and disengagement ripple across productivity, morale, and even your bottom line. Missed deadlines, lost information, and frustration among teams are just the beginning of the challenges this creates.

How Does Communication Overload Impact Hybrid Teams

The benefit of a hybrid workforce is the ability to collaborate both in-person and online, ideally building a stronger culture and better project outcomes. But if it’s not easy to collaborate with peers in person, remote and hybrid workers won’t want to come back to the office.

One of the most common complaints about having to go back to the office in a hybrid scenario is that staff are still doing all their communication online.

Just wanting people in chairs won’t be enough to convince your hybrid teams that commuting is worth the effort if their in-person experience doesn’t lead to more productive outcomes.

This is because collaborating with others online feels like the norm — no one wants to be forced back to the office only to find out they still have to attend all their meetings on Teams and could have done this from home.

When communication in a hybrid environment falls short, divides between the hybrid and ‘in-office’ workers grow. And when constant communication leads to no real results, frustration can ensue.

As the mental fatigue in your employees increases, a learned survival mechanism kicks in: learned helplessness takes over so employees can conserve their mental energy.

Rather than empowering your teams, the stream of emails and direct messages encourages them to completely disengage altogether.

5 Ways to Overcome Communication Overload in Your Hybrid Work Environment

In the age of communication abundance, hybrid work has amplified the challenge of managing multiple digital communication channels. While these tools do offer flexibility, they can also create communication barriers that ultimately just frustrate employees further and detract from your carefully planned workflows.

The good news? With some thoughtful hybrid communication strategies you can turn these challenges into opportunities for effective communication at both the enterprise level and the individual level — meaning everyone gets the information they need in the format they need it via the channel that makes the most sense.

Here are five practical ways to streamline communication in your hybrid workplace:

#1 Review the Existing Quality of Communication With an Audit

It’s impossible to fix communication overload without first understanding where the bottlenecks and communication barriers lie. Are too many updates clogging inboxes? Are your staff drowning in Slack messages, emails, and “quick calls”?

Kick things off with a short (anonymous) survey to gather employee feedback — this helps pinpoint which tools are really working and which are causing more frustration.

Look at how collaboration tools are being used and whether asynchronous communication is being prioritized for non-urgent matters.

Once you have a clear picture, create a framework to define what’s necessary (and what’s not) while encouraging practices like do-not-disturb settings during focus time.

By auditing and refining your communication practices, you’ll clear the path for deeper work and a happier, more productive hybrid team.

Match the Information Level With the Type of Communication

Let’s face it: we’ve all groaned at a Slack message that could have been a quick call — or worse, sat through an hour-long meeting that could have been an email.

Misusing digital channels doesn’t just waste time, it creates more communication barriers by overwhelming staff with the wrong type of information in the wrong place.

The key is flexibility. Use collaboration tools thoughtfully — Slack for quick updates, emails for more detailed information, and meetings only for discussions that truly require real-time input.

Encourage asynchronous communication wherever possible, respecting focus hours and reducing interruptions.

When information is shared in the right way, and at the right time, it encourages clarity, reduces frustration, and supports even more effective communication.

Create a Communication Hierarchy

Without a system, communication can feel like chaos management. A communication hierarchy helps by setting up clear guidelines for what needs to be escalated, who handles what, and how to avoid unnecessary noise.

For urgent matters, create an express route that ensures quick resolutions. For routine updates, bundle them into regular team briefings in person or concise reports.

Training your staff in concise messaging — like using clear subject lines, bullet points, and to-the-point summaries — makes communication smoother.

This hierarchy prevents important messages from getting buried in clutter, cuts through communication barriers, and ensures everyone knows what truly deserves their attention — and when.

Create a Culture of Effective Communication

Hybrid work thrives when everyone understands how to communicate efficiently. That starts with creating a culture where effective communication becomes the norm and not the exception.

Set clear expectations for when and where to communicate — quick updates go in chats, while project details belong in emails.

Protect deep work time by blocking out interruption-free hours and using tools to prioritize focus. Stick to a few key digital communication channels to avoid overwhelming your team, and make sure everyone knows how to use the tools in the best way possible.

It’s ok to enforce boundaries too — turning off notifications after hours or setting clear work-life limits helps your team stay engaged without burning out.

Regular feedback loops can help you uncover any lingering communication barriers, giving you the chance to fine-tune your practices as your hybrid workplace continues to evolve.

Make Hybrid Collaboration Simple with a Hybrid Workplace System

Hybrid work doesn’t need to feel like a juggling act. The right tools, like OfficeRnD Workplace, can bring clarity to your workplace by making in-person collaboration seamless and reducing reliance on excessive online communication to secure deskspace or book meeting rooms.

Take Müller, for example. This international food leader streamlined its hybrid workforce by integrating OfficeRnD Workplace to support desk and room booking while syncing effortlessly with collaboration tools like Slack and Microsoft Teams.

OfficeRnD’s open API also means your developers can create custom solutions tailored to your team’s unique needs, simplifying your operations.

By adopting a robust hybrid workplace system, you remove unnecessary digital communication channels and make hybrid collaboration feel effortless.

This overload isn’t just draining. It’s also costing your business with wasted time, distractions, and critical information lost in long email chains.

Post body:
In 2023, the global coliving market was valued at a whopping $13,285.27 million, and it’s projected to expand at a compound annual growth rate of 29.9% until 2032. So if you own or operate a coworking space and are searching for new revenue streams, you may want to consider turning your business into a coworking and coliving space.

In a world where housing costs are skyrocketing and people are increasingly turning to remote work, coworking-coliving spaces provide an ideal solution. They allow freelancers and remote workers to travel and find community, without breaking the bank on high rental costs or committing to long-term leases.

Here we dive into why coworking-coliving spaces are on the rise, how they attract members, and what you can do to make yours a success.

Quick Summary

  • Coworking-coliving spaces are becoming more popular as younger generations are increasingly opting for remote jobs, looking for alternatives to expensive housing costs, and seeking flexibility in their living arrangements.
  • Freelancers, digital nomads, and entrepreneurs are turning to coworking and coliving because of the community-building opportunities, amenities, and low-commitment membership options.
  • Choosing a favorable location, prioritizing safety, and providing a variety of membership options can help attract new members to your space.

What Are Coworking-Coliving Spaces?

Coworking-coliving spaces (also called coplaces) are hybrid spaces where members can live, work, and find community and connection, all in one building. They offer flexible living arrangements that serve as alternatives to traditional, long-term leases.

The types of people that coworking and coliving spaces attract vary. You’ll primarily see freelancers, digital nomads, and younger adults without families — all people who seek flexibility and affordable costs of living. More established professionals also use coplaces when traveling for work. Some even offer childcare options.

A major draw for potential members is the opportunity to participate in fun classes and activities, so often the market for coliving includes people who want community.

Typically, members in these spaces share common areas like living rooms, kitchens, and bathrooms, but they have their own private bedrooms (although sometimes there are options to share bedrooms as well).

For the most part, they also share chores, including cooking, cleaning, and laundry. However, some buildings offer these services for an extra fee.

Coliving Space Models

Under the coliving umbrella, you’ll find a variety of different model types. You can offer your members plans that last days, weeks, or months, with options to extend when their stays are up.

You can provide private or shared rooms or add-ons like personal amenities and services. But the basic premise is that someone rents an apartment or room in a building that has a coworking space.

Why Are Coworking-Coliving Spaces Becoming More Popular?

Back in 2016, coworking juggernaut WeWork expanded its brand to include WeLive, a series of residential spaces that focus on creating community.

Also, in the years leading up to the pandemic, millennials were known as the first generation to seek out coliving spaces for their affordability in big cities and opportunities for connection.

But then, from 2019 to 2021, the number of people working from home more than tripled. Freelancers, digital nomads, and other workers found themselves without ties to physical offices, which left them free to reimagine their living and working situations even further.

So it’s a combination of factors — the rise of remote work, the need for affordable living, and the work preferences of the upcoming generations — that has paved the way for coplaces.

Let’s dive deeper into the reasons coworking-coliving spaces are becoming more popular in 2024 and 2025.

The Rise of Remote Work

As remote work is becoming increasingly common, the number of digital nomads and freelancers continues to grow worldwide.

In 2024 alone, there are about 76.4 million freelancers in the US. This results in a large population that craves community since they’re not surrounded by people in a traditional office setting. With coworking-coliving spaces, they can make friends where they live and work.

Coworking-Coliving Spaces Offer Affordable Living Arrangements

Coworking, coliving, and more generally flexible workspaces tend to be more affordable for members than traditional setups.

This means they’re a great option for freelancers and digital nomads, as they often allow them to travel and work without breaking the bank.

College graduates and young professionals who want to live in major cities but can’t afford the rent can also save by opting for this more communal, more cost-friendly way of life.

Younger Generations Are Seeking Flexibility

Thanks to remote work, younger generations are finding freedom from in-office jobs. But this desire for flexibility extends to their living arrangements as well.

This makes coworking and coliving spaces attractive alternatives. They require less commitment than buying a home or a year-long apartment lease.

What Do Members Look for in a Coworking-Coliving Space?

If you’re thinking about starting or expanding a coworking-coliving space, let’s take a look at what attracts members to these communal living spaces.

Opportunities for Belonging (and Fun)

One of the main reasons people are attracted to coworking, coliving, and flexible office spaces is the community that comes with them.

Host events that actively foster a sense of belonging and allow your residents to get to know each other. They can be professionally oriented, geared toward personal growth, or just plain fun.

Offer activities, events, classes, and workshops to bring residents together and attract new members. For example, The Collective Old Oak, a coworking coliving space in London, offers perks like yoga classes, pasta-making classes, and graffiti workshops.

Membership Plans That Don’t Break the Bank

To ensure your membership plans are affordable, conduct market research and set your prices in line with those of your competitors.

Make sure that your plans are also more affordable alternatives to housing options, like hostels and Airbnbs, in your area.

You can also make it easy for members to pay for multiple services at once. You can include rent, utilities, and a coworking space fee all in one (weekly or monthly) payment for your members, which simplifies billing for everyone.

To simplify billing even more, consider automating it! For that, you can use coworking management software such as OfficeRnD Flex. See how.

Amenities That Dazzle

Just because these spaces are on the affordable side doesn’t mean they need to be barebones. In fact, part of the draw is that members can live in a nicer place (often with plenty of amenities) for less.

Offering amenities like pools and rooftop gardens can help differentiate your space from other temporary living solutions for digital nomads and freelancers. It can elevate your building to feel more like a hotel but at a reduced cost.

Amenities like yoga spaces and game rooms are also attractive to members because they help encourage work-life balance, which can be difficult for freelancers, who don’t necessarily have set work hours.

Safe Spaces

It’s important that your coworking-coliving space offers community and privacy. After all, no one wants to be social all the time. Everyone needs the option to retreat to their own private space, especially when they live and work in the same location.

Ensuring your members’ privacy also means protecting their belongings in both living and working areas. With so many people around all the time, it’s important that each of your residents feels confident that their things are safe and secure.

Low-Commitment Options

Typically, your clientele for a coworking-coliving space prefers a flexible lifestyle. They’re likely digital nomads, professionals traveling for work, or freelancers who’ll seek out one of these options instead of a hotel. So if you try to lock them into year-long leases, you may deter them from joining.

Instead, offer flexible membership options so that your residents can stay or leave as they please (within reason).

You can try to entice them to extend their stay by offering deals on room fares. For instance, a coworking-coliving company in Indonesia called Outpost offers a 20% discount for residents who stay longer than 28 nights.

What Are the Challenges of Running a Coworking-Coliving Space (And How to Overcome Them?

You may encounter the following challenges when running a coliving space, but here’s how to overcome them.

Operating 24/7

While there are some 24/7 coworking spaces, the majority are only open during the day. So if you’re incorporating coliving into your coworking space, you’ll run into the additional challenge of extending your operating hours.

Because your residents will be living in your space around the clock, you essentially can’t close. This means you’ll need night and weekend staff to ensure your members are safe and comfortable 24/7.

Taking into account their wages and additional operating costs associated with keeping your place open every day, it can be more expensive to run a coworking-coliving space.

Managing Your Space

When your clients live and work in the same space, there’s a lot to consider when it comes to creating an optimal layout.

You’ll need a wide variety of rooms for the coworking area, including private meeting rooms, private offices, and an open working floor. For the living section, you’ll need bedrooms, bathrooms, kitchens, and living rooms.

It can be challenging to nail down the right amount of space that makes your guests comfortable without overspending.

And in addition to choosing the right size and placement for all those areas, it’s important to keep them safe and clean. This means hiring a team to maintain your space.

Marketing to a New Audience

If you’re adding a coliving area to your coworking space, you’ll have to learn how to market to a slightly different audience. While many of your client base may be the same (like freelancers), they’ll be searching for new features from a living area.

Plus, signing up for a living space is more of a commitment. Many of your potential new members won’t get to see your building in person ahead of time, so it’s crucial that you provide online visuals of your space. These can look at photos, videos, and 3D tours on your website and social media channels.

You should also advertise all of the community-building events that your place offers, provide reviews from people who have stayed there, and note where you’re located in your city.

SharedEasy is an example of a business that does this well. It offers room photos, a 3D tour, testimonials, information about what to do in the neighborhood, public transportation options, and details about nearby airports.

Another important step is to invest in proper SEO to drive targeted traffic to your website.

6 Strategies for Operating a Coliving Space

Now that you know what potential members are looking for in a coworking-coliving space (and what challenges you may have to overcome), here are a few strategies and best practices to get you started.

Understand Your Members

Before you begin with any of the other tips on this list, take some time to get an idea of what type of member you’re targeting. In other words, what’s your Ideal Customer Profile.

This way, you can build a space that meets their needs. For example, is your business meant for people in creative jobs, corporate professionals, or something else?

Once you’ve decided on your target members, you can design your space around them and ensure they have everything they need to thrive.

Choose a Favorable Location

Digital nomads and freelancers often choose coworking-coliving spaces so they can travel and see the world. They may not be very familiar with your city, so it’s likely they’ll seek out a central location to get their feet wet.

New members likely want a location in the heart of your city, within walking distance of shops, restaurants, and public transportation (if applicable). Try to choose a safe but lively neighborhood.

If you’re deciding which city to start your business in, pick one that will attract digital nomads with warm weather, plenty of activities, nightlife, or proximity to the airport.

Prioritize Safety

Coworking-coliving spaces are still a relatively new concept, even though they’re becoming more popular. It’s understandable that members may be wary of safety, especially when they’re living and working in an unfamiliar place.

Get ahead of their concerns and integrate your safety plan into the building and marketing of your space.

Just like hotels have lockboxes, provide ways for your residents to safely store their valuables. You can also install security cameras and ensure members know how to contact onsite managers if needed.

Optimize Your Technology

It’s crucial to have accurate data to help you understand your customer base and guide your decisions, just like it is with a regular coworking space

Plus, the right technology can help you receive clients’ payments efficiently, check metrics like utilization rates, and easily manage your memberships.

Booking systems can also be a great way for new and existing members to reserve meeting rooms, activity rooms, offices, and other coworking spaces. They help eliminate the risk of double booking, ghost booking, and passive occupancy. Choose a software that is easy to implement, simple for your members to use, and customizable, so you can adjust it to fit your needs.

Offer Attractive Amenities

When it comes to choosing the amenities for your space, pick the ones that your target community will enjoy using. You can also consider what may be helpful or necessary for your location, such as air conditioning and a pool in a hot climate.

Other ideas for amenities include:

  • Rooftop or patio access
  • Gym
  • Kitchenette in your room
  • TV in your room
  • Sauna
  • Private bathroom
  • On-site restaurant or coffee shop
  • Laundry service
  • Game room

Provide a Variety of Membership Options

Since we know the typical customer base for coworking-coliving spaces is looking for flexibility, offer a variety of membership options. For example, let your residents stay for a few weeks to a year, and make it easy for them to renew their plan if they want to.

You can also offer membership tiers based on additional services (like room cleaning), room types (like a one or two-bedroom), or amenities (like a private bathroom).

For instance, The Collective Old Oak offers two-bedroom apartments, one-bedroom apartments, and studios. It provides membership plans that last from three months to a year, with options to renew.

Author: asen-stoyanchev

Post body:
Team coordination is a tricky task to master — particularly for hybrid teams. How do you coordinate a team that’s not working in the same building?

The reality is effective team coordination is essential to success. It keeps communication flowing, provides clarity around roles and responsibilities, and ensures that hybrid employees can work as efficiently as possible.

So what can you do to boost team coordination?

A lot. From using the right technology to setting up clear processes, let’s look at how you can set your hybrid workers up for success.

Quick summary:

To improve hybrid team coordination, focus on using the right technology, such as collaboration and scheduling tools, to enhance communication and alignment. Establish clear communication guidelines, define roles and responsibilities, and provide sufficient training to ensure all team members are equipped to collaborate effectively. Encourage open and honest feedback to build trust and continuously refine team processes. These strategies ensure clarity, accountability, and seamless collaboration across remote and in-office team members.

What Is Team Coordination?

Team coordination is the process of team members working together effectively toward a common goal. For example, to achieve a specific project outcome or build a new product.

For hybrid teams, the process involves organizing and aligning efforts between remote and in-office team members. It requires clear communication, transparent role definition, and digital tools to facilitate seamless collaboration — regardless of location.

What Are the Different Types of Team Coordination?

There are two main types of team coordination: explicit and implicit. Let’s look at these in more detail.

Explicit Coordination

Explicit coordination is the process of discussing and sharing team coordination efforts. You create clearly defined roles, responsibilities, and processes that are communicated and agreed on by team members.

A good example of explicit team coordination is project management.

A project manager creates a detailed project plan outlining each team member’s tasks, deadlines, and how to track progress. The project team reviews the plan, understands their role, and is aware of the process for completing the project.

Today, the whole process is done through robust AI project management platforms

Explicit coordination is helpful when managing hybrid employees as it provides clarity, ensuring everyone’s on the same page. However, it can become a little overbearing if it crosses the line into micromanagement.

To avoid micromanaging, focus on the outcomes — not the processes. Use explicit coordination to communicate objectives, deadlines, and deliverables, but don’t control how the work gets done more than necessary.

Implicit Coordination

Implicit coordination relies on a shared understanding and mutual trust among team members. It’s more casual than explicit coordination as it doesn’t involve cut-and-dry boundaries and expectations.

Imagine a graphic designer and a content writer are working together on a new campaign. Without needing constant direction, the designer anticipates the writer’s need for visual assets and proactively shares design drafts. The writer also adjusts the copy to align with the design without needing specific instructions.

Throughout the process, they both adjust their work based on unspoken cues. When one notices the other is behind schedule, they step in to assist. Both team members intuitively support each other without explicit instructions.

Although the idea of implicit collaboration is appealing, it can be challenging for hybrid teams. It lacks the clarity and certainty that most teams require to work together successfully. However, it can be useful for building rapport and trust between team members.

Other Types of Team Coordination

In addition to explicit and implicit coordination, other types of coordination play a part in successful hybrid collaboration:

  • Task coordination. You assign team tasks, set deadlines, and monitor progress to avoid overlap or confusion.
  • Communication coordination. You organize how team members share information, updates, and feedback to ensure smooth communication.
  • Role coordination. You clarify each team member’s responsibilities to eliminate duplication of efforts or gaps in coverage.
  • Schedule coordination. You align team members’ schedules to ensure timely collaboration and task completion. You also accommodate various working hours and time zones.
  • Resource coordination. You manage the allocation and distribution of resources (like tools, equipment, or materials) to ensure team members have what they need to succeed.
  • Goal coordination. You ensure all team members understand and are working toward a collective goal.

Coordinating all of these elements provides structure, clarity, and alignment, ensuring that hybrid teams work well together.

Why Is Successful Team Coordination So Important for Hybrid and Remote Teams?

Successful coordination in hybrid teams can help:

To Improve Team Communication

A key part of team coordination involves clarifying when and how to communicate with team members. It ensures that everyone knows:

  • Which communication platforms to use
  • Who to contact with specific questions
  • When to contact people

For example, let’s say that your hybrid team is working on developing a new product. Someone in the marketing team has a question about product functionality. With effective team coordination, the marketer knows:

  • Who to contact — the product development lead
  • How to contact them — via an instant communication channel
  • When it’s best to contact them — during some free time in their schedule

To Ensure Accountability and Responsibility

Team coordination involves establishing roles and responsibilities in the team. The clear division ensures that team members know exactly what they’re responsible for, which boosts accountability.

Why is this important?

Because having accountability can increase employee motivation and overall happiness. And a happy workforce is more productive (12%), according to studies from a UK university. All that improves the overall team dynamic.

To Increase Efficiency

Failing to align hybrid teams can impact efficiency. Duplicating work, wasting time on unnecessary activities, and working toward different goals are a few examples.

Team coordination brings everyone on the same page, minimizing errors and ensuring hybrid teams work as efficiently as possible.

Think about booking a meeting room space as an example. With effective coordination, you ensure that bookings are smooth and efficient. Without it, you risk double bookings or overstaying meeting time frames — both of which can impact the team’s ability to work.

5 Tips to Improve Hybrid Team Coordination

In workplaces where teams operate across remote and in-office settings, maintaining seamless coordination is key to effective collaboration and remote work productivity.

But how exactly can you ensure successful hybrid team coordination?

Here’s a quick checklist:

Let’s walk through this checklist in more detail.

1. Use the Right Technology

Technology is essential when coordinating hybrid teams. It facilitates seamless communication, enhances collaboration, and helps manage tasks and projects effectively — all of which ensures that hybrid team members stay connected and aligned.

Here are some useful systems to consider:

  • Collaboration technology that helps team members work together effectively, like client management systems or work scheduling platforms. The best collaboration tools depend on your business needs, but common examples include platforms like Google Workspace and HubSpot (both of which integrate with OfficeRnD Workplace).
  • Communication platforms that allow hybrid teams to stay in touch when working in different locations. Instant messaging platforms like Slack and video call software like Microsoft Teams are a couple of examples.

OfficeRnD Workplace is also a useful tool for hybrid work management and team coordination. Use it to see who’s in the office, visualize hybrid employee work schedules, and find and book desks and rooms for onsite collaboration on any device.

2. Establish Clear Communication Guidelines

Clear communication guidelines establish expectations for how, when, and where individual team members communicate. It reduces misunderstandings and provides clarity when people are working at home or in the office.

Here’s how to create clear communication guidelines:

  • Define communication channels. Specify which channels to use for different types of communication. For example, instant messaging for quick questions, email for long-form communication, and video calls for meetings.
  • Set response time expectations. Establish how quickly team members should respond to communication so team members know when to expect replies. For example, two working days for an email and a single day for instant messages.
  • Clarify who to contact for certain queries or updates. Identify team members responsible for specific topics to ensure everyone directs queries to the right person. For example, contacting the HR manager with personnel questions or team supervisors to find out more about specific tasks and activities.

Tip: Schedule a regular time for a full team catch-up to ensure everyone has a chance to be part of the wider workplace community.

3. Create Well-Defined Roles and Responsibilities

Clarify what everyone is responsible for in their day-to-day roles. When everyone understands their role and those of their colleagues, it reduces confusion and duplication of efforts. As a result, it’s easier for team members to work together.

Follow these steps to create well-defined roles and responsibilities for your hybrid team:

  • Conduct a role assessment. Review current roles to better understand the tasks, skills, and responsibilities that sit within each position.
  • Collaborate with relevant stakeholders. Work with managers and team leaders to define each role’s purpose. Their input is crucial because they bring hands-on insight into what the roles entail.
  • Document and share everyone’s roles. Create a shared document that outlines each team member’s responsibilities to ensure everyone knows what they’re responsible for.

4. Provide Sufficient Training and Resources

Providing sufficient training and resources is one of the best ways to improve team coordination.

When hybrid employees know how to use systems, tools, and processes effectively, they can collaborate. And when collaboration goes well, team coordination is easier to manage.

There are a few ways to equip hybrid team members with the necessary skills and tools to collaborate successfully. For example, you can host virtual communication workshops to provide staff with the skills and knowledge to collaborate remotely.

You could also provide tutorials on how to use the company’s collaboration tools. That way, hybrid employees can use company tools to their full capacity.

5. Encourage Open and Honest Feedback

Encouraging open and honest feedback builds trust with hybrid team members. As a result, they feel comfortable enough to share feedback about your team coordination efforts.

Their feedback is incredibly useful for finding areas of improvement and ensuring that hybrid team members feel supported when working away from the office.

Take a look at some of the ways to encourage open and honest feedback:

  • Create regular feedback opportunities. Schedule consistent one-on-one meetings and catch-ups so team members know they have opportunities to share their thoughts and feedback.
  • Allow anonymity. Use surveys to gather feedback, allowing employees to share honest thoughts anonymously without fear of judgment or repercussions.
  • Model the ideal behavior. Demonstrate openness to feedback by actively asking for it, responding positively to suggestions, and implementing improvements.

Name: Where’s The Coworking Space Industry Heading In 2025?
Author: asen-stoyanchev
Short cards description: The future is bright for the coworking space industry. The shift away from traditional office models has been a boom for coworking.
Post body:
The future is bright for the coworking space industry. The shift away from traditional office models has been a boom for coworking.

But coworking itself is experiencing rapid transformation. New trends are emerging related to how companies move forward in their workspace needs and what types of spaces appeal to workers.

It’s not just about location anymore. Branding, design, and strong community are what make today’s top coworking businesses stand out.

With new technologies and more growth coming, let’s dive deep into the exciting developments in coworking.

Quick Summary

  • Coworking spaces continue to be a golden opportunity in 2025 for owners and operators who offer the work environments members are looking for.
  • Trends currently shaping the industry include increasing flexibility, hospitality, and incorporating wellness into member services.
  • Innovators in this industry will overcome specific challenges and create a memorable member experience.

The Current State of the Coworking Industry

From remote workers and freelancers to hybrid companies and businesses looking for places to host events, the market for coworking spaces has never had more potential.

Let’s take a look at the state of the industry, including market characteristics and what’s helping the most successful coworking spaces thrive.

Is the Market for Coworking Spaces Still Growing?

Yes, coworking spaces are still rapidly expanding and reshaping the office landscape. In 2018, there were over 16,000 coworking spaces worldwide. By 2024, that number had increased to over 40,000.

In major US cities, coworking hubs are proliferating. Coworking Cafe reported that of the twenty-five cities they surveyed in 2024, only one didn’t increase its number of coworking spaces.

This growth, though, isn’t only in large cities. Suburban coworking markets are flourishing as workers look for options closer to home.

And the upswing isn’t limited to the United States either. Cities across the world — from Mexico City to Riyadh to Sydney — are seeing an increase in demand for coworking spaces.

These shifts are part of a broader transformation in commercial real estate. More property owners are catering to companies and individuals looking for new work solutions rather than traditional office space.

The shift to hybrid work has been a major driver as companies seek more flexible options. Landlords are increasingly collaborating with coworking space providers in partnerships that capitalize on these trends.

If you’re curious how the flex industry performed in Q2 2025, check out Beyond the Plateau: How the Flex Space Industry Found Stability in 2025. This analysis is based on the OfficeRnD FlexIndex report for Q2 2025.

Who’s Using Coworking Spaces?

Coworking spaces attract many users, from digital nomads to startups and established corporations.

For independent workers, coworking offers flexibility and networking opportunities. It provides them with a more dynamic professional setting than a home office.

It’s not just about technology and flexibility. Coworking spaces deliver a sense of community. They host events, workshops, and social gatherings. These collaborative experiences help freelancers and small teams form invaluable connections.

Many businesses hold training sessions or team-building activities. They take advantage of on-site meeting rooms and event spaces.

Large corporations are also increasingly using these workspaces. Often, they serve as satellite offices or overflow hubs.

What Makes Coworking Spaces Successful?

Success in the coworking industry depends on delivering features and amenities that appeal to a diverse set of users.

Location and accessibility are top priorities. Spaces near public transit or walkable neighborhoods attract more members. But location alone isn’t enough.

You have to offer a sense of community with modern amenities and technological infrastructure to make an ideal coworking location. You want your space to feel like a hub for productivity and professional growth.

That’s why mastering hospitality is key in 2025 and beyond.

Emerging Trends Shaping the Future of Coworking

What’s the norm in the coworking industry continues to evolve. No longer are these flex spaces just home offices away from home. They’re so much more than that, offering niche communities, wellness add-ons, and more.

Niche Spaces

The importance of community has already been stressed. But one of the best ways to create that community is to cater to specific groups.

Niche spaces are designed specifically for groups of people with shared interests or identities. Some examples include women, creatives, working parents, and freelancers.

Inclusive spaces designed for underrepresented groups are also popping up, such as spaces for LGBTQ members. These environments offer unique features and resources to make people feel welcome.

By providing services unique to each demographic’s needs, satisfaction and belonging increase.

For example, women-focused coworking spaces may offer extra safety features. Spaces designed for working parents may include nursing stations and on-site childcare.

This niche approach makes tight-knit communities and collaboration more likely. This smaller, community-centered approach appeals to members looking to feel seen and supported in a more personal setting.

Increased Flexibility

Despite some shifts toward working in the office, Owl Labs’ recent report showed that hybrid work is still trending upward in 2024.

This rise of hybrid work has driven coworking spaces to become more flexible. They’re offering more choices in membership options and in services that attract different users.

Many companies are partnering with coworking spaces, covering memberships for their hybrid employees. To entice these companies, options have expanded to include day passes, part-time memberships, and package deals for corporations.

Coworking spaces are also evolving to serve as “third places.” These spaces are separate settings from the home or the office. Coworking spaces can deliver this experience through fostering social interaction and a built-in culture.

Amenities also demonstrate the move toward flexibility — whether it’s gaming areas, quiet pods, or concierge-style service.

Check out what we have in store for 2025 and why it's important for you.

Positive Impacts

Modern coworking spaces are placing a stronger emphasis on wellness and social responsibility. They’re integrating offerings that improve members’ well-being and sense of purpose.

Here are some wellness programs that are becoming more common:

  • Yoga classes
  • Meditation sessions
  • Mental health resources
  • Wellness coaching

This shift to wellness has become more standard to help members manage stress and avoid burnout.

Environmental sustainability is another growing focus. Many coworking operators are adopting eco-friendly practices such as biophilic design, energy-efficient lighting, and composting.

Coworking spaces also encourage recycling and other green initiatives. It reduces their environmental impact and appeals to members who prioritize sustainability.

We recently held a super insightful sustainability webinar that featured space-as-a-service legend Antony Slumbers. Watch it for free here.

Challenges for the Coworking Industry

Just because the coworking market is strong, doesn’t mean it’s problem-free. In fact, the same growth and trends happening are opening up new challenges and considerations.

1. Underutilization

Fluctuating occupancy rates are a hurdle. Startups, freelancers, and small businesses can mean high turnover. Also, with the hybrid work trend, Mondays and Fridays are typically lower-traffic days as more workers stay home.

In saturated markets, especially in major cities, coworking spaces may have trouble filling vacancies if they don’t have a way to stand out.

To address these issues, operators are implementing loyalty programs and offering discounted day passes or special events on low-traffic days.

Spaces with a strong community culture and unique amenities do better at filling their work areas.

2. Authenticity vs. Scale

As coworking spaces scale, it’s more difficult to maintain authentic connections. Operators need to be modern and relevant, but also personal.

They also have to compete with larger operators with the resources to offer extensive services. To stay competitive, smaller spaces must focus on the community and belonging aspects of their coworking space.

They need to drive engagement with exclusive, localized offerings such as unique workshops and partnerships. They should personalize the member experience in ways not possible for larger operators.

Larger spaces should try to create micro-communities as much as possible. They can also create membership packages that allow members to customize their experience.

3. Flexibility vs. Profitability

Flexible membership options — including pay-as-you-go or part-time access — are a compelling way to attract users. But, they can also result in unpredictable revenue.

Economic fluctuations can further impact profitability. Corporate clients, in particular, expect flexibility along with competitive rates.

You can create a tiered loyalty program that rewards members based on the duration of their membership to help balance flexibility and profitability. It also may help to develop a dynamic pricing model based on seasonal changes or times of peak usage.

4. Costs and Compliance

Lastly, rising real estate costs are a major factor in negotiating favorable leases and managing the budget.

Changing labor laws, zoning regulations, and building codes add a layer of complexity that can require significant expenses. Keeping pace with technology isn’t cheap either.

Creating areas that are multi-functional helps — such as a meeting room that can also host events. And the right coworking software can be used to automate compliance and avoid fines.

How to Be at the Cutting Edge of the Coworking Industry

Let’s discuss how to be a leader in the coworking industry. These three strategies can get you off to a powerful start.

Leverage Technology

Modern tools help your space become more efficient and deliver a better member experience.

For example, use software such as OfficeRnD Flex for automating bookings and billing.

Going further, adopt artificial intelligence (AI) tools to level up the workspace. Coworking owners and operators can optimize layouts, track usage, and predict demand for certain amenities.

Technology can also personalize member experiences by recommending tailored events and sending automatic reminders.

Lastly, you could offer a mobile app where members can manage bookings, make payments, and access amenities.

Transform the Coworking Experience (Master Hospitality)

Community engagement remains central to the coworking model.

Start with free trials and unique membership options to get users in the door. Then, build an engaging space through networking sessions, wellness programs, and skill-building workshops.

Next, offer an experience that’s transformative. One of the best ways to do this is by involving your community.

Collaborate with local artists to fill gallery walls, host workshops, or co-create with members. Partner with local businesses to offer rotating pop-up services, such as massage therapy.

You can even combine coworking with a co-living space. These buildings have private residences, shared kitchens, and dedicated work areas. This combination attracts digital nomads and relocating professionals.

Be a Leader in Sustainability

Sustainability is a defining feature of leading coworking spaces. Operators can reduce their environmental impact and set a positive example with a comprehensive strategy.

Start with goals. Monitor energy consumption and set targets to become more efficient – set goals for reducing waste. Establish recycling stations, even for hard-to-recycle items like batteries or e-waste. Set up composting and other waste reduction initiatives.

Partner with environmental nonprofits to run carbon offsetting programs. Source local and/or sustainable ingredients, such as food and office supplies.

Then, reward environmentally friendly behavior among members. You can offer a points program where members earn points through sustainable actions that can be redeemed for free coffee or membership discounts.

The Future of Coworking: What to Expect in 2025 and Beyond

As we march into the future, here are three trends to expect in the coming years:

Continued Expansion of Hybrid Work

As hybrid work solidifies its place in corporate culture, more people will choose coworking. This move away from long-term office leases will favor subscription models and other flexible options offered by coworking spaces.

Companies will do this in large part to attract and retain top talent. As competition increases, coworking spaces will offer unique amenities like rooftop lounges, podcast studios, and wine tastings.

Short-term office rentals and hybrid meeting spaces will also become increasingly popular. That will allow businesses to scale workspace needs based on project demands.

Wellness and Mental Health Integration

Wellness and mental health support will remain a top priority in coworking. Spaces will expand their offerings to include more fitness classes and meditation sessions. Mental health resources and peer support networks will become more commonplace.

Burnout prevention and community-led wellness activities will become a more integral part of the coworking culture.

Shift to the Small Towns and Suburbs

With workers wanting to avoid long commutes, suburban coworking spaces are expected to flourish. They’ll serve as smaller satellite operations in a “hub-and-spoke” model.

These suburban hubs will offer modern workspaces with outdoor areas and wellness programs. They’ll act as appealing alternatives to traditional urban offices.

Coworking spaces may also start appearing in unexpected locations, such as airports, shopping malls, and residential complexes. This shift supports both work-life balance and convenience.

It’s time to apply that knowledge and become a leader in this industry. To do so, you’ll want the best tools.

Hybrid work is a model where employees split their week between the office and a remote location, on a set or flexible schedule.

We asked why teams come into the office. The answers were about the people: the energy of a room working through a problem, the ideas that show up when you’re sitting next to someone.

That question sits behind our new report, The Hybrid Work Playbook 2026. For most organisations, hybrid is now simply how work happens: some people in part of the time, others remote, everyone managing the in-between. Having a hybrid policy and running a hybrid office well are two different things. The companies that get the most from hybrid (better collaboration, lower costs, higher retention) do a handful of things differently, and the report turns those into habits any office team can apply.

Why You Need This Report

Good workplace decisions start with current data, not last year’s assumptions. The 2026 playbook is built for HR leaders, workplace and facilities managers, and operations teams who decide how office space gets used.

Key Highlights

Three numbers set the scene:

From there, the report covers:

(KPMG CEO Outlook) The CIPD found 70% of employees say the pressure to return comes from senior leaders. (CIPD)

Name: What Makes A Good Coworking Space: 23 Must-Have Features
Author: asen-stoyanchev
Short cards description: Creating a coworking space that attracts and retains members requires more than an open sign. As competition increases, owners and operators must deliver a workspace that drives productivity and community.
Post body:
Creating a coworking space that attracts and retains members requires more than an open sign. As competition increases, owners and operators must deliver a workspace that drives productivity and community.

They must create a member experience that keeps users loyal and encourages them to tell their friends.

According to research we did earlier this year, word of mouth is the most popular way members choose a space.

So what are the top qualities that define a standout coworking environment?

Quick Summary

  • A good coworking space provides features that inspire creativity, support productivity, and foster community.
  • It’s important to focus on functional features while also providing a welcoming environment.
  • Bringing together these factors into your coworking space creates a desirable place for members.

13 Essentials Your Coworking Space Should Have

Some coworking space features and amenities are negotiable — but not the ones on this list. If you want to succeed as a coworking space in 2025 and beyond, these offerings are necessities:

Reliable Internet

A coworking space must offer high-speed internet with minimal downtime.

If you have multiple network options, you can prevent congestion and ensure fast speeds. A backup internet source adds reliability. Built-in VPN services improve security, which is important for remote workers handling sensitive data.

We recently teamed up with technologywithin to provide coworking space operators with top tier internet services.

Robust Tech and Equipment

Coworking spaces should provide essential technology like printers, scanners, and ample charging stations.

Backup power systems and dedicated IT support maintain productivity when the inevitable arises. Offer access to printers through the cloud so that even mobile users can print. Noise-canceling headphones on loan add further flexibility, as do self-service tech kiosks.

Ergonomic and Adjustable Furniture

Ergonomic furniture supports member comfort during long hours.

That includes adjustable chairs and standing desks with anti-fatigue mats. Modular furniture can be rearranged, and varied seating styles — like booths and lounge chairs — accommodate different body sizes.

Some of your areas should be able to shift seamlessly to suite workshops, presentations, or quiet work sessions, depending on what’s needed that day.

Also, why not consider transforming your space into a coliving space?

Design-Led Workspaces

Well-designed spaces inspire creativity and work satisfaction.

Incorporate artwork, themed decor, and indoor plants to create a welcoming atmosphere. Natural lighting and high-quality ventilation contribute to a healthy, productive environment. Thoughtful design reminds members they’re not in a traditional office.

Focus-Friendly Workspaces

Members need focus-friendly areas that are protected from distractions.

Soundproof pods, private offices, and quiet floors support their desire for deep work. Features like acoustic panels and carpeting reduce noise in high-traffic zones. These spaces allow members to focus without interruption.

Designate specific hours and guidelines for silent working in quiet zones.

Collaboration Areas

Workers also need places to collaborate and communicate together.

These spaces must cater to both in-person and virtual teamwork. Meeting rooms should include screens, projectors, and video conferencing setups. Reservable spaces, from casual meeting rooms to formal presentation areas, ensure teams can collaborate effectively.

Include writable walls or glass partitions for brainstorming.

Dedicated Reception or Front Desk

A staffed reception area provides a professional first impression and a point of contact.

Receptionists assist with deliveries, help visitors check in, and assist members. They help book meeting rooms and private spaces for members who aren’t using your mobile app. The reception can double as a helpdesk for troubleshooting.

The OfficeRnD Visitor Hub is a robust visitor management system that streamlines visitor management and turns visitors into leads. Check it out!

Kitchen and Refreshment Areas

A well-equipped coworking space kitchen is important for convenience and community.

You will need a refrigerator, microwave, and coffee machines. Healthy snack bars or vending machines add value. Social dining areas encourage social interaction among members. That builds a sense of belonging and makes breaks more enjoyable.

Secure, Regular Access

Flexible, but secure entry options provide safe access to your space.

Keycards or app-based access make entrance easy and safe around the clock. Features like security cameras and fingerprint scanning software help protect the premises. Your facilities should also be compliant with ADA standards.

A Convenient Location

Location remains critical for coworking spaces.

Your site should be close to public transportation and have accessible parking. Nearby amenities like cafes, gyms, or shops improve the member experience. An attractive, visible location also enhances your coworking space’s brand. It makes it easier for members to find.

Storage Solutions

Members need secure, convenient storage for their personal items.

Offer lockers, lockable desk drawers, and individual storage cabinets. That protects members’ belongings and maintains a tidy workspace. You can include setups within lockers to charge devices overnight.

Community Boards or Digital Bulletin Boards

Bulletin boards keep members informed on upcoming events and general announcements.

These boards can be physical or digital. Either way, they connect members through engaging activities and clear information.

Bulletin boards are a great way to post team-building opportunities, workshops, member spotlights, and more.

Feedback System

A robust feedback system is vital for continuous improvement.

Use tools like mobile apps, email surveys, and suggestion boxes to gain insights. Target surveys to figure out member issues and pain points. Then, communicate any updates or improvements to show their input is valued.

This could significantly help you track your NPS score.

10 Optional Extras of a Coworking Space

Just because you cover the essentials doesn’t mean you can’t go further to stand out. If you’re looking to level up your coworking spaces, consider these options, that go beyond unique amenities.

Fresh Food Options

One palpable way to drive more value for members is to enhance your food offerings.

Go beyond convenience with an on-site cafe that provides fresh and healthy options. Sourcing foods locally from small businesses, like nearby bakeries and fresh juice producers, can elevate the experience.

If you can, host rotating food trucks nearby.

Wellness Amenities

Wellness facilities and amenities support physical and mental health to create a more balanced coworking culture.

Meditation rooms, fitness areas, and quiet pods for short naps signal an emphasis on well-being. Providing mental health resources, like access to counselors or wellness workshops, demonstrates this concern for your members.

Pet-Friendly Environment

Allowing pets in your coworking space can boost morale and create a relaxed atmosphere.

Pet-friendly areas are good for people who love animals. You can also designate pet-free zones for people who don’t want to be near animals or who have allergies.

A compromise is to offer “bring your pet to work” days.

Childcare Services

On-site childcare or partnering with local providers can drive satisfaction for working parents. Having their kids close by brings peace of mind and can increase long-term loyalty.

Spaces with flexible hours, activities for children, and skilled staff create a family-friendly atmosphere that parents will appreciate.

Sustainability Focus

Sustainable coworking spaces attract a growing number of eco-conscious members. This is where the industry is heading!

Incorporate features like energy-efficient lighting, smart thermostats, zero-waste policies, and recycling/composting programs. Demonstrate a commitment to environmental stewardship through achieving LEED certification for your building.

Incentivize the use of public transportation or biking to work. Install secure bike racks and have a bike repair station. Host sustainability workshops and educate members on the importance of eco-friendly practices in the coworking space.

Professional Development Opportunities

Coworking spaces that assist professional growth are likely to benefit from more loyal members.

Networking events, workshops, and mentoring programs are effective ways to provide these opportunities and make your space a hub for career advancement.

Industry-specific seminars or leadership training sessions don’t just develop skills, but connect peers professionally.

Outdoor Workspaces

Spaces to work outside can encourage creativity and relaxation.

Consider outdoor work areas such as rooftop lounges or courtyards to offer your members a unique setting to be productive. These spaces provide workers with fresh air, natural light, and a break from traditional workspaces.

They help with well-being and can inspire innovative thinking.

Higher-Tech Amenities

Another noticeable way to take your coworking space to a new level is through technology.

High-tech amenities give your space a modern and efficient workflow. Smart scheduling systems, digital lockers, and virtual concierge services are such features. VR stations for virtual meetings are another state-of-the-art inclusion.

On-Site Business Support

Take care of business support services on your premises to boost convenience.

You can offer the following:

  • Virtual addresses
  • Package handling
  • Mail services
  • Document shredding
  • And a lending library of office supplies

Additional offerings like notary services or event coordination make it easy to accomplish professional tasks without leaving the site.

Members-Only Discounts and Local Partnerships

Negotiate exclusive member deals with local businesses.

Partnerships with gyms, restaurants, and retailers add value to their membership. Partners also strengthen the coworking space’s connection to the community.

Name: How Flex Spaces Can Attract More Members By Focusing On Sustainability
Author: asen-stoyanchev
Short cards description: In an increasingly eco-conscious world, flex space operators are at the frontlines of a paradigm shift: transforming workspaces into green havens that foster community, growth, and sustainability.
Post body:
In an increasingly eco-conscious world, flex space operators are at the frontlines of a paradigm shift: transforming workspaces into green havens that foster community, growth, and sustainability.

A recent survey reveals that sustainability plays a very important role in the decision-making process of potential members.

Recently, a panel of experts gathered to explore how sustainability could be leveraged to attract more members and drive success in flex spaces.

Our webinar “Attract More Members by Focusing on Workplace Sustainability”, provided actionable insights you can employ to meet evolving corporate and societal demands for environmentally friendly workspaces.

And, of course, boost your membership rate.

Let’s dive into the key takeaways from this engaging discussion, led by prominent voices in sustainability, PropTech, and workspace design: Hubert Abt, Antony Slumbers, James Dearsley, Miro Miroslavov, and Monika Pawelczak.

This is just a quick recap of the webinar, for which we received extremely positive feedback. To learn all the insights, watch it here for free.

ESG Compliance: Not Just a Trend, But a Necessity

The conversation kicked off with a presentation by the unofficial Mr. ESG of the real estate world and CEO of workcloud24, Hubert Abt who demystified Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) compliance in the real estate industry.

ESG is often seen as a complicated, bureaucratic term, but Hubert broke it down to its essentials: transparency and intentionality.

To achieve ESG compliance, flex spaces need to focus on disclosing environmental impact data, improving operational efficiency, and shifting mindsets around sustainability.

The challenge is clear: we’re already exceeding planetary limits, with carbon emissions surpassing healthy thresholds. This means the goal isn’t just about compliance but about positioning your flex space as part of the solution.

Coworking operators who understand how to communicate their sustainability efforts effectively are far better positioned to meet corporate expectations, fulfill environmental requirements, and ultimately attract more members.

Why ESG Storytelling Matters

Antony Slumbers, a well-known advisor in the PropTech space, emphasized that ESG isn’t just about compliance—it’s about storytelling.

Customers, whether freelancers or corporate tenants, increasingly seek meaning behind the services they purchase. They want to support businesses that align with their values.

This desire to support sustainable initiatives creates an opportunity for coworking operators to tell an impactful story. Antony noted that coworking spaces need to “go all-in” on sustainability, not just implementing it in part.

Making your building more energy-efficient is just one piece of the puzzle; the real differentiator is in communicating why you care, how your actions contribute to a greener world, and how members can be a part of this journey.

Hubert backed this up with an example from the flex office industry: tracking and reducing energy consumption is key, but making tenants feel good about these efforts is equally important.

From visible dashboards that show carbon savings to educational materials on how individuals contribute to reduced emissions, coworking spaces need to leverage every opportunity to engage their community in sustainability.

Engaging Tenants for a Sustainable Future

Hubert, Antony, and the rest of the panel emphasized that the tenants’ engagement is central to successful sustainability initiatives.

The panelists discussed various methods that flex space operators can use to actively involve their members, from workshops on green behavior to transparency about energy consumption.

James Dearsley, CEO of Verv, pointed out that a combination of behavioral change and technology is what will ultimately drive results.

Flex operators should make it easy for tenants to engage in sustainability, whether by providing recycling solutions, sharing insights on energy consumption, or creating programs that reward sustainable behavior.

This sentiment was echoed by our own Miro Miroslavov, CEO of OfficeRnD, who added that the future of work is hybrid.

The more people opt for flexible and hybrid work solutions, the more we reduce commuting emissions. Facilitating hybrid work not only makes offices more sustainable but also caters to tenants’ needs for flexibility, further enhancing customer loyalty and satisfaction.

Certifications Bring Credibility, But Storytelling Differentiates

During the discussion, Hubert addressed the role of sustainability certifications. While certifications like LEED and WELL add credibility, especially for corporate clients, they shouldn’t be the only focus.

Certifications provide a benchmark, but what resonates with customers is how sustainability is woven into their experience.

This is where storytelling becomes crucial. According to Antony, flex space operators need to craft a narrative that showcases their vision of a greener workspace.

He stressed that, ultimately, human-centric and sustainable design wins. It’s about creating spaces that cater to people’s needs while also caring for the environment. As he pointed out:

It’s not enough to be sustainable on paper; spaces must inspire occupants to be part of the solution.

The ROI of Sustainability: More Than Financial

One significant challenge in the flex space industry is the cost and return on investment of sustainability efforts.

James highlighted that sustainability is not always viewed favorably when it comes to direct ROI. Many landlords remain wary of capital expenditure for sustainability upgrades without clear, immediate returns.

However, the panel agreed that sustainability’s ROI extends beyond financial metrics. A sustainable workspace boosts customer loyalty, improves retention rates, and attracts environmentally conscious tenants.

Hubert brought up a critical point:

Today’s customers, especially large corporations, are prioritizing sustainability in decision-making.

If coworking operators want to attract corporate clients and future-proof their business, they must be seen as ESG-compliant, transparent, and environmentally responsible.

Technology’s Role in Driving Sustainability

Technology was another key area of discussion. From IoT sensors that track energy consumption to smart waste management systems, technology provides powerful tools for understanding and minimizing environmental impact.

Hubert described how implementing sensors across a workspace can help create data-driven dashboards that allow members to track carbon footprints in real-time.

This kind of transparency not only meets compliance needs but also inspires a change in behavior among occupants.

Artificial intelligence (AI), as Antony mentioned, is also critical in guiding users toward better sustainability practices. AI can act as an educator, providing useful insights into efficient energy use, responsible material sourcing, and behavior change opportunities. This creates a strong foundation for sustainability in every aspect of workspace management.

Shifting Mindsets to Enable Transformation

The overarching message from the webinar was clear: true sustainability requires a shift in mindset.

While it’s crucial to follow best practices and implement sustainable technologies, the heart of sustainability lies in creating a shared mission that both operators and tenants can rally behind. Antony argued that flex operators who embrace a proactive ESG mindset can truly transform not only their spaces but also the industry at large.

Key Takeaway: Make ESG Easy and Engaging

The insights from the panel paint a vivid picture of how sustainability can be effectively integrated into coworking and flex office operations.

ESG compliance is becoming a necessity rather than an option, but it should not be viewed as a burden. Instead, flex operators must view sustainability as an opportunity to differentiate themselves, build stronger relationships with members, and create better work environments.

The simplest way to achieve this is to make sustainability compliance easy and engaging for your tenants. Create a narrative, engage your community, use technology to measure impact, and be transparent.

By doing so, you not only align with global sustainability goals but also meet the evolving expectations of your customers—and that’s a win-win for everyone involved.

Ready to Take Your Flex Space to the Next Level?

Whether you’re already implementing sustainability initiatives or just beginning your journey, there’s always room for growth. Start by assessing your sustainability status today and craft your story that will resonate with tenants tomorrow. Sustainability isn’t just the future of coworking—it’s what makes your space the place people want to work in right now.
