What Are the Benefits of Coworking Spaces?

Coworking spaces allow members to work alone or with others, whether they’re self-employed or part of a bigger company. It gives them to access many amenities (that would be expensive to buy) and the flexibility to choose their own working hours.

Let’s dive deeper into the top 9 benefits for members and companies who use these spaces.

1. Offers Flexible Working Hours

Unlike traditional offices that close after business hours, many coworking spaces are open 24/7. This allows members to have more flexible working schedules, whether independently or as part of a larger company.

This flexibility allows them to create a better work-life balance that suits their personal and professional needs.

The reality is that poor work-life balance is one of the main reasons why employees leave their jobs. Employers know this, so marketing your coworking space as a solution to this problem can motivate employers to suggest (or even offer as a benefit) coworking spaces to their remote employees.

2. Provides Remote Access

Coworking spaces are available around the globe (check the best ones in the USA), offering maximum flexibility for digital nomads and remote workers who need to work while on the move.

Thanks to consistent access to wifi, desks, meeting rooms, printing facilities, and other amenities, they can continue to work regardless of their location—allowing for minimum disruptions to their workflows.

As more companies are moving towards remote and hybrid work models, this alone will drive a lot of business for these spaces.

3. Offers Plenty of Amenities and Perks

Speaking of amenities, coworking spaces are fully equipped with all the necessary office furniture and amenities professionals could possibly need to get their work done:

  • High-speed internet: Reliable connectivity to keep members online and productive.
  • Meeting rooms: Professional spaces for client meetings and team discussions.

  • High-quality air and lighting: Including natural and LED lights, as well as air conditioning.
  • Recreation areas: Spaces to unwind and recharge (including indoor and outdoor).
  • Quiet zones: Designated areas for focused work without interruptions.
  • Phone booths: Private spaces for phone calls and meetings.

Many freelancers and small businesses may not have the funds to set up all this in a private office, so having everything available is a massive draw.

4. Reduces Member Loneliness

Many remote workers, freelancers, and entrepreneurs who work from home feel lonely and isolated. By joining a coworking space, they become part of a group and get to be around people who are also working to grow their businesses.

From the person greeting them when they arrive to the worker sitting at the desk next to them, these are the interactions that are missing when working alone. These moments of human connection are also what binds coworking communities together.

The relationships formed within these spaces can lead to:

  • Collaborations
  • Friendships
  • Partnerships
  • Mentorship opportunities

All of this improves the experience, creating brand loyalty and making members return time and again.

5. Gives Members a Chance to Network and Build Friendships

Thirty-four percent of coworking users view the ability to network as one of the main perks of coworking spaces.

Members can meet people they wouldn’t otherwise, which is highly beneficial to small businesses and freelancers. This is especially true if the space hosts:

  • Frequent networking events with expert speakers
  • Educational workshops
  • Meet and greets
  • Monthly challenges where members can engage with each other and share ideas

Some coworking spaces also have online platforms or community apps where members can connect and share resources — creating even more networking opportunities.

This can lead to what is known as the network effect.

6. Increases Productivity

Coworking spaces are designed to minimize distractions. Their designs provide members with high-quality air, a lot of natural light, adequate space to work in, soft background music, and often plenty of greenery.

These spaces also have different workstations based on varying work styles and needs. This includes dedicated desks, meeting rooms, larger tables for collaboration, and more.

Additionally, if the space is open 24/7, members can work during their most productive working hours. For example, while some members may be more productive in the morning, from 7 am to 11 am, others may prefer working in the evening.

7. Cuts Expenses for Individuals and Companies

Why Is Starting a Coworking Space a Smart Move?

Name: What’s The Ideal Office Seating Arrangement? [Quick Guide]
Author: asen-stoyanchev
Short cards description: As hybrid work continues to evolve, employers are thinking more about office layouts. As a result, they’re transforming office spaces to accommodate more agile, connected teams.
Post body:
As hybrid work continues to evolve, employers are thinking more about office layouts. As a result, they’re transforming office spaces to accommodate more agile, connected teams.

Assigned seating and fixed working hours no longer constrain office layouts. Today’s hybrid teams need flexible, adaptable workspaces that scale quickly and are 100% plug-and-play.

This comprehensive guide explores six types of office seating arrangements for hybrid teams, from remote-first to office-first.

Quick Summary

  • A hybrid workforce needs an office seating arrangement tailored to their work pattern.
  • Hybrid office seating arrangements facilitate collaboration while optimizing space utilization.
  • Space management tools can improve workplace experiences by making it easier for teams to book desks, schedule meeting spaces, and collaborate.

An Office Seating Arrangement is a Top Concern for a Hybrid Workforce

Office seating arrangements impact employees’ physical and mental comfort, affecting workplace productivity and well-being.

An optimal arrangement can create an agile work environment that caters to employee needs, improving engagement, collaboration, and productivity.

Realizing these benefits requires companies to be thoughtful and intentional in their physical workspace designs. The challenge for employers is to create an office environment that optimizes space utilization while providing the flexibility that hybrid teams need.

To dive deeper, check out our webinar: Navigating the Transition to a Hybrid Work Model.

Benefits of a Well-Designed Office Seating Arrangement in a Hybrid Workplace

According to Deliotte’s 2024 Human Capital Trends report, nearly 70% of the global workforce prefers a hybrid work arrangement.

A carefully considered office seating arrangement enhances the performance of a hybrid workforce. Employers and employees can enjoy the benefits of an office seating chart that fits the flexible work patterns of a hybrid team.

Optimizes Space Utilization

One of the most significant benefits of a well-designed seating arrangement is better space utilization.

Over 90% of CEOs reported cost savings after implementing a hybrid working model. The majority of those savings were due to better office space utilization.

Many teams switching to a hybrid work model find they don’t need as much office space as they used to. Designing your office layout for your team’s current needs and identifying and unloading under-utilized desks, offices, and other resources can lead to significant cost savings.

Boosts Productivity

The right office seating arrangement for your hybrid workforce will minimize distractions and maximize collaboration and productivity.

A thoughtful office seating plan should be flexible. That way, employees can decide when and where they’ll be most effective.

Improves Employee Experiences

A well-designed office seating arrangement is employee-centered. Hybrid-working employees need easy access and effective ways to collaborate and connect with colleagues (both face-to-face and virtually).

The right seating arrangement fosters a positive workplace experience and brings together physical and digital workspaces. This, in turn, can boost employee engagement, well-being, and talent retention in your organization.

Types of Office Seating Arrangements for Hybrid Working

Hybrid working is understandably diverse, with organizations adopting working arrangements that suit their needs.

The options range from prioritizing in-office attendance to allowing near-full-time remote working. So, there isn’t one single office seating arrangement that’s “best” or suitable for all hybrid workplaces.

A well-designed office design considers what employees need to be effective. It considers everything from the nature of the work to individual preferences to find what works. The goal is to find an arrangement that supports collaboration and encourages flexibility and productivity.

Below are six office seating arrangements that span the key modes of hybrid working.

Check out this hybrid work model quiz to find out the ideal hybrid work model for you.

Office Seating Arrangement for Office-First Hybrid Working

Office-first hybrid working prioritizes office attendance, with employees spending most of their time there. In this arrangement, an employer offers employees remote working on a single day each week or a few days per month.

Since the office is the principal place of work, this type of seating arrangement uses joint seating arrangements like cubicles or bench seating.

Cubicles are a classic office seating arrangement with employees provided with individual booths. Bench seating is more open, but the seating plan is still fixed, with each worker allocated a specific work area.

Contemporary office seating arrangements like open-plan seating, team tables, and flexible seating can promote collaboration and drive innovation.

Remove partitions, screens, and boundaries between team members to facilitate communication, reduce space requirements, and benefit from lower implementation costs than a conventional office layout.

Employers can also improve workplace occupancy and shape company culture with innovative amenities. Healthy food and drink places, gyms, and quiet spaces are improvements that help companies attract and keep good employees.

Office Seating Arrangement for Remote-First Hybrid Working

The remote-first work model lies at the opposite extreme of office-first working. Employees mostly work outside the office.

Remote-first workplaces rely on technology, with staff using online platforms and collaborative technologies to share, send, and complete work.

Office seating arrangements for a remote-first workforce should maximize collaboration between in-person and remote employees. Equip meeting rooms with the latest conference room tech and high-resolution screens to keep decentralized teams connected.

Hot-desking and office hoteling give these fast, dynamic teams the flexibility they need. Employees can choose where and when they work.

  • Hot-desking directs workers to available desks on a rota basis. Desk space can be allocated to any employee and without fixed seating, redundant office space is minimized.
  • Office hoteling is a managed arrangement where employees reserve access to office workspace and resources like meeting rooms. This office seating arrangement is very flexible. It lets employees plan their office time with the peace of mind that they have a place to work.

Flexibility doesn’t mean a free-for-all. Competent office management systems and protocols underpin remote-first office seating. These systems need to be readily accessed by all team members for desk bookings and oversight of space utilization.

Office Seating Arrangement for Split-Schedule Hybrid Working

A split-schedule workforce works a fixed proportion of the week on-site and remotely. These teams need options that can be scaled up or down according to changing daily demand.

Office seating also needs to support hybrid meetings with remote team members and support a smooth transition between in-person and remote working to minimize downtime.

Hybrid office spaces that have different schedules can use different hybrid office design solutions to make their employees more productive. These solutions help them work better together as their teams change daily.

Open-plan, modular seating can hold a quick desk meeting, add more workers who work in person, and encourage employees to talk to each other. Breakout spaces like huddle rooms reduce congestion and facilitate focused interaction with remote workers, keeping them on-page and engaged.

Office Seating Arrangement for Hybrid-At-Will Working

Hybrid-at-will working empowers employees to choose remote or in-office work on any given day. An ‘at-will’ schedule is particularly challenging for employers as they need to provide workspaces for regularized in-office work and visiting remote employees.

All workers need enough space, whether they are mostly working from home or not. Seating arrangements help everyone on the team feel included and involved.

Without careful planning, a hybrid-at-will-work policy can become unwieldy and expensive, due to the variable numbers of in-person workers. The design needs to include more space for use with flexible seating and desk sharing. This can be increased or decreased based on the number of employees in the company.

Research has shown that each hybrid-working employee needs up to 150 square feet of office space to use. There are two desks for every employee, and the office is planned to be most busy on Tuesday through Thursday.

Office seating management software can add structure to at-will hybrid working by facilitating desk and conference room bookings. The data generated by using office management tools for hybrid work environments can also provide managers with oversight of office occupancy.

Office Seating Arrangement for Fixed Hybrid Working

Fixed hybrid working fixes office attendance for most staff with scheduled remote working offered to a rotating group of employees.

For many employers, a conventional office setting can be the basis of creating seating plans that provide a productive work environment for on-site employees while being flexible enough to accommodate remote workers.

Your company’s office seating plan can help employees balance their work-from-home and in-person workdays better, making sure that team members who have problems can get help quickly.

Open-plan seating lets employees talk to each other more easily providing access and opportunities to talk about their worries or get in touch with line managers without feeling uncomfortable.

Employers also need to be mindful of maintaining a close-knit team where everyone is engaged and effective. Again, huddle rooms and meeting pods can be equipped for spontaneous hybrid meetings, while efforts to include quiet spaces can support employee wellbeing.

Office Seating Arrangement for Shift Hybrid Working

Shift working arrangements provide workers with office space, throughout the day and night with remote working for the remainder of their time. Office time is restricted with set start and end times and scheduling to ensure enough staff are always available.

Shift working has the additional challenge of providing an office environment that can accommodate the additional needs of night-shift workers (e.g. adjustable ergonomic seating or enhanced lighting). Cubicles are often good for workers who work shifts as they offer privacy and focus while working for a set amount of time.

Office managers and coworkers also need to be aware of who is in the office and the available resources at any given time.

A digital office map is a useful tool that renders a digital copy of your office seating plan. It can provide staff and managers with desk occupancy, the location of important resources, and a directory ofpeople the in-person team may need to access.

Use the Right Technology to Create a Better Office Seating Plan

Robust and responsive office management is key to making your hybrid office seating plan work. Whatever office seating arrangement you choose, hybrid work software can help.

With a hybrid work platform like OfficeRnD Workplace, teams can pull up an interactive office map to see who’s in the office, book desks, reserve meeting rooms, and much more.

With it, you can create and manage different seating arrangements such as hot deksing, desk hoteling, and activity-based working. Plus, it provides you with advanced workplace analytics and insights thanks to which you can make more informed business decisions. And it integrates with Google and Microsoft-based work suites.

Author: asen-stoyanchev
Short cards description: For any business or organization, creating an exceptional member experience is the key to success. One of the most reliable ways to measure how well you’re doing with these efforts is through your Net Promoter Score (NPS). So, what exactly is an NPS, and why is it important for coworking spaces?
Post body:
For any business or organization, creating an exceptional member experience is the key to success. One of the most reliable ways to measure how well you’re doing with these efforts is through your Net Promoter Score (NPS). So, what exactly is an NPS, and why is it important for coworking spaces?

NPS is a customer loyalty metric that gauges how likely your members are to recommend your space to others. It is a simple yet powerful tool that lends insight into customer satisfaction, member retention, and areas for improvement. In coworking, where member experiences directly influence growth and retention, boosting your NPS can mean the difference between just surviving and truly thriving.

If you want to take your NPS from good to great, follow us on this journey as we explore strategies to get you there. Let’s dive in.

Quick Summary

Some of the proven ways to increase your coworking space NPS score are:

  • Improving your customer service and community engagement through interactions and experiences
  • Enhancing the quality of amenities you provide to gain a competitive edge in the market
  • Personalizing the experience for each member by way of memberships, technology, and more

Understand Your Current NPS and What It Means

Before you can improve on anything, you first need to understand what your baseline is, and an NPS for a coworking space is certainly no exception. So, where do you start?

NPS is calculated by asking members: “On a scale of 0-10, how likely are you to recommend our coworking space to a friend or colleague?” Simple, right?

Based on their responses, members are then categorized into three groups:

  1. Promoters (9-10): These are your superfans – the members who love your space and are likely to recommend it to others, fueling the growth of your business.
  2. Passives (7-8): They are satisfied, but not enthusiastic enough to actively promote your space, making them vulnerable to leaving if a better option arises.
  3. Detractors (0-6): These members are dissatisfied. They are at the highest risk for churn and could harm your reputation with negative publicity (word-of-mouth, social media, etc.). Low scores from detractors highlight areas of dissatisfaction – whether poor service, inadequate amenities, or unaddressed concerns – signaling a need for immediate attention. This does however provide opportunities for growth and improvement, but we’ll touch on that more later.

Are you using the right coworking booking software?

Calculating NPS

To calculate your NPS, subtract the percentage of detractors from the percentage of promoters. The score can range from -100 (everyone is a detractor) to +100 (everyone is a promoter).

NPS = % of Promoters – % of Detractors

The rule of thumb says 40 indicates a good NPS, where 60+ is outstanding.

Now, let’s dive into some strategies that, when executed correctly, can significantly boost your NPS score.

#1 Improve Your Customer Service and Community Engagement

Have you ever heard the phrase, “you catch more flies with honey than you do with vinegar?” The adage refers to being kind rather than bitter and rude.

In most cases, customer service can make or break someone’s experience, regardless of the setting. In coworking spaces, good customer service can turn detractors into promoters, and a strong sense of community can keep your members loyal.

Your staff is often the first point of contact when a member needs help, so it’s vital to ensure they are responsive, friendly, thoughtful, and proactive in addressing concerns. Here are some actionable tips to improve and guarantee good customer service every time:

  • Faster Response Times: Implement systems for quick responses to member queries, whether through email, chat, or in-person requests. Even if a solution cannot be immediate, at least responding to the member and acknowledging their needs can go a long way.
  • Personalized Interactions: Get to know your members individually. Address them by name and make note of their preferences – these small gestures make a big difference. A pro tip is to pick something about them that stands out to you and use that to identify and recognize them. This could be a physical attribute, something they said in a conversation that resonated with you, or anything else that you can use to associate with that member.
  • Tackle Pain Points Head-On: Embrace member feedback. Use it to identify common issues and solve them promptly. Whether it’s resolving noise complaints or improving Wi-Fi speed, fast action shows that you’re listening and committed to providing a top-notch experience.

Improving Community Engagement

Building a strong coworking community is essential for creating a vibrant, connected environment that members love. Hosting regular events, such as workshops, social gatherings, and skill-sharing sessions, provides opportunities for members to interact and build relationships.

Networking events allow freelancers, entrepreneurs, and teams to connect, fostering both professional collaboration and personal friendships.

Encouraging collaboration can also be achieved through initiatives like member-led projects or interest-based groups, where individuals can come together to solve challenges or brainstorm new ideas.

By creating spaces – both physical and virtual – for members to engage, share knowledge, and support one another, you not only enhance their coworking experience but also build a loyal community that contributes to the overall success of your space.

#2 Enhance the Quality of Your Amenities and Workspace

A coworking space is more than just a rentable desk and some free Wi-Fi – it’s a productivity-enhancing, collaboration-boosting environment.

High-quality amenities and a comfortable workspace contribute to its reputation for providing a great member experience.

This can have a major impact on your NPS score. When members are not just satisfied, but pleased with the amenities and community within your space, they’re much more apt to refer friends, family, and colleagues to the space. And that’s the ultimate goal, right?

So, if your score is not quite where you want it to be, here are some easy ways to enhance your space, and in turn, enhance your NPS:

  • Ergonomic furniture
  • High-speed internet
  • Comfort and cleanliness
  • Technology integrations
  • Cafe and catering options
  • Workspace options, including outdoor spaces, private call booths, and quiet zones
  • Customizable lighting and temperature control
  • Art and aesthetics

The only way to really know what your members like, want, and need is to ask them. No one expects you to be a mind-reader, so don’t put that kind of pressure on yourself.

Gather member feedback on your amenities to learn what they value most and where improvements can be made.

Your members are the ones interacting with your space on a day-to-day basis, so only they can really provide feedback on how your amenities are serving them.

This also is not a set-and-forget type of business model. As your members’ wants and needs change, so should your amenities. Stay in tune with your members and how your offerings are impacting them.

Furthermore, make sure to have a space that’s accessible for people with disabilities.

#3 Personalize the Coworking Experience

Members are more likely to recommend your space if they feel that it’s designed with them in mind. Personalizing the coworking experience can go a long way in improving your members’ satisfaction.

Personalizing your coworking space doesn’t equate to custom-built offices where every member designs their own space.

While that would be quite the perk, personalization can happen on a small scale too. Let’s take a closer look at some examples:

  • Customized Membership Plans: Offer flexible options, such as pay-as-you-go, part-/full-time memberships, day passes, basic vs. premium memberships, etc. so members can choose what works best for them. Everyone’s reason for coming to a coworking space is different, so having the freedom and flexibility to choose the plan that works best for them shows members you are willing to work with them to meet their needs.
  • Tech Tools: Implement apps (such as a coworking booking platform) that make it easy to book meeting rooms, connect with other members, and manage memberships. Members will appreciate the seamless experience and see you as a modern, high-tech establishment.
  • Member Perks: Surprise your members with thoughtful perks like free coffee, discounts at local cafes or retail stores, or even weekly snacks. These small touches show that you care about their happiness both personally and professionally.
  • Flexible Workspace Options and Layouts: Offer a variety of layouts that allow members to choose the type of environment that suits their working style. This includes open-plan spaces for collaborative work, semi-private booths for focused tasks, and fully private offices for teams or individuals who need more privacy and a quiet work environment.

Leveraging Technology to Personalize the Coworking Experience

The buck doesn’t stop there though – leveraging technology is a powerful way to personalize the coworking experience and streamline operations for members.

We also see many benefits in coworking spaces that leverage technology in the following ways:

  • Space Booking Apps: Apps for booking spaces allow members to easily reserve desks, meeting rooms, or event spaces on-demand, giving them the flexibility to choose the right environment for specific instances. One such software is OfficeRnD Flex with its highly customizable resource booking platform.
  • Membership Management: Member management tools can automate payments, track usage, and provide access to exclusive resources, making the experience seamless and customized for each individual.
  • Coworker Connectivity: Connecting members – through virtual community platforms and social networks or in-person events – fosters collaboration, enabling coworkers to engage, share thoughts, and collaborate on projects.

With integrated technology, coworking spaces can offer a more tailored, convenient, and engaging experience, helping members feel more connected and in control of their workplace needs.

OfficeRnD Flex is a coworking space management software that allows you to automate mundane administrative tasks and offer an unmatched member experience.

Creating a Welcoming and Inclusive Environment

At the end of the day, people just want to be in a place where they feel safe and comfortable, surrounded by people who make them feel good. Creating an inclusive environment that caters to different industries and professionals – from freelancers to startups – will make your space more attractive and welcoming.

Coworking spaces definitely fall under the category of hospitality. By fostering a culture of warmth, attentiveness, and care, staff can make every member feel valued and right at home.

Small touches like friendly greetings, remembering members’ preferences, and offering personalized assistance help build strong connections and enhance the overall experience.

#4 Collect and Act on Feedback

Raising your Net Promoter Score starts with listening – listen to what your members like, don’t like, want, and need to enhance your space and its offerings. Regularly gathering feedback from your members and using that information to make meaningful improvements is your first step to a higher NPS.

But, how exactly should you go about asking for this feedback? We thought you might ask. So, we’ve prepared some tips for gathering information from your members:

  • Surveys: Conduct member surveys after key interactions, like upon completion of onboarding or events, to gauge their satisfaction and identify areas for improvement.
  • One-on-One Interactions: Sometimes, a simple chat with a member can provide valuable insights into their needs and experiences.
  • Suggestion Boxes: Anonymous submissions allow members to provide more honest feedback with no repercussions. This is generally where you will find your most authentic comments.
  • QR Codes: Spread QR codes throughout the space and place them strategically during events for a fun and interactive feedback experience for your members.

Creating Regular Touchpoints

Regular touchpoints, such as quarterly feedback surveys, post-event evaluations, and membership renewal discussions ensure that you are constantly gathering insights that will help drive your business forward.

During our FlexWorld Series 2024 May event, CEO of coworking powerhouse, Firmspace, Kenny Kane, shared his philosophy on collecting feedback saying:

Form authentic relationships and ask for open and honest feedback throughout the membership and at renewal times.

Responding to Negative Feedback

Take criticism and negative feedback as an opportunity to transform a member’s experience. No matter how big or small the complaint, this is your chance to turn a potential detractor into a loyal promoter.

When responding to negative feedback, transparency is key. Acknowledge the concerns promptly, thank members for their input, and offer a clear plan of action on how you will address the issue.

Follow up with updates to show you are committed to making improvements and truly care about their experience.

Implement a Plan of Action

Use the feedback to implement continuous improvement measures by identifying recurring patterns or pain points.

Whether it’s upgrading facilities, improving customer service, or tweaking your event schedule, let members know when changes are made in direct response to their feedback.

This not only boosts satisfaction but also reinforces a culture of listening and adapting, which can significantly increase your NPS and member retention over time.

#5 Member Retention Strategies

Happy members stick around, and loyal members become your promoters. The longer a member stays, the more invested they become in your space, and the more likely they are to recommend it.

Let’s take a look at some key strategies for retaining members:

  • Rewards Programs: Offer incentives like discounts, priority booking, or extra amenities for long-term members.
  • Flexible Membership Options: Give members the ability to scale up or down as their needs change. Flexibility is key to keeping them satisfied.
  • Referral Programs: Encourage your existing members to spread the word by offering rewards for successful referrals.
  • Regular Updates: Regularly updating members on new features, events, and improvements in response to their feedback reinforces their loyalty and trust in your space and shows you are willing to be vulnerable and transparent with them.

In Conclusion

Improving your coworking space’s NPS is not just about hitting a target – it’s about creating a continuously evolving, member-centric experience.

By understanding your current NPS, focusing on customer service, upgrading amenities, personalizing the experience, acting on feedback, and prioritizing member retention, you can transform detractors into promoters and create a thriving community.

Name: Coworking Office Supply Management: 11 Best Practices
Author: asen-stoyanchev
Short cards description: Without a clear supply management strategy, it’s easy for expenses to get out of hand. When it comes to coworking office supply management, avoiding runaway costs can be even trickier.
Post body:
Without a clear supply management strategy, it’s easy for expenses to get out of hand. When it comes to coworking office supply management, avoiding runaway costs can be even trickier.

Because you’re managing supplies to create an experience for your members — rather than simply selling a physical product to customers — it can be more difficult to gauge what you need and how your supply spending translates to higher revenues.

If you’re concerned with how your expenses are looking, or just know that you can better optimize your office supply spending, read on. This article covers best practices for managing coworking office supplies and shows you how you can save money with an effective system.

Quick Summary

  • Track and Manage Supplies: Regularly track supplies to reduce costs, avoid overstocking, and prevent shortages. Bulk purchasing for high-use items and controlled access to supply rooms can optimize usage and prevent waste.
  • Sustainability and Eco-Friendly Practices: Promote: sustainable practices by using eco-friendly products, minimizing waste, and educating members on responsible supply use. This can enhance your coworking space’s reputation among environmentally conscious members.
  • Leverage Technology for Efficiency: Use technology and coworking management software for supply tracking, automating reorders, and integrating with accounting tools to streamline operations and boost cost savings.

Why Tracking Supplies Is Crucial in Coworking Spaces

Effective coworking space management is more than just keeping shelves stocked and workspaces comfortable. It’s a strategic approach to make your space efficient — and to ensure you’re offering the full coworking space experience to members.

Here’s what you stand to gain from tracking and managing your office supplies:

Reduces Expenses

Regular tracking helps identify patterns of overuse or waste. It allows you to fine-tune your ordering practices and save money.

That’s because high-use items can be ordered in bulk. And emergency understock situations can be avoided to save on last-minute purchases, which are often more expensive.

Accurate tracking also aids in predicting future needs, keeping supply levels optimal. Additionally, maintaining a detailed record of supplies on hand can reduce losses due to misplacement or misuse.

For example, if the printer ink is often running out, you might find that members are using it to produce their own projects.

Are you using the right booking platform for your coworking space.

Boosts Sustainability

The beauty of tracking your supplies to minimize waste is that you boost sustainability in the process. This environmental focus can be seen as an amenity of your coworking space.

Tracking supplies can reveal that certain items are rarely used and don’t need to be ordered as often. It guides decisions on paperless initiatives, reducing single-use items, or choosing environmentally friendly products.

Supporting eco-friendly initiatives not only helps the environment, but it also boosts the space’s reputation among eco-conscious members.

Increases Member Satisfaction

The other reason to track supplies is so that necessary ones are always available. That allows your members to work without disruption or hassle.

A well-managed supply system contributes to a tidy, organized, and professional atmosphere. It improves the overall member experience.

Imagine a member running out of staples or printer paper while preparing for a crucial presentation. Regular tracking prevents such situations.

11 Best Practices for Coworking Office Supply Management

So what can you do to better manage your coworking supplies?

These eleven tips are specifically tailored for owners and managers of coworking spaces. With these best practices in hand, you can dial in your systems on supplies.

Conduct Regular Supply Audits

First, it’s essential to conduct regular audits of your coworking space supplies. These periodic checks should be scheduled routinely. They’ll make sure everything is accounted for.

This practice helps you avoid the following:

  • Discrepancies
  • Shortages
  • Overstocking

It helps you track usage, predict needs, and adjust your ordering accordingly. Audits are also a chance to dispose of outdated or unneeded items to reduce clutter.

Pro tip: rotating who’s responsible for conducting the audit allows your team to have a broader perspective on managing supplies. You should also have staff perform random spot checks on supplies to maintain optimal levels.

Implement Controlled Access Systems

Using controlled access systems is a security practice to make sure only authorized individuals are in certain zones. It can greatly reduce the theft, misuse, and disorganization of supplies.

Choose a staff member, for example, the community manager to be the supply coordinator. They will manage the supply room and watch how supplies are distributed. This person makes sure that supplies are used appropriately and provides a sense of accountability to members.

A coworking management solution such as OfficeRnD Flex integrates with KISI to provide seamless access control. 

A keypad or lock system could restrict access to the supply room. Provide only a select group of employees with the code or key to control access.

Or, the time for accessing the supply room could be reserved for hours when staff are present. Either way, keep an access log of who comes in and when. That can help identify patterns or issues later.

Organize Supplies Efficiently

Keeping supplies organized makes sure they’re accessible and well-maintained. An organized supply room saves time for members, but it also reduces waste. Items are less likely to be lost or overlooked.

Using these practices makes it easier and faster to manage supplies. This helps make coworking spaces more productive.

Start by grouping similar items, then clearly label shelves. Color coding is a great way to differentiate supplies. The goal is for members to easily find what they need without having to rummage through disorganized piles.

Place frequently used items — such as paper, pens, and coffee — at eye level for quick access. Less-used items can be stored higher up or in less accessible areas.

Create a clear layout and encourage members to return supplies to the right location when they’re done. Have staff make their rounds and tidy up the supply area regularly.

Is your space dog-friendly? Don’t forget to check on the canine supplies!

Encourage Responsible Use of Supplies

To be truly effective, the members of your flex or coworking space have to be on board with your best practices.

Encourage them to minimize waste and use supplies responsibly. Implement clear guidelines and signage throughout the workspace. Signs could include tips on printing, such as how to select double-sided printing or how to use devices to make certain print jobs obsolete.

Raising awareness of the impact of everyday decisions can be helpful to illustrate the point. For example, a sign could include a stat on how much paper is saved through digital note-taking. Digital platforms or apps can also send regular reminders and tips.

Organize monthly challenges to make this whole process fun and less formal. Rewards could be given to whoever meets a supply use goal, or those who show the most improvement.

Maintain a Detailed Supply Log

A supply log is crucial for effective supply management. It tracks all supplies and current stock levels. It should include a reorder level — the point at which more should be ordered — and how much to typically order.

The longer you keep these supply logs, the more valuable they’ll become. They aid in budget planning and predicting future needs. You can look back at them and better understand problem areas and inefficiencies.

Analyze these logs to determine which supplies are the best candidates for bulk purchasing. Inversely, you’ll be able to see which supplies are slow-moving or even obsolete.

Use Technology for Expense Tracking and Reporting

As with just about anything, the right technology for supply management can make a world of difference. The goal is to streamline your financial data and make strategic decisions to improve your efficiency.

Tracking your expenses via Excel or Google Sheets is an excellent starting point. But as your coworking space evolves, you’ll probably want more dedicated financial software solutions such as QuickBooks.

OfficeRnD Flex is a coworking management software that integrates with Quickbooks and allows you to automate billing and accounting. See how.

Technology should also be used to generate detailed reports, such as monthly expense summaries and budget vs. actual spending.

These reports help you to do the following:

  • Analyze patterns
  • Identify cost-saving opportunities
  • And adhere to your budget

A fairly recent breakthrough is mobile expense tracking. Using mobile apps, staff update expense records on the go.

For example, if staff have to purchase supplies while outside the office, they can snap a photo of the receipt and input the details immediately into the system.

That saves on the stress of maintaining receipts and remembering to report expenses.

Implement a Reorder Point System

Effective reordering is the mechanism for always having adequate stock on hand. You need a specific strategy, known as a reorder point system, to maintain optimal supply levels and ensure a smooth ordering workflow.

Your supply log should already have minimum stock levels for each item. Automate these reorder points using supply management software to alert you when stock levels fall below that threshold. It’s a proactive approach to avoid running out of essential supplies and overspending on last-minute orders.

For important items, put a buffer in your stock to protect yourself if demand unexpectedly increases.

Reviewing your supply logs will help you know how to make seasonal adjustments to your reorder points. For example, if there are always extra runs on supplies around tax time, you can be prepared for it.

Analyze Usage Trends

Your financial software should have built-in data analytics tools that can help you detect trends in your supply logs.

By understanding peak usage times, you can optimize the ordering schedule of your coworking space to align with demand.

For example, if printer paper use spikes at the beginning of each month, you can plan larger orders in preparation for that.

Or, if flexible work schedules mean fewer workers are in your space on Mondays and Fridays, you can adjust accordingly.

It’s also important to maintain a project calendar. Keep in touch with members about upcoming projects and any special needs that will be important to their work.

Promote Eco-friendly Practices

As mentioned earlier, incorporating sustainable practices is a key way to differentiate yourself and gain loyalty from your members. Your coworking space can significantly reduce its carbon footprint, achieve environmental goals, and attract eco-conscious members.

Start by choosing sustainable and earth-friendly office supplies. Some examples include recycled paper, biodegradable pens, and reusable coffee cups.

Add reusable supplies to common disposable items, like refillable pens and notebooks.

As for recycling, it’s not just paper and plastic. Electronics and digital accessories can often be recycled as well. Ask nearby retailers, manufacturers, or recycling operations about your local options.

Energy-efficient office equipment, such as LED lights and low-power-consumption devices, reduce environmental impact. And seeking out suppliers with a similar focus on sustainability is a way to broaden your environmental advocacy.

Educate Members

An investment in educating your members goes a long way.

New members should have an onboarding process that introduces them to the coworking space’s supply management approach. Emails or online resources can outline best practices for using supplies efficiently. Visual reminders near supply stations can remind people about the benefits of responsible use.

The objective is to create a culture that holds itself accountable and strives to innovate, cutting costs and negative impacts.

You can also create surveys or suggestion boxes to gather input from members on how to improve supply management and address any concerns.

Offer Premium Supplies as Upsells

Premium supplies provide an opportunity to enhance the member experience while bringing in additional revenue.

Provide basic supplies for free to meet everyday needs. But introduce premium options for an additional fee.

Some options for premium supplies are:

  • High-quality stationery
  • Personalized notebooks
  • Branded pens
  • Ergonomic accessories (check out our recommended coworking space furniture here)

Personalization services, such as custom-engraved pens or notebooks, can add a touch of exclusivity and professionalism. Offer these premium items as part of a subscription package, where members get a special selection of expensive supplies each month.

You can also run special promotions to highlight these upsell options. You can introduce seasonal offers, such as holiday-themed stationery.

Attracting members who seek customized supplies diversifies your revenue stream while catering to a different demographic of members.

Moving forward, you can optimize your office space even further with robust enough coworking software. All in all, you can easily keep members happy and automate the rest.

Name: Scaling Your Coworking Business: Strategies For Multi-Location Management
Author: asen-stoyanchev
Short cards description: Coworking has moved from a niche option for freelancers to a core part of how companies handle office space. The market keeps growing , and for operators running one full space, the question of a second, third, or tenth location is a real one.
Post body:
Coworking has moved from a niche option for freelancers to a core part of how companies handle office space. The market keeps growing, and for operators running one full space, the question of a second, third, or tenth location is a real one.

Multi-location coworking management is the practice of running two or more coworking spaces under one brand and operating system, keeping the member experience consistent while adapting each site to its local market.

The numbers back the opportunity. The U.S. coworking market passed 9,100 active locations in early 2026, and globally the sector is estimated at roughly $30 billion in 2026, projected to reach about $53 billion by 2030. Flex still makes up a small slice of total office inventory, around 2% in the US, which leaves room for operators who run tight, well-managed spaces.

But scaling isn’t just expansion. Adding locations tests whether your model works when you’re not in the room, and whether your systems hold up across sites you can’t personally oversee every day.

Expanding your coworking brand takes careful planning, a repeatable operating model, and a clear read on what makes each space work. Master multi-location management and you’re building something that lasts.

Quick Summary

Five strategies for scaling and managing multiple coworking locations:

  • Assess readiness for expansion: Confirm high occupancy, strong community engagement, and financial stability before you expand. Run a feasibility study, including market research and risk assessment, for each new location.
  • Build a repeatable business model: Standardize operations, keep branding and member experience consistent, and use a pricing structure flexible enough to fit regional markets.
  • Build a strong management team: Hire and train local managers with leadership and people skills, and balance central strategic control with local day-to-day autonomy.
  • Use the right technology: Run multi-location management software and a CRM from one dashboard for cleaner operations, member tracking, and reporting.
  • Tailor community and marketing: Engage each local community with events and partnerships while keeping brand messaging consistent across sites.

Is your coworking space ready to expand?

Scaling a coworking business is exciting, but before you commit, check whether your current operation is actually ready.

A solid growth strategy starts with an honest look at your existing space: is the foundation strong, and is the timing right?

Key indicators for expansion

Signs that your coworking space is ready to scale:

Consistently high occupancy rates: One of the clearest signals is consistently high occupancy rates. If your space runs at or near full capacity most of the time, demand is strong and you’re using the space well. High occupancy lifts revenue and builds an active community, both of which you need to sustain multiple locations.

If you can’t keep up with demand, staying put can hurt you.

When paying members can’t get the spaces they want, when they want them, they’ll look elsewhere. If occupancy stays high and new inquiries keep coming, it’s probably time to explore growth.

Strong community engagement: A healthy community is what makes a coworking space work. If members show up to events, collaborate, and stick with your brand, your community-building is paying off.

A strong community at your flagship gives you something to replicate. Behind that community is a solid team.

Local managers shape your community more than almost anything else. A dedicated, engaged, goal-oriented team makes expansion feel achievable. Look at your team and decide whether you can lean on them for the next location.

Financial stability and profitability: Before you consider expanding, your current operation should be stable and profitable.

That means covering operational costs at your existing space and generating enough profit to reinvest in a second one. A solid financial footing means you can support new locations without putting the original at risk.

Conducting a feasibility study

Even with the signs pointing to readiness, run a full feasibility study before you expand. It helps you judge the odds for a new location and cut down on risk.

Steps to conduct a feasibility study:

  1. Market research in potential new locations: Start with demand for flexible workspace in the area you’re considering. Look at demographic trends, the local business ecosystem, and economic conditions. Understanding what potential members in that area want helps you tailor your offering and pick sites with the most room to grow.
  2. Competitive analysis: Assess the coworking spaces and other flexible workspace options already in your target area. Find gaps your brand could fill, and weigh competitors’ strengths and weaknesses. This tells you how to position a new location so it stands out.
  3. Risk assessment: Every expansion carries risk. Identify and weigh it early. Consider economic downturns, changes in local regulations, or shifts in demand. Build in ways to manage that risk, such as diversifying your member base or offering flexible membership options that adapt to market changes.

Building a repeatable business model

A repeatable business model keeps operations, brand, and member experience consistent as you add locations.

That means standardizing operations, giving members a consistent experience, and setting a pricing structure that stays uniform in principle but flexes by market.

You don’t need cookie-cutter spaces. Whether you’re opening one more location or building an entire coworking network, the underlying model should stay the same.

Location names, branding, color schemes, and physical appearance can all vary between your spaces, but the fundamental groundwork needs to be the same.

Hotel chains show how this works. Marriott runs over 30 brands, from Moxy Hotels to The Ritz-Carlton.

Each brand has its own name, look, and value proposition, but all run on Marriott’s operating practices, which keeps the experience consistent.

The point of a repeatable business model is a strong base for growth.

It makes multiple locations easier to manage and gives members a consistent experience, which makes your brand more resilient as you expand.

Standardizing operations and processes

Standard procedures keep every location running smoothly and give members the same experience wherever they are. They tidy up daily operations and set the base for scaling, so managing several sites at the same standard gets easier.

Consider the following:

  • Create operation manuals and SOPs: Document your core processes. Write detailed operation manuals and Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) covering daily tasks, staff responsibilities, emergency protocols, and reporting. These become the reference for staff at every location, so your spaces run consistently regardless of where they are.
  • Keep branding and member experience consistent: Your brand connects all your locations. Whether a member walks into your flagship or a new site, they should recognize the same atmosphere, values, and experience. Even without the exact same paint color, members should sense they’re inside the same brand.

Most coworking spaces standardize branding elements: logos, color schemes, interior design, furniture, and even office supplies, to create a cohesive identity. A consistent brand image builds loyalty and keeps members satisfied.

You can stay on brand while honoring what’s distinct about each space through your tone, communication, and member experience. From customer service to the events and amenities you offer, that consistency builds trust and keeps members with you as you grow.

Setting a pricing structure that scales

As you expand to multiple locations, a pricing structure that scales keeps you profitable and attracts a range of members.

A good pricing model is flexible enough to meet different market demands while staying consistent across all locations.

Flexible membership options

A one-size-fits-all model rarely works across locations. A range of membership options lets you attract a diverse base and adapt to demand at each site.

Common membership options include:

  • Hot desking
  • Day passes
  • Dedicated desks
  • Private offices
  • Weekend coworking
  • Community/virtual office
  • Team/corporate plans

You might also consider offering a free trial.

Regional pricing adjustments

Different markets have different price sensitivities, so adjust your pricing to local economic conditions and competitor rates.

During your market research, find out what members in each region are willing to pay and set prices accordingly.

This keeps your offering competitive and accessible while getting the most revenue out of each location.

Choosing the right locations

Location choice is one of the biggest factors in whether a new site works. Each one depends on a careful read of what drives demand and member satisfaction.

From understanding the local market to convenience and access, picking the right location takes both strategic thinking and detailed research.

Factors to consider when selecting new locations

There are several factors when deciding your next location, but the two biggest questions are: “Can this market sustain this type of business, and will there be demand for it?” and “How easy is it for potential members to get here?”

Let’s get into it.

Demographic analysis and target markets

The demographic profile of a location shapes its potential. Analyze the local population to identify target markets, such as freelancers, startups, or remote workers.

Consider age, income, education, and industry presence. These drive the volume of demand.

They also tell you whether a market can sustain a coworking business and help shape your value proposition and offering.

For example, an urban setting with young, tech-focused professionals might call for a modern space with strong tech, while a suburban demographic may prefer a community-focused environment with collaborative areas and more social events.

Understanding your target market lets you tailor the space to local demand and attract the right members. Some operators use coworking consulting services for help with that.

Accessibility and transport links

Convenience and access matter for attracting and keeping members. How often do you skip going somewhere just because you’re not sure about parking?

Check the transport infrastructure around potential sites, including proximity to public transit and major roads, to judge whether it’s a good spot.

Beyond public transport, locations with ample parking draw members who prioritize convenience. Parking, especially free parking where feasible, is a strong draw.

Proximity to business hubs and amenities

A location near business districts, retail centers, or universities adds real appeal.

Being close to shops, cafes, restaurants, and gyms gives members everything they need within walking distance. Proximity to business hubs also creates networking and collaboration opportunities, which are key selling points.

Strategies for site selection

Site selection drives your occupancy rates and the success of your expansion.

It can push the business forward or set it back. Consider these strategies when choosing a site:

  1. Use real estate partnerships: Relationships with real estate professionals and developers give you an edge. They can point you to emerging neighborhoods, upcoming developments, and prime commercial properties. They can also help negotiate lease terms and find opportunities that fit your goals, so you make informed decisions and secure sites positioned for growth.
  2. Use data analytics for site selection: Data helps you choose well. Use analytics to assess potential sites on foot traffic, competition density, and local economic indicators. Geographic Information Systems (GIS) and similar tools map demographic trends, transport patterns, and commercial activity, helping you find sites with the most potential and cut down on risk.
  3. Pilot with a pop-up coworking space: Before committing to a long-term lease, test the market with a temporary or pop-up space. You’ll gauge local demand, gather feedback, and refine your offering with real-world input. Pop-ups can go in vacant commercial properties or shared spaces with flexible terms.

The pop-up approach has a long track record. Industrious, one of the largest US operators, has run pop-up spaces to test new formats and locations. Its asset-light model, where it operates space in a profit-sharing agreement with the property owner, helped it grow fast enough that in January 2025 CBRE acquired full ownership at a valuation of roughly $800 million.

Austin-based coworking startup Reset took a lighter approach, partnering with local restaurants and renting their spaces during off-hours. The restaurants earn income during slow times, and Reset builds awareness for its brand.

Piloting this way lets you validate a location, build awareness, and make informed decisions before committing to a permanent site.

Building a strong management team

As you add locations, a strong management team keeps operations consistent, protects your culture, and drives results across every site.

Good leadership at every level is how you manage the complexity of multi-location operations and keep each space, old and new, running well.

Why leadership matters in multi-location management

Strong leadership carries any multi-location business. A study by Zenger Folkman, reported in Forbes, found that the worst-ranked leaders were tied to $1.2M in losses, while the best contributed nearly $4.5M in gains.

In coworking, where member experience and community engagement carry the business, you need managers who can lead with vision and adapt on the fly.

Community managers are often the face of your brand, interacting with members daily, solving problems, and building an inclusive community.

How well they lead directly affects member satisfaction, retention, and the success of each location.

Hiring and training local managers

When hiring local managers, look for a mix of operational know-how and strong people skills.

Prioritize candidates with experience in hospitality or customer service, a knack for building relationships, and proven leadership.

Look for adaptability and problem-solving, since managing a coworking space means handling a lot of moving parts.

Providing ongoing training and support

Even strong managers need ongoing training and support. Invest in regular programs covering operational processes and best practices, plus leadership development, conflict resolution, and community engagement.

Provide workshops, mentorship from more experienced managers, and management tools that cut down on busywork.

Continuous support and development keep community managers aligned with your goals and ready for the challenges of the role, all while building the kind of inclusive environment that keeps members happy.

Centralized vs. decentralized management

Centralized and decentralized approaches determine where decisions get made.

A centralized approach concentrates decision-making at the top, usually at headquarters or a core leadership team.

In this model, key decisions on operations, policies, procedures, branding, and strategy come from a central authority, which keeps things consistent across locations.

The downside: it can slow things down locally, stopping managers from responding quickly to specific needs or opportunities.

A decentralized approach gives local managers more autonomy to make decisions that fit their location.

Central leadership still sets overall strategy and core guidelines, but day-to-day operations, problem-solving, and some strategic calls happen closer to the action.

That flexibility means faster response to local demand and more room to try new things at each space. Without oversight, though, it can create inconsistencies in brand experience and operations across locations.

Finding the right balance

Each style has trade-offs. Successful multi-location management usually lands between the two.

Centralize the core: branding, financial management, and overall strategy. Decentralize day-to-day operations and community engagement so local managers can tailor their efforts to their members.

That balance gives you consistency and flexibility, and it lets your team drive results at every location.

Multi-location management technology

As you expand, running multiple locations gets more complex. The right technology keeps operations clean, improves communication, and gives members a consistent experience across every site.

Centralized management software, a platform that runs your business functions from one dashboard, is how you oversee day-to-day operations across sites.

These platforms let you handle core tasks from a single interface. That keeps things consistent across sites, cuts down on admin, and gives you real-time visibility into each location’s performance.

Key features of centralized management software include:

  • Billing
  • Member management
  • Resource allocation
  • Space utilization
  • Reporting and analytics
  • Visitor check-ins
  • Communications

Customer relationship management (CRM) systems

A CRM, software that tracks member interactions, manages leads, and personalizes communication across locations, is central to managing relationships with members and prospects.

With a CRM, you keep a detailed history of each member’s preferences, billing, and feedback, which helps you deliver a personalized experience and build loyalty.

Tools like HubSpot, Salesforce, or Zoho CRM can be set up for a coworking business, helping you manage and grow your community.

Key functions of a CRM include:

  • Member tracking
  • Lead management
  • Database communication
  • Reporting and analytics

Communication and collaboration

Clear communication is part of the foundation for managing multiple locations.

In a business that’s complex and geographically spread out, consistent communication keeps day-to-day operations smooth and the member experience unified.

Why it matters:

  • Consistency across locations: Keeps every site on the same standards, policies, and procedures, so the brand experience stays consistent.
  • Faster decisions: Keeps the right people in the loop so decisions get made quickly and with better information.
  • Better collaboration: Connects teams at different locations, so they share what’s working.
  • Faster problem-solving: Lets issues get spotted and resolved quickly as information moves between sites.
  • Employee engagement: Keeps staff connected wherever they work, which helps job satisfaction and retention.

Virtual meeting platforms

With teams across locations, virtual meetings become necessary. Zoom, Google Meet, or Microsoft Teams enable face-to-face contact without travel, keeping headquarters and local managers connected.

Regular virtual meetings keep things transparent, share updates, and surface challenges early, so every location stays well managed.

Marketing and community building across locations

Scaling well means marketing your brand and building an engaged community across every location, not just running operations.

A unified marketing strategy paired with local community engagement keeps your brand consistent while fitting the character of each location.

Unified marketing strategies

Consistency runs through multi-location management: consistency in experience, in offerings, and in branding and messaging.

Usually that means the same logos, color schemes, and brand voice across all communications.

On your website, social media, or printed materials, a clear, consistent message builds trust and recognition, so potential members understand what you offer no matter where they are.

A brand guideline document helps keep every location on the same standards.

That said, with a network approach like Australian coworking group YoCo, logos and color schemes can vary.

Each YoCo space is its own entity operating on shared foundations. Even with a different color on the wall, members should feel the essence of your brand at any location.

Social media and digital marketing

Social media and digital marketing help promote your spaces across locations.

Show up on Instagram, Facebook (Meta), LinkedIn, and X to share content about your spaces, member success stories, and events.

Paid ads can target specific regions, helping you reach potential members in each area.

You might also create location-specific accounts or pages that fit the local community while staying inside your overall brand strategy.

Local community engagement

Community is what makes a coworking space. Getting members to interact leads to stronger connections and better collaboration.

Here are some of the best ways to build it.

Hosting local events and networking

Local events are one of the best ways to build community across your spaces. Regular networking events, workshops, and social gatherings connect members and create a sense of belonging.

Tailor events to the local community, whether that’s industry meetups, skill-sharing sessions, or wellness activities.

Local events lift member engagement and attract new members by showing off the collaborative environment your space offers.

You can add local flavor too, featuring food, drink, activities, and services from local vendors.

Joint events with local businesses and organizations strengthen your presence in the community and add value for members.

Partnering with local businesses and organizations

Beyond using local vendors at events, consider cross-promotion with them.

Team up with nearby cafes, gyms, or shops for member discounts. They promote your space to grow your membership, and members get discounts to businesses they already like.

These partnerships introduce new audiences to both sides.

Local chambers of commerce and business associations widen your network and open more avenues for collaboration. There’s real potential here for attracting new members.

Monitoring performance and growth

As you expand into multiple locations, monitoring performance becomes central to long-term success.

Tracking Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) shows the health of each location, surfaces trends, and informs decisions.

Without consistent monitoring, it’s hard to hold service and profitability steady across every site.

KPIs for multi-location management include:

  • Occupancy rates: A fundamental KPI, showing how much of your available space is in use. High rates signal strong demand and efficient use; low rates may point to a need for marketing or pricing changes. Tracking this across locations shows which sites perform and which need attention.
  • Revenue per location: Shows the financial performance of each site. It helps you assess profitability, understand revenue streams, and compare locations. It also flags underperforming spaces and whether pricing, marketing, or services need adjusting. Read more about the different types of coworking revenue here.
  • Member satisfaction and retention: Satisfaction drives retention and a loyal community. Surveys, feedback forms, and direct conversations tell you how members feel and let you address concerns fast. Retention rate, the share of members who stay over time, reflects satisfaction directly. High retention points to a strong community and a compelling offer; low retention signals a need for improvement in services, community engagement, or support.

Regular performance reviews and reporting

Regular reviews and reporting keep you on top of coworking KPIs and on track.

Periodic reviews, monthly, quarterly, or annually, help you spot trends, benchmark locations against each other, and set goals.

Detailed KPI reports give you a full picture of the business and support decisions based on evidence rather than guesswork.

Putting the data to use

Basing strategy on real performance metrics rather than assumptions is a strong approach. With data, you can:

  • Spot growth opportunities: Data shows which locations are thriving and why, so you can copy those tactics elsewhere.
  • Improve operations: A clearer read on the business helps you tighten operations, cut costs, and run more efficiently across locations.
  • Adapt to change: Coworking shifts fast. Reviewing performance data lets you respond quickly to market changes, member needs, or competitive moves.
  • Improve member experience: Understanding what drives satisfaction and retention lets you tailor services and community activities to what members actually want.

In conclusion

Managing multiple coworking locations takes a strategic approach that balances operational consistency with local community engagement.

From assessing readiness and choosing locations to building a management team, using the right technology, and tracking performance, each piece plays a real role in the success of your business.

Thriving across locations comes down to your ability to adapt, improve, and use the right tools to keep things running.

Follow the strategies here and your expansion will be well planned, your brand consistent, and your operations clean across every location.
