Regular Check-ins

Consistent virtual or in-person check-ins can help ensure employees feel supported and connected. Regular one-on-ones are crucial for effective communication and collaboration in a hybrid workplace.

They can take various forms, such as daily stand-up meetings, weekly one-on-ones, or weekly team meetings.

Check-ins should ensure that all team members are on the same page. You’ll want to address any challenges and celebrate successes together.

Regular check-ins also foster a culture of transparency and accountability. This helps to build trust within the team. They allow employees to voice concerns, seek feedback, and stay updated on company goals and priorities.

Check-ins are a great way for managers to track progress and provide support. Managers can then use this information to address potential issues. This might include problems related to workload imbalances or personal conflicts.

Check-ins may also help remote workers to overcome feelings of isolation. Check-ins are a great way to keep them connected to the broader team and company culture.

Studies have shown that remote working can worsen the symptoms of burnout for some workers. So, it’s important to give your employees the support they need. This is particularly true when they’re not working from the office.

Regular check-ins need a structured approach. You need to use a clear agenda and follow-up actions to ensure that meetings are productive and valuable for everyone.

Digital tools, such as video conferencing and collaborative platforms, can be useful here. They enhance the effectiveness of remote interactions, making sure everyone is on the same page.​

Advanced Collaboration Tools

We always recommend tools like Slack and Microsoft Teams. Today’s conference room technology can enable real-time communication and project management across different locations and time zones. Plus, many smart space solutions can help you optimize space, which could impact collaboration.

These platforms offer a range of features. The most useful include real-time messaging, video calling, file sharing, and task management.

These all streamline workflows and ensure everyone is on the same page.

These tools will reduce friction in your hybrid workplace. This will enhance team members’ ability to collaborate.

And, if you use OfficeRnD Workplace, you can integrate these tools into your existing workflows.

Plus, advanced collaboration tools can provide analytics and insights into team performance. This allows managers to identify areas for improvement and celebrate achievements.

These tools support asynchronous communication, allowing team members to contribute at their convenience. This is particularly beneficial for global teams.

Regular training on these tools will be necessary. It will ensure that all employees can use their features, maximizing their benefits for you​.

Clear Communication Guidelines

Clear communication guidelines are critical in a hybrid workplace. They ensure everyone remains aligned and informed.

The guidelines should outline the preferred channels for different types of communication. They might recommend email for formal updates and chat tools for quick questions. You can also use video conferencing for meetings.

Top-notch communication helps prevent misunderstandings. This means everyone has all the important information they need.

It also sets expectations for response times. This can help manage workload and reduce employee stress. It’s important to establish norms for virtual meetings. Create clear agendas and seek participation from all team members.

You should review and update communication guidelines based on feedback. Taking evolving needs into account can help maintain these guidelines’ effectiveness.

A culture of open communication will build trust within your hybrid teams. Training on effective communication practices can further support these efforts. It will ensure that all employees can engage with each other in a productive way​​.

According to a Project.co study, 30% of workers think it’s become more difficult to communicate at work recently. So, proper communication protocols have never been more important.

Dedicated Workspaces

Hybrid employees should have dedicated at-home workspaces. They allow workers to maintain their productivity and work-life balance in a hybrid environment.

They face fewer distractions and can draw clear boundaries between their work and personal lives. This makes for a productive, professional atmosphere.

You can support this by providing guidelines on setting up an ergonomic and efficient home office. This might include, say, tips on lighting, furniture, and organization.

Stipends or resources for home office equipment are also useful. They can enhance employees’ ability to create a comfortable and effective workspace.

Check in with employees to ensure their home office setups meet their needs. Try to help identify any issues they might face.

Encouraging breaks and setting clear expectations for work hours can further support employees. These measures allow workers to maintain a clear distinction between their work and home lives.

This will go a long way towards preventing burnout.

Dedicated workspaces aren’t always possible in physical offices. OfficeRnD Workplace’s booking system for desks and meeting rooms can make this easier.

The software will make flexible desk arrangements straightforward for your employees.

Team-Building Activities

Team-building activities are essential for fostering strong relationships and community. They can play a very important role within a hybrid workplace.

Team-building activities can include things like virtual games and online escape rooms. You could also opt for in-person retreats and collaborative projects.

The goal is to create opportunities for team members to connect on a personal level. This helps them to build mutual trust and collaborate well.

Effective team-building activities should be inclusive and enjoyable for all participants. They should cater to diverse interests and preferences.

Using employee feedback about their interests can help tailor the activities to be engaging and meaningful.

You should also integrate team-building into regular work routines. You can do this by starting meetings with icebreakers or scheduling monthly virtual social events. This can strengthen teams’ sense of connection.

Health and Wellness Programs

Health and wellness programs help to support hybrid employees‘ physical and mental well-being. They can include virtual fitness classes, mental health resources, and counseling services.

Wellness helps employees to manage stress, stay healthy, and maintain a positive work-life balance. Wellness programs can also reduce burnout and improve job satisfaction. This leads to higher productivity and engagement.

Flexible options for wellness activities include on-demand fitness videos and mindfulness apps. These can accommodate different schedules and preferences.

Plus, you can encourage participation through incentives and regular communication about resources.

You could also consider wellness webinars and workshops. These can cover topics like nutrition, stress management, and ergonomics.

Performance Metrics

Clear performance metrics are essential in a hybrid workplace. They should focus on outcomes and results, rather than hours worked. This will ensure you’re judging your employees by their contributions and achievements.

Key performance indicators (KPIs) are always useful. They might include project completion rates, quality of work, and client satisfaction. They will allow you to give your employees valuable feedback.

Performance metrics also allow managers to recognize and reward high performers. This can boost morale and motivation.

Quantitative and qualitative metrics provide a comprehensive view of performance. They consider factors like teamwork, creativity, and problem-solving.

Meaningful KPIs and performance metrics will allow you to drive continuous improvement. This ensures that all employees contribute to the organization’s success.

Professional Development

Professional development is key to maintaining a productive hybrid workforce. Consider offering online courses, webinars, workshops, and access to industry conferences.

Continuous learning helps employees stay current on industry trends. It also means they develop new skills and advance their careers.

Companies that invest in professional development tend to have happier, longer-lasting employees. When workers feel valued and supported in their growth, they stick around.

Seek your employees’ input on areas of improvement when making their development plans. This allows you to tailor opportunities to their specific career goals. It also makes their own interests part of the process.

Name: The Art Of Upselling For Increasing Coworking Space Revenue
Author: asen-stoyanchev
Short cards description: The coworking industry has truly revolutionized the traditional office setup, offering flexibility, community, and a vibrant working environment.
Post body:
The coworking industry has truly revolutionized the traditional office setup, offering flexibility, community, and a vibrant working environment.

In a recent study, 89% of coworking space members said they’re happier than they were before joining a coworking community and 83% reported being less lonely. This tells a great story; a true testament to the value prop of a coworking space.

As this up-and-coming industry drives forward though, operators are constantly seeking ways to maximize revenue.

While net new members are great for some metrics, what really makes a coworking company profitable is their current members. Once you have a dedicated and loyal customer base who trusts you, you can further enhance their experience by upselling.

Quick Summary

  • Understand your members and the community they’re looking for and tailor your premium offerings accordingly
  • Start slow – Create basic packages to grow and expand upon as your business flourishes
  • Offer premium services that are unique to your space or location. Don’t forget to target the wants and needs of your members
  • Track and measure your upselling efforts and adjust accordingly

Understanding the Concept of Upselling in Coworking Spaces

Upselling is a true art when done with your customers’ best interest in mind. It involves encouraging customers to purchase additional services or higher-end products than what they originally intended.

Now, don’t get this confused with cross-selling. Cross-selling refers to the promotion of additional products and services to accelerate your sales pipeline.

While they both increase the ticket price, upselling ensures the customer receives a bigger, and often better, version of their intended purchase, where cross-selling promotes the purchase of additional line items. Upselling gives the impression that you’re looking out for your buyer, while cross-selling can come across too “salesy.”

The coworking industry is all about community and building relationships. Upselling to your existing members is one of the best ways to foster your relationships, while also increasing your bottom line. It doesn’t have to come across as pushy or intrusive.

When done strategically, upselling will show the customer you’re looking out for them. It becomes apparent that you want them to receive the best bang for their buck and really truly benefit from their investment with you.

Learn how to upsell by incorporating childcare into your space.

How to Upsell Effectively: Knowing Your Clients

The cornerstone of any successful upselling strategy is a thorough understanding of your clients. This involves more than just knowing their names and companies; it requires a deep dive into their behaviors, preferences, and pain points.

We find it helpful to engage with your clients regularly through surveys, feedback sessions, and informal conversations. We also suggest learning about their business challenges, their day-to-day needs, and what they value most in your coworking space.

By truly understanding your clients, you can tailor your offerings to meet their specific needs, making your upsell proposals more relevant and appealing.

An example – let’s say that you learn that the majority of your target audience prefer working at night. Then, you can create special memberships that allow 24/7 access to your space.

And by the way, if you want to gauge how profitable your space truly is, pay attention to your Revenue per Available Desk (RevPad).

The Importance of Client Data and Feedback

Client data and feedback are invaluable assets in refining your upselling strategies. We highly recommend you utilize a robust member management system to collect and analyze data on how clients use your space and services.

You’ll also want to look at your analytics and track metrics like usage patterns and service utilization. This data helps identify trends and opportunities for upselling.

OfficeRnD Flex is a customizable coworking management platform that can help you do all that and much more.

Segmentation and Identifying High-Potential Clients for Upselling

Not all clients have the same potential for upselling. Segmentation allows you to categorize your clients based on specific criteria such as usage frequency, service preferences, and business size.

By segmenting your client base, you can identify high-potential clients who are more likely to benefit from and be willing to invest in higher-priced services and packages.

Personalized Marketing Approaches

Personalization is key to effective upselling. Generic marketing messages are easy to ignore, but personalized approaches can capture your client’s attention and interest. Using the client data and segmentation insights you’ve gathered, you’ll be able to craft personalized marketing messages that resonate with each client group.

The goal is to make each client feel valued and understood, showing them how your more expensive offerings can meet their unique needs and enhance their coworking experience.

Start Upselling: Enhance Basic Membership Packages

Enhancing your basic membership packages is a great starting point for upselling. Incorporating value-added services makes the basic package more appealing.

This could include:

  • Increased Internet Speed: Offering faster internet can be a simple yet highly appealing upgrade for many clients
  • Additional Meeting Room Credits: Adding a few extra hours of meeting room access can make basic package more attractive
  • Access to Exclusive Events: Including invitations to certain networking opportunities, workshops, or community events can enhance the perceived value of the basic package

By enhancing the basic package, you make it easier to transition clients to higher levels of membership in the future.

Tiered Membership Levels with Added Benefits

Tiered membership levels are an effective way to cater to different client needs and budgets, making it easier to upsell. Each tier should offer progressively more benefits, encouraging members to upgrade.

For example:

  • Bronze Membership: Includes standard access to the coworking space, basic internet, and a limited number of meeting room hours
  • Silver Membership: Adds faster internet, more meeting room hours, and access to additional services like printing and administrative support
  • Gold Membership: Offers all the benefits of the Silver membership, plus exclusive access to premium areas, priority booking for events and amenities, and more comprehensive business support services

By clearly differentiating the benefits of each tier, you can make the value proposition of upgrading evident to your clients.

Day Passes

Day passes are a flexible option that can attract a variety of clients, from freelancers needing occasional workspace to potential long-term members wanting to try out your space. You can use day passes as an upselling tool by:

  • Offering Discounts on Bulk Purchases: Encourage clients to buy multiple day passes at a reduced rate
  • Bundling with Additional Services: Include perks like free coffee, printing credits, or access to events with day passes

Day passes can serve as a gateway for clients to experience the benefits of a full membership.

Offering Exclusive Access to Premium Spaces and Amenities

Creating exclusive areas within your coworking space can add a sense of prestige and encourage clients to upgrade their membership.

Loyal members willing to pay more for exclusive spaces deserve that luxury, and other members will yearn for the day they have access to those otherwise restricted areas.

These exclusive areas can be anything from private offices to premium lounges and VIP meeting rooms.

Private offices are ideal for clients needing dedicated quiet time and premium lounges and VIP meeting rooms can offer comfortable, ergonomic furniture and feature the latest technology. By making these premium amenities exclusive and desirable, you can entice clients to pay extra for access.

Special Discounts for Long-Term Commitments or Bundled Services

Long-term commitments and bundled services can provide significant value to your members while securing steady revenue for your coworking space.

You might want to consider offering:

  • Discounts for Annual Memberships: Encourage clients to commit to a longer-term membership by offering a discount when they pay upfront
  • Bundled Services Packages: Combine popular services/amenities into bundles at a discounted rate. For example, a bundle might include a higher-tier membership, additional meeting room hours or guest passes, and virtual office services at a lower combined cost than purchasing each separately
  • Referral Discounts: Offer existing clients a discount on their membership if they refer a new member for a long-term commitment

These incentives not only increase revenue but also build client loyalty and satisfaction.

Offering Premium Services or Amenities

Differentiating your space from the rest of the competition becomes increasingly important as you work towards growing your business.

One of the most effective ways to boost revenue from existing clients is by offering premium services and amenities.

These enhancements not only add value to your membership packages but also create a more attractive and productive environment for your clients.

Common premium services that coworking spaces offer could include:

  • Advanced IT support for members’ peace of mind
  • Enhanced privacy options by way of enhanced private offices, soundproof booths, or extra IT security
  • High-tech meeting and conference rooms equipped with video conferencing capabilities, whiteboards, and other business tools
  • On-demand concierge and administrative support services
  • Premium service bundles geared towards specific client types

Premium amenities are an added bonus and can be the cherry on top when trying to close a deal. Popular premium amenities include:

  • Wellness programs
  • Catering and beverage services
  • Networking events and workshops
  • VIP lounges
  • Quiet zones
  • Podcast studios
  • Outdoor spaces

Offering premium services and amenities is a powerful strategy for increasing revenue from existing members.

By identifying client needs and offering high-value services and amenities, you can enhance the overall client experience and foster customer loyalty.

Enhanced Tech Services

Enhanced tech services can certainly be lumped into premium services, but technology is also a beast of its own nature.

The integration of advanced technology within coworking spaces can significantly enhance the member experience and, in turn, increase revenue. By offering enhanced tech services, coworking spaces can attract tech-savvy clients and provide added value that justifies higher membership fees.

Smart Office Solutions

Smart office solutions utilize the Internet of Things (IoT) to create a more efficient, comfortable, and productive work environment. Implementing these technologies can make your coworking space more appealing to potential and existing clients.

Here are a few ideas to get your juices flowing:

  • IoT Devices: Smart devices like connected printers, smart locks, and occupancy sensors can streamline operations and improve security. For example, the integration between OfficeRnD and Kisi allows members to open and unlock doors right from their phones.
  • Automated Lighting: Implementing smart lighting systems that adjust based on occupancy and natural light can reduce energy costs and enhance the working environment. Clients will appreciate the comfort and energy efficiency.
  • Temperature Control: Smart thermostats that allow members to control the temperature of their workspace can significantly improve comfort levels. These systems can be programmed to optimize energy use while maintaining a pleasant working environment.

Virtual Office Services

Virtual office services are essential for remote workers, freelancers, and businesses that need a professional presence without a physical office.

Offering these services can attract a broader range of clients and provide additional revenue streams. Two of the best options for this include cloud storage and virtual receptionists.

Providing secure, reliable cloud storage solutions allows members to store and access their files from anywhere.

Virtual receptionist services can handle calls, schedule appointments, and manage client interactions. These services add a layer of professionalism and can be particularly appealing to small businesses and startups

Advanced Booking Systems

Efficiently managing resources like meeting rooms and equipment is crucial to a successful coworking space. Advanced booking systems can streamline this process and provide a better experience for your clients.

Consider offering the following features:

  • Online Booking Platforms and Applications: User-friendly online platforms where members can easily book meeting rooms, equipment, and other resources reduces administrative burden and allows members to manage their own bookings. Check out the coworking booking platform that OfficeRnD Flex offers.
  • Real-Time Availability: Using IoT and integrated software to provide real-time updates on room and equipment availability helps prevent double bookings and ensures members have access to the resources they need when they need them.
  • Automated Reminders and Notifications: Automated reminders and notifications can help clients keep track of their bookings and reduce no-shows. This ensures optimal utilization of your resources and enhances the client experience.

Enhancing your coworking space with advanced tech services is a powerful way to increase revenue from existing clients. By integrating these technologies, you can position your coworking space as a cutting-edge, efficient, and highly desirable workplace.

Building a Community and Providing Networking Opportunities

Building a vibrant community and providing ample networking opportunities are a big part of offering premium services.

After all, hospitality is the most powerful differentiator in 2024. This is something that Edward Hobbs from “x+why” and Kenny Kane from Firmspace discussed during FlexWorld Series 2024.

Hosting events not only enhances the client experience but also fosters loyalty and engagement, encouraging members to invest more in your organization.

So how else can you leverage exclusive member-only events, access to a global network, and community-building activities to boost your revenue? Let’s find out.

Exclusive Member-Only Networking Events

Exclusive networking events are a powerful tool to foster connections amongst your members and add significant value to their coworking experience.

These events can be tailored to the interests and needs of your community, providing opportunities for professional growth, collaboration, and social interaction. Consider the following events:

  • Industry-specific meetups
  • Expert panels and workshops
  • Socials and mixers

For example, Amanda Lewan from Bamboo organizes an introvert-friendly networking and community-building event for like-minded women in Ann Arbor.

By promoting these exclusive events, you can justify higher membership tiers that include access to such valuable networking opportunities.

Access to a Global Network of Coworking Spaces

Offering access to a global network of coworking spaces can be a major selling point for members who travel frequently or work remotely.

This benefit not only enhances the value of their membership but also opens up new revenue streams for your coworking space.

Highlighting the convenience and flexibility of accessing coworking spaces worldwide can attract more clients and encourage existing members to upgrade their membership.

Community-Building Activities and Collaboration Opportunities

Creating a strong sense of community within your coworking space can significantly enhance member satisfaction and retention. Community-building activities and collaboration opportunities can transform your coworking space from a simple workspace into a thriving hub of innovation and support.

Here are a few ideas:

  • Collaborative projects
  • Interest groups and clubs
  • Member spotlights and showcases
  • Mentorship programs

By promoting these community-building activities, you can create a more engaging and supportive environment that encourages members to stay longer and invest more in your services. This is something that fosters hospitality as well.

Promoting Health and Wellness Programs

Health and wellness have become paramount for professionals seeking a balanced and productive lifestyle. Coworking spaces can leverage this trend by offering comprehensive health and wellness programs, not only enhancing the overall health, well-being, and experience of their members, but they can use it to provide an additional revenue stream.

Many workers are going to see the opportunity to take part in wellness programs as a must – I mean who doesn’t want to prioritize their health? And if they’re able to prioritize their health while they’re at work (and not take more time out of their day at the top or bottom), then it’s a win-win.

So, how can you upsell wellness in your coworking space?

On-Site Fitness Classes and Wellness Programs

Offering on-site fitness classes and wellness programs is a great way to attract health-conscious professionals and provide added value to your members.

These programs can range from yoga and pilates to high-intensity interval training (HIIT) and meditation sessions.

Promote these wellness programs as part of a higher-tier membership package or offer them as add-ons, providing flexible options for members to choose from.

Access to Premium Gym Facilities

An investment for sure, but access to premium gym fasciitis can be a significant draw for potential clients and an excellent upsell for existing members.

If your space allows for it, set up a well-equipped gym within your coworking space. Include essential equipment such as cardio machines, free weights, and functional training equipment.

Don’t feel the need to transform your office space into Planet Fitness though. If an on-site gym is not feasible, partner with nearby premium gyms to offer discounted memberships or exclusive access to your members. You can offer these as part of a premium membership or as an a la carte option.

Personalized Wellness Plans and Mental Health Support

Personalized wellness plans and mental health support are becoming increasingly important as more professionals seek holistic approaches to their well-being.

Providing these services can set your coworking space apart and create a supportive environment that fosters productivity and well-being.

Promoting health and wellness programs is a powerful strategy for increasing revenue from your existing member base.

These programs not only boost your revenue through higher-priced membership sales, but also foster a thriving, productive, and forward-thinking community within your coworking space.

Offering Food and Beverage Options

One of the last amenities we want to highlight is one everyone can appreciate: food and beverage!

Offering food and beverage options is a powerful way to create a welcoming and productive environment that encourages members to stay longer and invest more. I know if I could just get my morning coffee at work rather than waiting in the drive-thru, I’d definitely be willing to pay more.

Here’s how you can leverage premium coffee services, snack bars, catered lunches, culinary events, and subscription-based meal plans to increase revenue from your existing members.

  • Premium/Gourmet Coffee Services: Invest in top-notch coffee machines and offer a selection of premium coffee blends. Partner with local roasters to provide unique and high-quality coffee options that can become a daily ritual for your members.
  • Snack Bars: Set up snack bars stocked with a variety of both health-friendly snacks and indulgent options. Include items such as fresh fruit, granola bars, artisanal snacks, and more. This convenience can keep members fueled throughout the day without having to leave the workspace.
  • Catered Lunches: Offer catered lunches from local restaurants or in-house kitchens. Providing a variety of lunch options, including vegetarian, vegan, and gluten-free choices can cater to diverse dietary needs.

Upsell these offerings by adding them to premium-tiered memberships, provide food and beverage allowances where members can add money to their account, or charge a la carte.

Subscription-Based Meal Plans

Subscription-based meal plans offer convenience and cost savings for members while providing a steady stream of revenue to your coworking space. Here’s an example of how to design and implement meal plans:

  • Flexible Meal Options: Offer a range of meal plans to suit different needs and budgets. For example, provide options for daily lunches, weekly meal kits, or monthly meal subscriptions.
  • Healthy and Diverse Menus: Work with local caterers or in-house chefs to create diverse and healthy menus that cater to various dietary preferences and restrictions. Highlight the quality and variety of the meals to attract health-conscious members.
  • Convenient Delivery and Pickup: Ensure that meal delivery and pickup processes are seamless. Set up designated areas for meal pickups or deliver meals directly to members’ desks.

Upselling Through Digital Channels

In the digital age, leveraging online platforms and tools can significantly enhance your ability to upsell and increase revenue from existing clients in coworking spaces. It will happen with the right marketing strategies.

Utilizing personalized email marketing, social media for exclusive offers, and creating a seamless online upselling experience through your website and apps can drive engagement and encourage members to invest more in your services.

Personalized Email Marketing Campaigns

Email marketing remains one of the most effective ways to communicate with your members directly.

By personalizing your email campaigns, you can create targeted messages that resonate with your members’ specific needs and preferences. Here are some strategies to help you get started:

  • Segment your Audience: Divide your email list into segments based on member behavior, preferences, and membership levels. This allows you to tailor your messages and offers to each group effectively
  • Personalized Recommendations: Use data from member interactions and preferences to suggest relevant services, upgrades, or events. For example, if a member frequently books meeting rooms, offer them a package deal for additional meeting room hours.
  • Exclusive Offers: Send personalized emails with exclusive offers and promotions, such as discounts on premium memberships, early access to events, or limited-time deals on additional services

By delivering personalized and relevant content, you can increase the likelihood of members taking advantage of upsell opportunities.

Utilizing Social Media for Exclusive Offers and Promotions

Social media platforms are powerful tools for engaging with your community and promoting exclusive offers and services. Here’s how you can effectively use social media to upsell:

  • Targeted ads
  • Exclusive promotions
  • Engaging content

Social media not only helps you reach a broader audience, but also provides a platform for real-time interaction and feedback, making it easier to tailor your offers to your members’ needs.

Creating a Seamless Online Upselling Experience Through the Website and Apps

Your website and mobile apps are critical touchpoints for interacting with your members and facilitating upsells. By creating a seamless and intuitive online experience, you can make it easier for members to discover and purchase additional services.

Here’s how:

  • User-friendly Interface: Ensure your website and apps are easy to navigate, with clear CTAs and a streamlined checkout process
  • Integrated Booking and Payment Systems: Integrate booking and payment systems within your website and apps to allow members to book services, purchase event tickets seamlessly, or automate their billing processes. For more information on integrating payment systems, take a look at how OfficeRnD uses Stripe2.0.
  • Personalized Dashboards: Create personalized member dashboards that highlight relevant services, upcoming events, and special offers based on their usage patterns and preferences. This can encourage members to explore and purchase additional options.
  • In-App Notifications: Use push notifications and in-app messages to inform members about new services, exclusive offers, and important updates. Personalized notifications can prompt members to take action and explore upsell opportunities.

Digital platforms will allow you to provide a smooth and engaging upselling experience that encourages members to invest more in your coworking space.

Tracking and Analyzing Upselling Performance

Now that you know how to upsell to your current members, it’s time to look at how well you’re upselling initiatives are going. It’s not enough to just implement upselling strategies, it’s crucial that you track and analyze your performance as well.

By understanding which approaches work best and continuously ideating and improving based on data, you can optimize your efforts and ensure sustained growth.

Key Metrics to Track Upselling Success

Identifying and monitoring key metrics is essential for evaluating the effectiveness of your upselling efforts. During our recent FlexWorld Series, we were honored to have the opportunity to talk with industry experts about this very topic.

OfficeRnD CEO, Miro Miroslavov moderated the “Measure What Matters in Coworking” session, and spoke with CCO at Industrious, Anna Levine, COO at Clockwise, Alexandra Livesey, and Product and Data Director at OfficeRnD, Mihail Kyosev about the most important metrics across that successful coworking spaces use.

The group concluded one of the best metrics to measure success in your coworking space is the occupancy rate. However, there are different ways to measure occupancy.

Occupancy almost directly correlates with profitability, but it’s important to look at the overall occupancy rate as well as the revenue occupancy.

Revenue occupancy is the percentage of rental revenue on a monthly basis. This tends to be the preferred occupancy KPI as it takes into account discounts and upgrades.

Sure it’s great if you have a full space, but imagine a space full of members with premium packages and memberships? Revenue occupancy is going to show you where you fall for the month in terms of budget and profit as opposed to just how many people are using your space.

Upselling conversion rates and sole revenue growth from upsells are also highly useful. The conversion rate allows you to see the percentage of members who respond to upselling offers and make additional purchases while the sole revenue from upsells will give you the exact dollar amount brought in from the upgrades.

Both numbers will give you a sense of how well your members respond to upselling and gives you a goal to work towards.

Churn rate is always important to monitor as well. Effective upselling should ideally help reduce churn by increasing client satisfaction and loyalty, so you’ll want to make sure you pay attention to this.

Engagement metrics are another great way to measure your upselling. Take note of how many and how often members are taking advantage of their premium services. Are they attending social gatherings? Are they using the meal services?

If members are not using the services they’re investing in, find out why. The goal is to keep members happy with these extra add-ons, so make sure they’re worth their while.

  • Optimize Pricing and Offers: Adjust pricing structures and upselling offers based on performance data to maximize uptake and revenue
  • Enhance Member Experience: Use feedback and engagement metrics to enhance the overall member experience, ensuring that upselling initiatives add real value and improve satisfaction
  • A/B Testing: Continuously test different upselling messages, offers, and delivery methods to identify the most effective approaches. Use A/B testing to compare performance and iterate on your strategies
  • Training and Development: Equip your staff with insights and tools they need to effectively implement upselling strategies. Regular training and development based on performance data can improve their effectiveness

Tracking and analyzing upselling performance is essential for maximizing revenue from your existing members.

Name: Coworking Spaces vs. Traditional Offices: Evaluating the Best Choice for Businesses
Author: asen-stoyanchev
Short cards description: Many businesses face a real decision in a work landscape that keeps shifting. Is the traditional office still worth it? Does a coworking space make more sense? Which one sets a business up to succeed?
Post body:
Many businesses face a real decision in a work landscape that keeps shifting. Is the traditional office still worth it? Does a coworking space make more sense? Which one sets a business up to succeed?

It’s about more than having somewhere to work. It’s about picking an environment that supports growth, productivity, and community.

This article breaks down the differences between coworking spaces and traditional offices, with the pros and cons of each.

Understanding these trade-offs gives you, as a coworking space owner, a clearer read on what potential members are weighing. That helps you position your space and win the businesses comparing their options.

Quick Summary

  • Coworking spaces and traditional offices are both viable workspace options, each with clear advantages.
  • A coworking space is a shared work environment used by people and teams from multiple companies.
  • A traditional office is a dedicated physical workspace leased or owned by a single company.
  • The right choice depends on a business’s specific needs, budget, and values.

What Is a Coworking Space?

A coworking space is a shared office environment where individuals and teams from different companies work under one roof, paying for access through flexible memberships instead of a long lease.

They’re often used by freelancers, small companies, startups, and remote workers, and they usually offer a mix of:

  • Private offices
  • Open desks
  • Communal areas

Members can work on their own or together in a shared setting.

Coworking spaces are built for flexibility. They match how modern professionals work and the tools they expect. Companies get high-speed internet, meeting rooms, and other amenities without signing a traditional office lease.

Coworking has grown fast over the past decade, driven by demand for flexible workspace. There are now roughly 42,000 coworking spaces worldwide, with the figure expected to reach about 44,000 by the end of 2026.

Flexible office spaces have become places where diverse groups of professionals share ideas, resources, and opportunities.

What Are the Advantages of a Coworking Space?

Coworking spaces give building owners and operators an edge. Here’s how.

Flexibility

Flexibility is the core of a good coworking space, and it starts with the lease terms.

Short commitments appeal to businesses that can’t predict how their team size will change.

A traditional office lease often runs 5 to 10 years in competitive markets. Coworking spaces work differently, offering anything from month-to-month to one-year contracts.

So if you own a building, instead of leaving it empty while a few tenants weigh a long lease, you can fill it with startups and small companies that need space now.

Cost Savings

With the rise of hybrid work, many businesses can’t justify the cost of a full traditional office.

Gallup’s 2025 data shows that only about 21% of remote-capable U.S. employees work fully on-site, while hybrid remains the dominant arrangement at 51%. Companies want alternatives that fit how they actually operate.

Coworking cuts overhead, which is a strong pitch. Members share resources like Wi-Fi and office equipment, and they can tap into community and networking events you host at the building.

Recent CoworkingCafe research backs up the cost argument: for a team of 10, coworking is cheaper than a conventional lease in the vast majority of U.S. markets, with savings topping $100,000 a year in the priciest metros. Lower cost is a marketing message that lands.

Innovation and Collaboration

Coworking spaces have a track record of hosting companies through their early growth. Several now-large tech companies spent their early days in shared workspaces.

The open, collaborative atmosphere encourages creativity and cross-industry connections. Promoting that culture attracts entrepreneurs and businesses looking to collaborate.

Niche Coworking Spaces

A steady trend in coworking is spaces built for specific industries.

Examples include:

  • Tech
  • Healthcare
  • Creative design

Industry-specific spaces let you position your workspace as a hub for like-minded professionals. That’s a real competitive advantage.

The niche could also be sustainability. With corporate focus on environmental responsibility, you can market to companies looking to cut their carbon footprint.

Point to shared resources and lower energy use. Or add features like bike-sharing programs, solar panels, or green roofs.

Want to learn more about the latest trends in flex and coworking? Download this free report that's packed with valuable data.

What Are the Disadvantages of a Coworking Space?

Coworking spaces have real challenges. Here are the main ones, and how you can address them as an operator.

Privacy Concerns

Operators have to work harder to guarantee data privacy and security for members.

Networks are shared and conversations can be overheard, so protecting private information matters.

Many operators install private phone booths for sensitive calls and set up more secure Wi-Fi. Those steps reassure businesses that they can get the benefits of coworking without giving up privacy.

Distractions and Noise

The same environment that fuels connection can also bring noise. Businesses need both collaborative and quiet space for their teams.

Building owners increasingly add quiet zones for focused work. Soundproofing helps create separate areas that block noise, balancing a lively community with room to concentrate.

Brand Identity

Building a distinct culture and brand is harder in a shared space, since companies have less control over their physical environment.

For companies that want more branding, you can set up private areas where they can display their identity. You can also host events or workshops that fit their brand.

For example, if several of your members work in sustainability, a sustainability workshop helps them build their culture inside your space.

What Is Considered a Traditional Office?

A traditional office is a dedicated physical space leased or owned by a single company. Large corporations, healthcare facilities, and government agencies use them most.

Traditional offices usually contain:

  • Private office spaces
  • Cubicles
  • Break rooms
  • Reception areas

All under one roof. The company pays a lease to rent the space or, less commonly, owns the building.

A traditional office gives a structured environment built on stability. It has been the default for business operations for decades.

What Are the Advantages of a Traditional Office?

The traditional office has been the go-to for a long time because it offers clear benefits.

Professional Image

A dedicated office is a strong part of a company’s image. The company can express its brand through design in a prime location.

A traditional office gives clients a sense of legitimacy that impresses their own customers and partners. It costs more, but businesses may pay for it if it helps them win.

Coworking spaces offer a different image: a modern business in an active, professional community.

Focus and Control

A company in its own office has more control over the space. Thoughtful layouts improve productivity, cut distractions, and create room for deep focus.

A graphic design firm, for example, knows exactly how many breakout rooms it needs for brainstorming and where the team needs adjustable desks and inspiration boards. That can push it toward a traditional office.

Adaptable coworking spaces can close much of this gap.

Structure

The layout gives a traditional office a degree of structure many businesses like.

From executive offices to departmental zones, a dedicated space lets a company set a clear hierarchy and workflow.

Marketing and sales teams might sit next to each other, so working together is easy. Leadership can oversee operations directly.

Coworking operators can copy some of this structure by:

  • Creating designated areas
  • Letting members reconfigure spaces
  • Designing for visibility

What Are the Disadvantages of a Traditional Office?

The structure and control come with real drawbacks for today’s businesses.

High Costs

The cost of running a traditional office is substantial.

Companies that go this route pay for:

  • Rent
  • Maintenance
  • Utilities
  • Office supplies

Build-out alone runs $150 to $200 per square foot before anyone sits down. These are fixed, often long-term commitments that eat into profit and tie up cash flow.

Coworking is a far more cost-effective model, which is exactly why it draws so many businesses.

Limited Flexibility

A company in a traditional office can feel boxed in. Long, expensive leases make it hard to scale up for growth or trim down. Some teams grow or shrink with the season or the project.

That rigidity doesn’t suit businesses that need to pivot with the market.

The proof is in the many companies trying to justify their office space while more of their team works remotely.

Technology Lag

Traditional offices often fall behind on technology. They’re built for stability, not frequent change, so upgrades tend to be more disruptive.

Coworking spaces are usually more compact and modular. A steady flow of members and turnover creates both the reason and the chance to keep tech current and attract new businesses.

Technology keeps mattering more. Falling behind on infrastructure is a risk for any flex space operator planning to last.

A Pros and Cons Summary for Coworking Spaces vs. Traditional Offices

Here’s the comparison in one place:

Coworking spaceTraditional office
Lease termsMonth-to-month to 1 yearTypically 5 to 10 years
Upfront costLow; no build-outHigh; build-out, furniture, setup
ScalabilityAdd or drop space easilyConstrained by the lease
PrivacyShared networks and space; private options cost moreFully private and controlled
BrandingLimited; some private areasFull control of the environment
NetworkingBuilt into the communityMostly internal to the team
TechnologyIncluded and regularly updatedManaged in-house; upgrades slower
Best forFreelancers, startups, hybrid teams, satellite officesLarge teams, confidential work, specialized setups

Neither option is perfect. The right choice comes down to each business’s needs and preferences, which is what the next section covers.

How Do You Know Which Space Is Right for Your Business?

This is one of the most common questions your potential members ask themselves. The choice between coworking and a traditional office depends on factors specific to each business.

Most businesses weigh team size and growth stage, and they get clear on their current and future operational needs.

Remote Workers and Freelancers

Coworking is a clear fit for teams that need flexible work.

Buffer’s 2023 State of Remote Work report found that 98% of respondents want to work remotely at least some of the time. Companies competing for that talent benefit from coworking’s lower cost, and it gives freelancers and remote workers a place to connect when they need one.

Small Business Owners

Small teams benefit from the adaptability and scalability of coworking, which supports growth without the weight of a traditional lease.

Some businesses depend on heavy, specialized equipment, like medical devices or manufacturing tools. Those companies may find a traditional office fits better.

Property Developers

Developers should look ahead when deciding how to manage their assets. The number of coworking spaces keeps climbing: in the U.S., CoworkingCafe’s Q2 2026 report counted about 9,384 flex offices nationwide, up steadily quarter over quarter. That’s a chance to attract startups and tech companies and generate revenue.

Coworking can slot into existing buildings. Flexible, modern, well-equipped space makes a property more appealing to tenants and job candidates alike.

Professionals in Confidential Industries

Sectors like law and finance need maximum client confidentiality and a formal, trustworthy image.

Traditional offices are the clear choice here because of their private, controlled environment.

11 Tips to Capitalize on the Growing Demand for Coworking Spaces

Here’s how to serve businesses that choose coworking, ideally yours.

  1. Implement a membership system: Offer diverse membership tiers, including virtual office services. Cater to different needs and budgets, and widen your market.
  2. Use your location: Promote the convenience of your location as a lifestyle choice. Point to proximity to public transit, dining, and entertainment.
  3. Introduce an incubator program: Partner with local startups, accelerators, or investors. Mentorship and funding attract early-stage companies.
  4. Offer childcare solutions: Stand out with on-site childcare amenities, or partner with local providers, for parent entrepreneurs and remote workers.
  5. Get green-certified: Pursue sustainability certifications to appeal to eco-conscious businesses. Point to energy efficiency, waste reduction, and sustainable design.
  6. Be pet-friendly: Let members bring pets. It supports work-life balance and sets you apart.
  7. Collaborate with culture: Work with local artists and cultural institutions. Rotating exhibits add to the aesthetics and the community.
  8. Focus on wellness: Add meditation spaces and fitness studios to support members’ physical and mental health.
  9. Use your space well: Smart furniture and configurable workspaces adapt to different events and working styles.
  10. Partner up: Set up partnerships with tech, wellness, and lifestyle brands. Offer members exclusive deals and experiences.
  11. Use a coworking management platform: OfficeRnD Flex automates billing and payments and keeps members happy. Learn more here.

Coworking Spaces vs. Traditional Offices: Final Recommendation

There’s no single right answer for every organization. But work is trending toward remote, adaptable, and project-based models, and coworking spaces are built for exactly that.

Technology plays a big part. Coworking spaces are more likely to adopt:

  • Smart access control systems
  • Internet of Things devices
  • AI-managed meeting rooms

There’s also the cultural shift toward work-life balance and sustainability. Coworking spaces are better set up for flexible schedules and remote work.

They can also lower a company’s carbon footprint at a time when customers care about sustainable practices.

For businesses aiming to succeed today, coworking is a strong strategic choice. Use that to your advantage.

Name: The Network Effect: Leveraging Community for Business Growth in Coworking Environments
Author: asen-stoyanchev
Short cards description: The coworking market has grown fast. It grew from $26.2 billion in 2025 to a projected $30.12 billion in 2026 at a 15% compound annual growth rate, and it’s expected to reach $53.46 billion by 2030. Post body:
The coworking market has grown fast. It grew from $26.2 billion in 2025 to a projected $30.12 billion in 2026 at a 15% compound annual growth rate, and it’s expected to reach $53.46 billion by 2030. Remote work, the gig economy, and startups chasing flexible, cost-effective office space have all pushed it forward.

That growth has crowded the field. Most operators offer the same core services: shared desks, private offices, meeting rooms, and amenities like fast internet, coffee, and printers.

In that kind of market, the spaces that put hospitality and community first hold a real edge over the ones that treat their space like a landlord.

Community and hospitality reinforce each other. Members get a supportive network and good service, which raises satisfaction and productivity. That, in turn, builds an engaged member base, which is what keeps a coworking business growing over time.

Quick Summary:

The network effect in coworking spaces is the pattern where a workspace becomes more valuable as more people join and interact within the community. As membership grows, the opportunities for networking, collaboration, and knowledge sharing grow with it, making the space more attractive to prospective members. Operators can build on this by running events, workshops, and social activities that get members talking and working together.

We call this the “Network Effect.” In a coworking space, it means that as more businesses and individuals join the community, the opportunities for networking, collaboration, and business growth increase, making the space more valuable to each member.

What is the network effect in coworking spaces?

The network effect is a business principle: when more people use a product or service, its value increases. That creates a positive feedback loop. The more users who join, the more attractive the network becomes to the next user.

The data backs this up for coworking specifically. 95% of coworking members report business growth since joining a space, whether that’s new clients, new revenue, or career advancement. 80% of members say they turn to fellow members for help or guidance on their work. Those numbers only get stronger as a community fills out.

Examples in technology and social networks

  • Social media platforms (e.g., Facebook, LinkedIn): Each new user can connect with existing users, share content, and interact, which raises the value of the platform for everyone.
  • Marketplaces (e.g., eBay, Airbnb): As more buyers and sellers join eBay, the variety and availability of goods increase, attracting even more users. More hosts and guests on Airbnb widen the range of available stays.
  • Communication tools (e.g., WhatsApp, Slack): More users make these platforms more useful, whether for personal messaging or team collaboration.

How does the network effect work in a coworking space?

As more individuals and businesses join a coworking space, the potential for networking, collaboration, and knowledge sharing goes up.

That makes for a more active and valuable environment for everyone. A larger, more varied member base attracts people who see a range of skill sets and backgrounds to collaborate with.

A growing community also justifies more events, workshops, and services, which improves the member experience and pulls in more people still.

Examples:

  • Collaboration opportunities: In a space with a healthy membership, a freelance graphic designer might meet a startup founder who needs branding help. Both benefit.
  • Community building: Larger spaces can run more frequent, more varied events, from professional workshops to social gatherings, which strengthens the community and makes the space more attractive to potential members.
  • Support networks: As membership grows, so does the collective knowledge available. Members tap this network for advice, support, and mentorship, which raises the value of the space for all of them.

What can give you an edge in a competitive coworking space market? Hint: hospitality. We discussed that extensively during our annual FlexWorld conference. Check out the recap here.

The role of community in coworking spaces

Community matters to freelancers, startups, and small businesses in different ways. A good one drives collaboration, provides support, and creates connections that help members grow professionally and personally.

The referral loop is where this shows up most clearly. 65% of members have passed on work or leads to someone else in their coworking community. People refer business to the person they’ve nodded to in the hallway for months, not to a stranger, and coworking creates that familiarity just by putting people in the same space day after day.

Why community matters for different groups

For freelancers:

  • Combatting isolation: Freelancers often work alone, which gets lonely. A coworking community gives them social interaction and a sense of belonging. 88% of members report that coworking cuts down the isolation that keeps solo founders and freelancers from building a network at all.
  • Networking opportunities: Access to a range of professionals leads to new client relationships, partnerships, and work.
  • Skill sharing: Freelancers learn from their peers and pick up skills that improve their own work.

For startups:

  • Support systems: Startups gain a supportive environment where they can share experiences, ask for advice, and get feedback from other founders.
  • Resource sharing: They cut costs by sharing meeting rooms, office equipment, and even professional services.
  • Funding opportunities: Being close to other startups and investors can open doors to funding and investment.

For small businesses:

  • Scaling flexibility: Coworking spaces offer flexible terms, so small businesses can scale up or down as their needs change.
  • Collaborative opportunities: Small businesses find clients, partners, or service providers within the community.
  • Enhanced credibility: Belonging to a professional network can improve a small business’s reputation.

Types of communities in coworking spaces

Across our network of coworking partners, we’ve found two main community types: industry-specific communities, or “niche spaces,” and interest-based communities.

Niche coworking spaces are built with specific members in mind and serve a distinct purpose.

When part of the market is underserved, “niching down” tends to retain more members than a general space would, because those members’ specific needs are actually being met.

Higher satisfaction and loyalty feed the network effect directly. For more on niche coworking spaces, see this breakdown of the most popular flex space niche groups.

Interest-based communities are on the rise too. People gravitate toward others who share their interests, and the workplace is no different.

Two of the most common interest-based spaces we see are “social impact and sustainability” spaces and “wellness-oriented” spaces.

Benefits of a strong community

If you’ve ever been part of a strong community, you know the payoff. From support and comfort to networking and collaboration, it’s worth something.

Here’s how a strong coworking community helps its members:

Networking and collaboration

  • Members connect with potential clients, partners, and mentors, which leads to joint projects and business.
  • Regular events, workshops, and social gatherings create real connections.
  • Working next to motivated peers helps people stay focused and productive.
  • A supportive environment helps members push through challenges.

Personal and professional growth

  • Community support drives personal development through mentorship, skill-sharing, and peer feedback.
  • Professional growth comes from continuous learning, industry connections, and exposure to new ideas.

Well-being and satisfaction

  • A sense of belonging improves mental well-being and job satisfaction.
  • Social interaction and community engagement support a healthier work-life balance.

Community sits at the center of successful coworking spaces, giving freelancers, startups, and small businesses support and opportunity they wouldn’t get on their own.

By building belonging and making collaboration easy, coworking communities help members do better work.

Whether industry-specific or interest-based, these communities offer benefits that drive growth, which is what makes coworking spaces a genuine resource rather than just a desk rental.

The role of community managers

Community managers make or break a coworking space. They connect members, build the community, and keep the environment positive and productive.

Their work goes well beyond admin. It includes community building, event planning, and one-on-one member support.

Key responsibilities of community managers

  • Organizing community events
  • Building a supportive environment
  • Creating spaces for collaboration
  • Encouraging a culture of collaboration

How community managers affect the member experience

  • More collaboration and new ideas

Community managers are the connectors and the support system for members. Their work builds the interconnected community that makes the whole space more valuable.

Networking opportunities in coworking spaces

Coworking spaces create networking through both formal and informal channels, giving members plenty of ways to build relationships, share knowledge, and start collaborations.

Here’s how those opportunities show up.

Formal networking events

Workshops: Workshops usually focus on a specific skill or industry trend, bringing members together to learn and interact. Inviting industry experts to lead them gives members a chance to connect with influential people and pick up useful insights.

Examples: a Lunch & Learn for independent workers, or a hands-on DIY workshop.

Seminars: Seminars on business strategy, technology trends, or marketing give members a way to share and gain knowledge. Q&A sessions let members interact directly with speakers, which deepens the discussion and the networking.

Examples: a panel discussion, or an investor Q&A.

Informal networking events

Casual interactions and shared workspaces: Open desk areas and common lounges spark conversations and spontaneous introductions. Some of the most valuable business conversations happen in the two minutes it takes to make a cup of coffee.

Chats in the kitchenette or by the coffee machine turn into real professional relationships.

Booking and using shared meeting rooms introduces members to each other, especially when they coordinate schedules and share space. That kind of cross-company meeting room use is growing: meeting room bookings rose worldwide in 2025, up 24.5% in Asia-Pacific alone, as more members used shared spaces specifically to collaborate across companies (Cushman & Wakefield).

Events and celebrations: Holiday parties, happy hours, and milestone celebrations give members a relaxed setting to network.

Examples: a weekly happy hour, or launch parties for the community.

Community events: Social events like game nights, movie screenings, or lunch outings help members connect personally, which strengthens the professional bonds. Interest-based groups within the space, like book clubs or fitness groups, do the same.

Examples: a cooking workshop, a book club, or game nights.

Collaboration and innovation in coworking

Coworking spaces are more than places to work. They’re environments that support collaboration and new ideas.

The network effect amplifies both. The space gets more valuable as more members join and interact.

None of this happens by magic. It happens because a coworking space puts a genuinely diverse set of professionals in close, repeated, low-stakes contact, which is exactly the condition under which unplanned collaboration happens. A traditional office is full of people who do the same job. A coworking space is full of people who don’t.

Collaborative projects that start in coworking spaces:

  • Joint ventures
  • Cross-industry projects

How diverse skill sets drive new ideas:

  • Diverse membership and interdisciplinary collaboration
  • Resource sharing and shared expertise
  • Creative, stimulating environments

The network effect in collaboration and innovation

As membership grows, so do the chances for collaboration. Each new member adds to the collective knowledge and resources, which raises the value for everyone.

Successful collaborations attract more members, which increases the potential for new partnerships and projects. That drives business growth and creates a self-reinforcing cycle of value.

What’s next?

The network effect can turn a coworking space into a growing, active hub. Build a collaborative environment, support a diverse and engaged community, and use the right technology, and your space stands out in a crowded market.

This article will help you assess whether your coworking space business model is set up to be profitable. We’ll look at some common pitfalls, why some coworking space owners struggle, the operating costs to pay close attention to as you prepare to open your doors, and some revenue-boosting tips you’ll need to start a successful coworking space.

Ultimately, we’ll answer the question, “Are coworking spaces profitable?” — and when they are, under what circumstances?

Quick Answer: Coworking spaces can be profitable, particularly in urban areas with high demand for flexible work environments. Profitability depends on factors such as location, occupancy rates, membership pricing, and operational efficiency. How Much Profit Does a Coworking Space Generate?

A coworking space’s profit margin depends on many factors, including the space’s size, overhead costs, location, and demand. Generally speaking, the larger the space and the more loyal members you can attract, the larger your profits will be.

But on average, how profitable are coworking spaces? According to data cited by Sharpsheets.io, the average coworking space provider earns $742K in gross revenue per year, with a ~30% operating profit margin. This means that if your business were to bring in revenue in this ballpark, you could have around $222K in profit.

But to get there, you need to set your space up for success. Carefully monitor and control your costs while also providing a superior service from the start to attract high volumes of loyal customers. This makes your coworking space a worthwhile investment.

What Are the Typical Expenses of a Coworking Space?

To start a successful coworking space, you will need the right team members, utilities, logistics, equipment, and marketing — in addition to the space itself.

But how much of your overall budget should you expect to spend on each aspect?

Here are some of the typical startup operating costs you’ll need to factor in:

Office Equipment and Furniture

The cost of furniture and equipment can vary wildly depending on whether you’re purchasing new, high-end items or working with refurbished technology and lightly used desks and chairs.

Building Refurbishment

Is your space good to go, or does it need a little TLC before it’s ready for users? Perhaps new carpet, or an upgrade for the kitchen areas? What about amenities?

To accurately calculate your coworking space startup costs, you’ll need to factor in the structural and cosmetic attention the space needs ahead of your grand opening.

Connectivity Setup

Don’t forget to include this cost: your coworking space’s all-important connection to the internet! Will new wiring or outlets be needed, and are meeting rooms set up with the AV equipment your clients will need?

License

What kind of business license(s) do you need to operate in your state and city, and what are the associated fees?

Insurance

Whether you’re paying monthly or annual premiums, protecting your new business is vital and should be factored into your launch costs.

Professional liability insurance and commercial property insurance are examples of insurance types that might be relevant, and you’ll need to carefully research to ascertain which insurance types you’ll need.

Legal Fees

There might be legal costs associated with getting the paperwork for your new space in order. Whether these costs are connected with getting your lease agreement ready or reviewing the insurance coverage necessary, be sure to include them in your total startup cost tally.

How Do Coworking Spaces Make Money?

Now that you have your startup costs in order, let’s look at the different ways your coworking space can start making money:

Membership Fees

For most coworking spaces, the bulk of the revenue comes from a subscription model for your core offering of dedicated desk space.

You could opt to charge your customers weekly, monthly, or annually. But don’t forget to offer a daily option for those trying your space out for the first time, as well as flexible add-ons for loyal customers.

Meeting Rooms

Your meeting and conference rooms have high earning potential for your business, so make sure you optimize them for usage. Use a management software solution such as OfficeRnD Flex to manage coworking room bookings.

Additional Services

Consider providing lockers or bike racks for a small additional charge. An additional revenue stream could be printing rooms and mailing services.

You can also consider hosting networking events for your local professional community. In addition to bringing in more revenue, this draws more flexible workers into your space for the first time.

Why Do Some Coworking Spaces Struggle to Generate Revenue?

Here are some of the top pitfalls coworking spaces on the road to generating high revenue face:

Poor Marketing

A brand-new coworking space will only succeed if the right people know about it. As you plan the launch of your space, create a marketing plan that identifies the core channels to reach your target audience, along with a communications strategy for onboarding them as coworking space members.

Issues Retaining Clients

If clients struggle with booking the spaces they want when they want them, they might lose faith in them. The best way to avoid this is to offer a streamlined experience for members from the start.

Mastering hospitality can really elevate your coworking space.

High Rent Costs

Sky-high rent continues to be an issue for many coworking spaces. DeskMag’s 2023 survey found that spaces with high rental expenses were more likely to struggle to be profitable than those with lower costs.

You’ll need to make the most out of every single square foot. This makes a management platform for tracking space usage like OfficeRnD Flex, particularly helpful.

3 Tips for Generating Coworking Space Revenue

Owning a coworking business has a lot of benefits. To become a highly profitable coworking space within your first few years in business, you’ll need to offer a consistently high standard of service. Look for Upselling Opportunities

Use a management platform to make sure you always have a real-time view of your bookings and cancellations, and consider offering last-minute promotions to sell space that is going unused.

Make Data-Led Decisions

These pre-built dashboards show your most important KPIs at a glance, so even when you’re juggling multiple tasks at once, it’s easy to view and digest business-critical data.

When Does a Coworking Space Typically Break Even?

When you ask yourself, “Are coworking spaces profitable?” you’re no doubt wondering how long it will take you to break even or start turning a profit.

There’s no simple answer to this — it depends on many factors, including your overhead costs and location. The DeskMag survey mentioned above found that just 11% of coworking space locations were profitable within the first year. So, the chances are you will need to be patient to see returns.

For businesses that can weather this rocky start, though, the prospects are good. The same survey found that 68% of coworking space locations that are four to six years old are profitable.

In the long run, you’ll reap the rewards of setting up your business the right way from the beginning. So, take care to offer your customers an intuitive way to book and pay for their spaces to begin fostering loyalty from day one.

What Is a Coworking Space’s ROI?

To calculate your coworking space’s return on investment (ROI), you’ll need to compare your initial investment with the ongoing revenue stream and profits you expect.

We estimate it takes around $500K of initial investment to get a coworking space up and running.
