Author: asen-stoyanchev
Short cards description: Most people don’t enjoy spending time at work as much as they like hanging out with friends and family. But imagine the difference it would make in your team’s performance if you could recreate this “feel good” effect in your office environment.
Post body:
Most people don’t enjoy spending time at work as much as they like hanging out with friends and family. But imagine the difference it would make in your team’s performance if you could recreate this “feel good” effect in your office environment.

That’s exactly what workplace hospitality sets out to achieve.

Workplaces have changed a lot over the past few years, with the rise of hybrid teams being one of the most notable trends. But just because employees aren’t in the office every day doesn’t mean hospitality matters less. Maybe hospitality is even more important in those settings.

This article discusses workplace hospitality in detail, including what it is, its benefits, and how you can apply it in your place of work — even if that place is remote.

Quick Summary

  • Workplace hospitality is the practice of treating employees with the same care a hotel or restaurant gives its guests, so people feel welcomed and valued at work.
  • By being more hospitable, organizations can attract and retain talented employees, boost productivity, increase trust, and build belonging.
  • You can improve workplace hospitality by using the right software, recognizing employees’ work, adding in-demand amenities, holding regular one-on-ones, and introducing well-being policies.

What is workplace hospitality?

Workplace hospitality is the practice of treating your employees as well as you treat your guests. Hospitality venues like hotels and restaurants make guests feel special from the moment they walk through the door, and there’s no reason employers can’t do the same for their teams.

With workplace hospitality, organizations aim to increase employee satisfaction and well-being, which leads to other positive effects.

Workplace hospitality covers several aspects, including the following:

  • Workplace culture
  • Facilities
  • Amenities
  • Technology
  • Workplace relationships

As more companies adopt a culture of hybrid work and question traditional organizational structures, many managers are looking for ways to improve their workplaces and processes. Workplace hospitality is a growing way to meet employees’ needs.

One way hybrid workplaces can improve operations is through software. OfficeRnD Workplace helps organizations create work environments where people gather to collaborate and do their best work.

Besides offering office booking tools such as desk booking and meeting room booking, the software includes a visitor management system and collaborative scheduling features that let employees plan to meet up at the office.

One sure way to improve workplace hospitality and boost brand awareness is by welcoming guests with a sleek visitor management system. Learn more here.

Why is workplace hospitality important?

Ignore workplace hospitality and your team members can start to feel like cogs in the machine, expected to perform task after task without anyone considering their well-being or experience.

That’s a real risk with younger workers. 75% of Gen Z would reconsider applying to a company with unsatisfactory inclusion efforts, and workers across generations increasingly want their jobs to have a deeper purpose. Gen Z and millennials now make up a large share of the workforce, so you can’t afford to alienate them.

To avoid that, pay attention to workplace hospitality. It also helps you better support different work styles.

Check out a free visitor log Excel template.

Why workplace hospitality matters for hybrid teams

We’ve mentioned “the office” a few times, but workplace hospitality doesn’t apply only to teams in a physical space. People who work from home can sometimes feel more isolated, which leaves a team less connected and, often, less able to produce great work.

Some managers treat remote work as a privilege, so offering hybrid work is a form of workplace hospitality. But being genuinely hospitable means going further.

We’ll show you how shortly.

Benefits of workplace hospitality

If you’re already familiar with the benefits of hybrid work, you can probably guess the positive impact of workplace hospitality.

Here are some of its biggest payoffs.

Attracts top talent

Every company wants a team of standout employees. But since these people have options, they go wherever they’re treated best.

Managers sometimes assume a high enough salary guarantees they can hire the best in the business. Most candidates also weigh factors like:

  • Cultural fit
  • Values
  • Perks

All of these tie back to workplace hospitality.

Boosts employee retention

Say you hired that standout team. Now you need to retain them.

Your employees are one of your most valuable resources. Training them costs money, and if they leave, you’ll spend even more onboarding and training a replacement.

The days of jobs for life are long gone. Median job tenure has fallen to 3.9 years, its lowest level since 2002, as many employees move between companies to advance their careers and pay.

Even employees who stay can start “quiet quitting,” where effort drops without anyone handing in notice.

One way to keep people is to make sure they feel valued and satisfied at work, which is what workplace hospitality delivers. Show your team you value them, and they’ll show up for you.

Builds a sense of belonging

Belonging sits on the third step of Maslow’s hierarchy of needs, so it’s a core human need. No surprise, then, that 91% of employees who feel they belong at work are engaged, compared with just 20% of those who lack that sense of belonging.

This matters even more for hybrid teams, who can have a harder time connecting with colleagues.

Workplace hospitality can also spark more communication between departments or employees who don’t usually interact, so everyone feels more connected.

Increases trust

Research shows that employees in high-trust workplaces are 260% more motivated, 50% less likely to look for another job, and absent less often.

Workplace hospitality is one way to earn that trust.

Improves productivity

Employees with high job satisfaction are around 12% more productive than those without.

A few things explain that boost. Satisfied employees tend to be more motivated, engaged, creative, and focused, so they make fewer errors.

Productive employees feed into revenue and profits, which is why this should be a priority.

5 ways to increase the hospitality of your workplace

Here are five practical ways to make your workplace more hospitable.

Use the right software system

Software plays a growing part in employees’ workplace experiences. Beyond handling work tasks, it can improve how people feel about coming in.

In a hybrid setup, employees can book desks and rooms ahead of time to make sure they can access what they need at the office. That’s the same courtesy as a restaurant taking table reservations.

With OfficeRnD Workplace, hybrid workers can book desks, rooms, and amenities from tools built around how they work. It also includes a set of smart space solutions to help you manage your space.

Recognize employees’ hard work

Companies with formal employee recognition programs have almost a third less voluntary turnover than those without them.

To offer that recognition, send out newsletters or make announcements during meetings, whether in person or virtual.

You can also just tell someone they did a good job in a Slack message. Small acknowledgments add up.

Add the office amenities employees actually want

If you want to be hospitable to your team, think beyond workstations and office badge technology.

A well-lit office, or one that uses aspects of Feng Shui, can change the whole atmosphere. One report found that offices with natural greenery increased productivity by 15%.

That same research found the most in-demand elements among office workers were natural light, indoor plants, quiet working spaces, a view of the sea, and bright colors.

Use office wayfinding best practices, too, so people can navigate the space without friction.

Schedule regular one-on-one meetings

Because trust between managers and employees matters so much, it helps to have a set process for building those working relationships. Regular, scheduled one-on-ones, virtual or in person, do exactly that.

Research shows that 36% of employees prefer weekly conversations with their manager, with fewer wanting less frequent check-ins.

One-on-ones let employees set SMART goals (specific, measurable, achievable, relevant, and time-bound) with their managers and revisit them later. They can also just be a comfortable space to raise concerns.

Introduce policies and programs that support well-being

Most workers now expect mental health support at work. In the 2025 NAMI/Ipsos Workplace Mental Health Poll, 91% of employees said mental health care benefits are important to a positive workplace culture. Providing this in some form goes a long way toward showing people they’re looked after.

Some organizations give employees access to online therapy or wellness subscriptions. Others offer “mental health days” to help people protect their physical and mental well-being.

Examples of workplace hospitality in the real world

Some of the best-known companies already put workplace hospitality into practice. Here are two: Google and Slack.

Google

Google offices include amenities designed to make employees comfortable, from nap spaces to climbing walls.

The company also builds “third spaces,” areas that aren’t home or a desk, where employees can spend time together. Google designers intentionally added areas like cafés to build community and encourage new ideas. These spaces give employees room to develop relationships with colleagues and unwind.

Google now asks most employees to work from the office three days a week, and it tracks attendance through badge data. Even within that structure, the offices themselves are built to make the in-office days worth showing up for, which is its own form of hospitality.

Slack

Slack builds one of the best-known workplace communication tools, so it’s fitting that its own work practices back that up.

Slack teams set “core hours,” a limited window when everyone agrees to be available for meetings and collaboration, and manage the rest of the day around their own schedules. The company trusts its people to organize their time and tasks.

Slack also runs “Focus Fridays,” meeting-free days each quarter when teams cancel internal meetings so employees can do deep work without interruption. In its pilot, 84% of Slack employees found Focus Fridays beneficial.

It’s a strong example of a flexible work culture, where employees control how and when they work as long as the work gets done.

Increase your hybrid workplace hospitality with OfficeRnD Workplace

Making a workplace hospitable can feel hard when you have a remote or hybrid policy, but the right software helps.

The right technology makes hybrid work smoother for your team, and a smoother experience is what workplace hospitality is about.

Door Access control is one of the most important aspects of running a safe and secure coworking and flex space. First and foremost, coworking spaces are shared workplaces by definition. Therefore, in theory, many can and will have access to the space. It’s the coworking space operator’s job to ensure secure access to only authorized community members.

One way to enforce the security of the space is via good old keys. Managing physical keys is hard though. Very hard. It’s not very secure either.

Of course, in 2024, there are much better ways to secure your coworking or flex space than keys. Arguably, one of the best ways is to rely on an industry-leading digital security platform, such as Kisi.

Modern Access Control System for Coworking Spaces with Kisi

Kisi is one of the leading and one of the first technology companies offering tailored access control and security solutions for the coworking industry! They have thousands of happy customers due to their ease of use and robust security features built specifically for shared workplaces!

Kisi’s sturdy hardware and user-friendly software work in perfect harmony to enhance the security of your spaces. Remotely manage your locations, streamline operations, and stay compliant while enjoying mobile unlocks.

Some of the benefits of a modern access control system are:

  • Full control and visibility over who accesses your buildings while granting members autonomy over their spaces.
  • In-and-out tracking and intrusion detection to monitor your spaces.
  • 2FA (two-factor authentication) to better protect against thefts and breaches. Kisi can be integrated with your contact sensors, alarms, and cameras.
  • Apply security standards to all your real estate buildings. Manage multiple buildings, floors, and elevators.

Integrated Coworking Management Solution

The best coworking and flex space management systems, such as OfficeRnD Flex are offering advanced integrations with the best access control systems, such as Kisi.

The main benefits of the integration are:

  • Automation – synchronize member’s access to various areas of your space based on memberships, contracts, passes, bookings, or other important information.
  • Enhanced Member Experience – allow members to use either your OfficeRnD Mobile App or the Kisi Mobile App to open every door they have access to.
  • Better Reporting – gain much better insights about your space occupancy based on true check-in information that flows between the two systems.

Some of the more common use cases are:

  • New members will be granted access automatically based on their membership level or other details, such as day passes or bookings.
  • Former members’ access will be revoked automatically.
  • If a member is with a company that’s on contract for a specific office, the integration will give access, for example, to the main doors and the specific office.
  • If a member or external user books a meeting room, the access of this member will be changed to allow for accessing this meeting space.
  • If a member is a drop-in and has a certain number of day passes, they will be able to access the space as long as they have valid day passes.

Furthermore, that works flawlessly with many doors, many floors, and many locations.

The system will automate all processes and save your community managers and other staff a lot of time and headaches!

Here’s what Bernie Mehl, founder and CEO at Kisi has to say about our integration:

OfficeRND has technology in the company name and as such part of their DNA. This fits very well to Kisi’s product forward organization and leads to high satisfaction among our shared customer base.

Use the OfficeRnD Mobile App to Unlock Space Doors

The best part of the OfficeRnD Flex and Kisi integration is providing Member Mobile Keys to your community! The integration will allow your members to easily open every door they are allowed to using the same Mobile app they use for booking or other collaboration features.

After the door access integration is connected and Member Mobile Access is enabled members will be prompted to authenticate their digital office key when they first log in to the mobile app. Once the user has authenticated their access credentials they can tap the key icon within the OfficeRnD Member app and put their phone near the door reader. The phone will sync with the reader and unlock the office or meeting room door as needed.

Hundreds of coworking space operators worldwide use the OfficeRnD <> Kisi integration! Here’s what Craig Baute, CEO and Founder of Creative Density Coworking and Denswap has to say about it:

Our focus of 2023 was to take as many tasks off the community manager as possible so they can focus on the community. Kisi has been a surprisingly key part of that because as day passes, meeting rooms, and new members started to join. We use to have to manually add members to our door system and remove members. Kisi does that automatically and she just doesn’t think about it anymore, saving around around 2 hours of work each month. It’s more accurate, secure, and takes an annoying tasks off their list.

One less thing to train

We started to really lean on the integrations of OfficeRnD so training new staff members is easier since I live 1,400 miles away. Moving to Kisi has been a big relief to our community manager, members, and the security of our space because it handles day pass codes, meeting room access, everything. It’s allowed us to encourage more day usage because of that, which is driving new revenue all without the staff do more work but be a friendly person.

Suprising win. Kisi Integration is Driving Member Useage and Interaction

A killer feature we didn’t expect from moving to Kisi is app usage. Kisi integration has made everyone’s life easier, but because the digital key is in the coworking app, members have started to use the app. They now see upcoming events, how-to articles, meeting rooms bookings. It’s the sticky feature that made the app useful, which has taken a lot of the load off our staff and increased member engagements. There are lots of surprising wins besides the obvious.
